For just as the four kinds of nutriment for beings enter through the mouth and pervade the major and minor limbs, so too for a yogi, the wholesome qualities of the four planes enter through the mouth of virtue and bring about the fulfillment of the goal. Therefore, it is called 'mokkha'. 'Pamokkha' means 'good in the forefront' (pamukhe sādhu); the meaning is leading, best, principal. It should be understood as foremost, leading, best, and principal for the attainment of wholesome qualities, that is, for the purpose of acquiring the wholesome states of the four planes.

Kāyiko avītikkamoti tividhaṃ kāyasucaritaṃ. Vācasikoti catubbidhaṃ vacīsucaritaṃ. Kāyikavācasikoti tadubhayaṃ. Iminā ājīvaṭṭhamakasīlaṃ pariyādāya dasseti. Saṃvutoti pihito, saṃvutindriyo pihitindriyoti attho. Yathā hi saṃvutadvāraṃ gehaṃ “saṃvutagehaṃ pihitageha”nti vuccati, evamidha saṃvutindriyo “saṃvuto”ti vutto. Pātimokkhasaṃvarenāti pātimokkhasaṅkhātena saṃvarena. Upetotiādīni sabbāni aññamaññavevacanāni.

'Bodily non-transgression' is the threefold good bodily conduct. 'Verbal' is the fourfold good verbal conduct. 'Bodily and verbal' is both of those. By this, it is shown to include the virtue that has right livelihood as its eighth factor. 'Restrained' means closed; the meaning is 'one with restrained faculties, one with closed faculties.' Just as a house with closed doors is called 'a closed house, a shut house,' so here one with restrained faculties is said to be 'restrained.' 'By the restraint of the Pātimokkha' means by the restraint designated as the Pātimokkha. 'Endowed with' and so on are all synonyms for one another.

Iriyatītiādīhi [M 3.0037] sattahipi padehi pātimokkhasaṃvarasīle ṭhitassa bhikkhuno iriyāpathavihāro kathito. Tattha iriyatīti catunnaṃ iriyāpathānaṃ aññatarasamaṅgibhāvato iriyati. Tehi iriyāpathacatukkehi kāyasakaṭavattanena vattati. Ekaṃ iriyāpathadukkhaṃ aparena iriyāpathena vicchinditvā ciraṭṭhitibhāvena sarīrarakkhaṇato pāleti. Ekasmiṃ iriyāpathe asaṇṭhahitvā sabbairiyāpathe vattanato yapeti. Tena tena iriyāpathena tathā tathā kāyassa yāpanato yāpeti. Cirakālavattāpanato carati. Iriyāpathena iriyāpathaṃ vicchinditvā jīvitaharaṇato viharati.

By the seven terms beginning with 'He moves' (iriyati), the dwelling in the postures of a bhikkhu established in the virtue of the Pātimokkha restraint is described. Therein, 'he moves' (iriyati) means he is endowed with one of the four postures. With these four postures, he proceeds by turning the cart of the body. 'He protects' (pāleti) means he protects the body by maintaining it for a long time, having alleviated the discomfort of one posture with another. 'He keeps going' (yapeti) means he keeps going by not remaining fixed in one posture but by proceeding through all postures. 'He maintains' (yāpeti) means he maintains the body in various ways with each respective posture. 'He fares' (carati) means he proceeds for a long time. 'He dwells' (viharati) means he carries on his life by interrupting one posture with another.

Micchājīvapaṭisedhakenāti –

By means of the rejection of wrong livelihood:

“Idhekacco veḷudānena vā pattadānena vā puppha phala sinānadantakaṭṭhadānena vā cāṭukamyatāya [V 3.0034] vā muggasūpyatāya vā pāribhaṭayatāya vā jaṅghapesanikena vā aññataraññatarena vā buddhapaṭikuṭṭhena micchāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti, ayaṃ vuccati anācāro”ti (vibha. 513) –

'Here, a certain person makes a living by wrong livelihood despised by the Buddha, by some means or other, such as by giving bamboo, giving leaves, giving flowers, fruits, bathing powder, or tooth-sticks; or by flattery, by hinting, by acting as a children's attendant, or by being a messenger. This is called misconduct.' (Vibh. 513)

Evaṃ vuttaanācārasaṅkhātamicchājīvapaṭipakkhena.

By means of the opposite of that wrong livelihood designated as misconduct, as spoken of thus.

Na veḷudānādinā ācārenāti –

By conduct that does not involve giving bamboo and so on:

“Idhekacco na veḷudānena na patta na puppha na phala na sināna na dantakaṭṭha na cāṭukamyatāya na muggasūpyatāya na pāribhaṭayatāya na jaṅghapesanikena na aññataraññatarena buddhapaṭikuṭṭhena micchāājīvena jīvikaṃ kappeti, ayaṃ vuccati ācāro”ti (vibha. 513) –

'Here, a certain person does not make a living by wrong livelihood despised by the Buddha, by any means or other, such as by giving bamboo, giving leaves, giving flowers, fruits, bathing powder, or tooth-sticks; nor by flattery, by hinting, by acting as a children's attendant, or by being a messenger. This is called proper conduct.' (Vibh. 513)

Evaṃ vuttena na veḷudānādinā ācārena.

By means of such stated conduct, which does not involve giving bamboo and so on.

Vesiyādiagocaraṃ pahāyāti –

By 'having abandoned unsuitable resorts such as prostitutes':

“Idhekacco vesiyagocaro vā hoti vidhava thullakumāri paṇḍaka bhikkhuni pānāgāragocaro vā, saṃsaṭṭho viharati rājūhi rājamahāmattehi titthiyehi titthiyasāvakehi ananulomikena saṃsaggena, yāni pana tāni kulāni assaddhāni [M 3.0038] appasannāni anopānabhūtāni akkosakaparibhāsakāni anatthakāmāni ahitakāmāni aphāsukakāmāni ayogakkhemakāmāni bhikkhūnaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ upāsakānaṃ upāsikānaṃ, tathārūpāni kulāni sevati bhajati payirupāsati, ayaṃ vuccati agocaro”ti (vibha. 514) –

'Here, a certain person resorts to prostitutes, widows, spinsters, pandakas, bhikkhunīs, or taverns. He dwells in association with kings, royal ministers, sectarians, or their disciples in an unsuitable manner. Furthermore, he serves, frequents, and attends upon families that are faithless, lacking in confidence, not a source of support, who are abusive and reviling, who wish for what is harmful, unbeneficial, and uncomfortable, and who wish for a lack of security from bondage for the bhikkhus, bhikkhunīs, male lay followers, and female lay followers. This is called an unsuitable resort.' (Vibh. 514)

Evamāgataṃ vesiyādiagocaraṃ pahāya.

Having abandoned the unsuitable resort beginning with prostitutes, as it has been described.

Saddhāsampannakulādināti ettha ādi-saddena upanissayagocarādiṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Tividho hi gocaro upanissayagocaro ārakkhagocaro upanibandhagocaroti. Katamo upanissayagocaro? Dasakathāvatthuguṇasamannāgato kalyāṇamitto, yaṃ nissāya asutaṃ suṇāti, sutaṃ pariyodapeti, kaṅkhaṃ [V 3.0035] vitarati, diṭṭhiṃ ujuṃ karoti, cittaṃ pasādeti. Yassa vā pana anusikkhamāno saddhāya vaḍḍhati, sīlena sutena cāgena paññāya vaḍḍhati, ayaṃ upanissayagocaro. Katamo ārakkhagocaro? Idha bhikkhu antaragharaṃ paviṭṭho vīthiṃ paṭipanno okkhittacakkhu yugamattadassāvī saṃvuto gacchati, na hatthiṃ olokento, na assaṃ, na rathaṃ, na pattiṃ, na itthiṃ, na purisaṃ olokento, na uddhaṃ olokento, na adho olokento, na disāvidisaṃ vipekkhamāno gacchati, ayaṃ ārakkhagocaro. Katamo upanibandhagocaro? Cattāro satipaṭṭhānā, yattha cittaṃ upanibandhati. Vuttañhetaṃ bhagavatā “ko ca, bhikkhave, bhikkhuno gocaro sako pettiko visayo? Yadidaṃ cattāro satipaṭṭhānā”ti (saṃ. ni. 5.372), ayaṃ upanibandhagocaro. Iti ayaṃ tividho gocaro idha ādi-saddena saṅgahitoti daṭṭhabbo.

“Of families endowed with faith, etc.”: Here, the term “etc.” includes the sphere of reliance and so on. For the sphere is threefold: the sphere of reliance, the sphere of protection, and the sphere of binding. What is the sphere of reliance? A virtuous friend endowed with the ten qualities of a worthwhile conversation, relying on whom one hears what has not been heard, clarifies what has been heard, dispels doubt, straightens one’s views, and gladdens the mind. Or one who, by emulating, grows in faith, virtue, learning, generosity, and wisdom—this is the sphere of reliance. What is the sphere of protection? Here, a monk who has entered a village or is walking along a road keeps his eyes lowered, looking only a yoke’s length ahead, restrained as he walks. He does not look at an elephant, a horse, a chariot, a foot soldier, a woman, or a man. He does not look up, down, or around in all directions as he walks—this is the sphere of protection. What is the sphere of binding? The four foundations of mindfulness, where the mind is bound. For this has been said by the Blessed One: “And what, monks, is a monk’s own ancestral domain, his own proper sphere? It is just these four foundations of mindfulness.” This is the sphere of binding. Thus, this threefold sphere should be understood here as included by the term “etc.”

Appamattakesu vajjesūti asañcicca āpannasekhiyaakusalacittuppādādibhedesu vajjesu. Bhayato dassanasīloti paramāṇumattaṃ vajjaṃ aṭṭhasaṭṭhiyojanasatasahassubbedhasinerupabbatasadisaṃ katvā dassanasabhāvo, sabbalahukaṃ vā dubbhāsitamattaṃ pārājikasadisaṃ katvā dassanasabhāvo. Sammā ādāyāti sammadeva sakkaccaṃ sabbaso vā ādiyitvā.

“In minor offenses” refers to offenses such as unintentional breaches of training rules or the arising of unwholesome states of mind. “Being in the habit of seeing danger” means regarding even an atom-sized fault as a mountain like Mount Meru, which is one hundred sixty-eight thousand yojanas high, or regarding even the slightest harsh speech as being like a pārājika offense. “Rightly undertaking” means properly and attentively undertaking it in every way.

Vaṭṭadukkhanissaraṇatthikehi [M 3.0039] sotabbato sutaṃ, pariyattidhammo. Taṃ dhāretīti sutadharo, sutassa ādhārabhūto. Yassa hi ito gahitaṃ etto palāyati, chiddaghaṭe udakaṃ viya na tiṭṭhati, parisamajjhe ekaṃ suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā kathetuṃ vā vācetuṃ vā na sakkoti, ayaṃ na sutadharo nāma. Yassa pana uggahitaṃ buddhavacanaṃ uggahitakālasadisameva hoti, dasapi vīsatipi vassāni sajjhāyaṃ akarontassa na nassati, ayaṃ sutadharo nāma. Tenevāha “yadassa ta”ntiādi. Ekapadampi ekakkharampi avinaṭṭhaṃ hutvā sanniciyatīti sannicayo, sutaṃ sannicayo etasminti sutasannicayoti āha “sutaṃ sannicitaṃ asminti sutasannicayo”ti. Yassa hi sutaṃ hadayamañjusāyaṃ sannicitaṃ silāya lekhā viya suvaṇṇaghaṭe pakkhittā sīhavasā viya ca sādhu tiṭṭhati, ayaṃ sutasannicayo nāma. Tenāha “etena…pe… avināsaṃ dassetī”ti.

What is heard (suta) is the Dhamma of study, to be listened to by those seeking escape from the suffering of the cycle of existence. One who retains it is called a ‘retainer of what is heard’ (sutadhara), being a repository for what has been heard. For if what is grasped from here escapes from there, like water in a cracked pot, it does not remain. Such a one cannot speak a single discourse or Jātaka in an assembly, nor recite it – this is not called a ‘retainer of what is heard.’ But for one in whom the Buddha’s word, once learned, remains just as it was when first grasped – even if they do not recite for ten or twenty years, it does not perish – this is called a ‘retainer of what is heard.’ Therefore, he said: “That which is his…” Even a single word or syllable, uncorrupted, accumulates; this is accumulation (sannicayo). What has been heard is accumulated in this person, thus he is called ‘one who has accumulated what has been heard’ (sutasannicayo). As it is said: ‘What has been heard is accumulated in him, thus he is called “one who has accumulated what has been heard.”’ For in whom what has been heard is accumulated in the casket of the heart, like an inscription on stone, or like lion’s fat placed in a golden vessel – it remains well. This is called ‘one who has accumulated what has been heard.’ Therefore, he said: “By this… he shows its imperishability.”

Dhātāti paguṇā vācuggatā. Ekassa hi uggahitabuddhavacanaṃ niccakālikaṃ na hoti, “asukasuttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā kathehī”ti vutte “sajjhāyitvā aññehi saṃsanditvā paripucchāvasena atthaṃ ogāhitvā jānissāmī”ti vadati. Ekassa paguṇaṃ pabandhavicchedābhāvato gaṅgāsotasadisaṃ bhavaṅgasotasadisañca akittimaṃ sukhappavatti hoti, “asukasuttaṃ [V 3.0036] vā jātakaṃ vā kathehī”ti vutte uddharitvā tameva katheti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “dhātā”ti. Vācāya paguṇā katāti suttadasakavaggadasakapaṇṇāsadasakavasena vācāya sajjhāyitā, dasa suttāni gatāni, dasa vaggāni gatānītiādinā sallakkhetvā vācāya sajjhāyitāti attho. Suttekadesassa hi suttamattassa ca vacasā paricayo idha nādhippeto, atha kho vaggādivaseneva. Manasā anupekkhitāti manasā anu anu pekkhitā, bhāgaso nijjhāyitā cintitāti attho. Āvajjantassāti vācāya sajjhāyituṃ buddhavacanaṃ manasā cintentassa. Suṭṭhu paṭividdhāti nijjaṭaṃ niggumbaṃ katvā suṭṭhu yāthāvato paṭividdhā.

‘Retained’ (dhātā) means proficient, verbalized. For one person, the Buddha’s word that has been learned is not always available; when asked, “Recite such-and-such a sutta or jātaka,” he says, “After reviewing it, consulting with others, and grasping the meaning by way of inquiry, I will know.” For another who is proficient, it flows naturally and easily, without interruption in its continuity, like the current of the Ganges or the stream of the life-continuum; when asked, “Recite such-and-such a sutta or jātaka,” he draws it forth and recites it immediately. It is with reference to this that ‘retained’ was said. ‘Made proficient by speech’ means recited by speech by way of tens of suttas, tens of chapters, and tens of fifties, noting things such as, “ten suttas have been mastered, ten chapters have been mastered.” For mere familiarity with a part of a sutta or just a single sutta is not intended here, but rather proficiency by way of chapters and so on. ‘Attended to with the mind’ means repeatedly examined with the mind, reflected upon and contemplated part by part. ‘For one who is adverting’ means for one who is contemplating the Buddha’s word with the mind in order to recite it with speech. ‘Thoroughly penetrated’ means it is penetrated well and as it truly is, having made it untangled and free of thickets.

Dve mātikāti bhikkhumātikā bhikkhunīmātikā ca. Vācuggatāti purimasseva vevacanaṃ. Tisso anumodanāti saṅghabhatte dānānisaṃsapaṭisaṃyuttaanumodanā, vihārādimaṅgale maṅgalasuttādianumodanā, matakabhattādiavamaṅgale tirokuṭṭādianumodanāti imā tisso anumodanā[M 3.0040]. Kammākammavinicchayoti parivārāvasāne kammavagge vuttavinicchayo. “Vipassanāvasena uggaṇhantena catudhātuvavatthānamukhena uggahetabba”nti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Catūsu disāsu appaṭihatattā catasso disā etassāti catuddiso, catuddisoyeva cātuddiso, catasso vā disā arahati, catūsu vā disāsu sādhūti cātuddiso.

‘The two matrices’ are the Bhikkhu-mātikā and the Bhikkhunī-mātikā. ‘Verbalized’ is a synonym for the previous term. ‘The three kinds of anumodanā’ are: at a meal for the Sangha, the anumodanā connected with the benefits of giving; at an auspicious ceremony for a monastery and so on, the anumodanā of the Maṅgala Sutta and others; at an inauspicious ceremony such as a meal for the deceased, the anumodanā of the Tirokuṭṭa Sutta and others—these are the three kinds of anumodanā. ‘The determination of valid and invalid acts’ refers to the determination taught in the Kammavagga at the end of the Parivāra. “It should be learned by one who is learning by way of insight, through the means of the analysis of the four elements”—this is stated in all three sub-commentaries. Because he is unobstructed in the four directions, he has four directions (catasso disā etassa), thus he is ‘catuddiso.’ Catuddiso is the same as cātuddiso. Or, he is worthy of (arahati) the four directions, or he is excellent (sādhu) in the four directions, thus he is ‘cātuddiso.’

Abhivinayeti sakale vinayapiṭake. Vinetunti sikkhāpetuṃ. “Dve vibhaṅgā paguṇā vācuggatā kātabbāti idaṃ paripucchāvasena uggahaṇampi sandhāya vutta”nti vadanti. Ekassa pamuṭṭhaṃ, itarassa paguṇaṃ hotīti āha “tīhi janehi saddhiṃ parivattanakkhamā kātabbā”ti. Abhidhammeti nāmarūpaparicchede. Heṭṭhimā vā tayo vaggāti mahāvaggato heṭṭhā sagāthakavaggo nidānavaggo khandhakavaggoti ime tayo vaggā. “Dhammapadampi saha vatthunā uggahetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti mahāpaccariyaṃ vuttattā jātakabhāṇakena sāṭṭhakathaṃ jātakaṃ uggahetvāpi dhammapadampi saha vatthunā uggahetabbameva.

‘In the higher Vinaya’ means in the entire Vinaya Piṭaka. ‘To train’ means to instruct. They say: “‘The two Vibhaṅgas should be made proficient and verbalized’; this is said with reference to learning even by way of questioning.” When for one it is forgotten and for another it is proficient, he said: “It should be made suitable for reviewing with three people.” ‘In the higher Dhamma’ means in the discrimination of name-and-form. ‘The lower three chapters’ means these three chapters below the Mahāvagga: the Sagāthakavagga, the Nidānavagga, and the Khandhakavagga. Because it is said in the Mahāpaccariya commentary, “It is proper to learn the Dhammapada together with its stories,” a reciter of the Jātakas, even after having learned the Jātaka with its commentary, should indeed also learn the Dhammapada together with its stories.

Kalyāṇā sundarā parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanā vācā assāti kalyāṇavāco. Tenāha “sithiladhanitādīnaṃ…pe… vācāya samannāgato”ti. Tattha parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanāyāti ṭhānakaraṇasampattiyā sikkhāsampattiyā ca katthacipi anūnatāya parimaṇḍalapadāni byañjanāni akkharāni etissāti parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanā, padameva vā atthassa byañjanato padabyañjanaṃ, taṃ akkharapāripūriṃ katvā sithiladhanitādidasavidhaṃ byañjanabuddhiṃ aparihāpetvā vuttaṃ parimaṇḍalaṃ nāma hoti. Akkharapāripūriyā hi padabyañjanassa parimaṇḍalatā. Tena vuttaṃ “sithiladhanitādīnaṃ [V 3.0037] yathāvidhānavacanenā”ti, parimaṇḍalaṃ padabyañjanaṃ etissāti parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanā. Atha vā pajjati ñāyati attho etenāti padaṃ, nāmādi. Yathādhippetamatthaṃ byañjetīti byañjanaṃ, vākyaṃ. Tesaṃ paripuṇṇatāya parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanā.

He has speech that is beautiful, lovely, and with well-rounded words and expressions, thus he is one with beautiful speech (kalyāṇavāco). Therefore, he said: “endowed with speech… of soft and firm sounds, etc.” Therein, ‘with well-rounded words and expressions’ means that because of perfection in the places and organs of articulation and perfection in phonetic training, and being nowhere deficient, its words, expressions, and letters are well-rounded. Or, the word (pada) itself is the expression (byañjana) of the meaning, thus ‘word-expression’ (padabyañjana); when this is spoken with full syllables and without losing the tenfold development of pronunciation, such as soft and firm, it is called ‘well-rounded’ (parimaṇḍala). For it is through the fullness of the syllables that the word-expression has roundedness. Therefore it was said: “by speaking according to the rule with soft, firm, etc., sounds.” This speech possesses a well-rounded word-expression, thus it is ‘parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanā.’ Alternatively, meaning is understood or known (pajjati ñāyati) by this (etena), thus it is a ‘word’ (pada), such as a name, etc. It expresses (byañjeti) the intended meaning, thus it is an ‘expression’ (byañjana), i.e., a sentence. Due to their completeness, the words and expressions are well-rounded.

Apica yo bhikkhu parisati dhammaṃ desento suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā nikkhipitvā aññaṃ upārambhakaraṃ suttaṃ āharati, tassa upamaṃ katheti, tadatthaṃ otāreti, evaṃ idaṃ gahetvā ettha khipanto ekapasseneva pariharanto kālaṃ ñatvā vuṭṭhahati, nikkhittasuttaṃ pana nikkhittamattameva hoti, tassa kathā aparimaṇḍalā nāma hoti atthassa aparipuṇṇabhāvato. Yo pana suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā nikkhipitvā bahi ekapadampi agantvā [M 3.0041] yathānikkhittassa suttassa atthasaṃvaṇṇanāvaseneva suttantarampi ānento pāḷiyā anusandhiñca pubbāparañca apekkhanto ācariyehi dinnanaye ṭhatvā tulikāya paricchindanto viya taṃ taṃ atthaṃ suvavatthitaṃ katvā dassento gambhīramātikāya udakaṃ pesento viya gambhīramatthaṃ gamento vaggihārigatiyā pade padaṃ koṭṭento sindhavājānīyo viya ekaṃyeva padaṃ anekehi pariyāyehi punappunaṃ saṃvaṇṇanto gacchati, tassa kathā parimaṇḍalā nāma hoti dhammato atthato anusandhito pubbāparato ācariyuggahatoti sabbaso paripuṇṇabhāvato. Evarūpampi kathaṃ sandhāya “parimaṇḍalapadabyañjanāyā”ti vuttaṃ.

Furthermore, a monk who, while teaching the Dhamma in an assembly, sets aside a sutta or a jātaka and brings up another sutta that causes reproach, speaks a simile about it, and brings it down for that purpose; thus, taking this and inserting it here, carrying it along on one side only, he knows the time and rises. The sutta that was set aside, however, remains merely set aside. His talk is called 'unrounded' because of the incompleteness of its meaning. But as for the one who, having set aside a sutta or a jātaka, does not go outside by even a single word, but by way of explaining the meaning of the very sutta that was set aside, even brings in other suttas, considering the connection in the Pāli and what comes before and after, standing in the method given by the teachers, delimiting like one with a brush, making each and every meaning well-established and showing it, like one sending water through a deep channel, causing it to reach a deep meaning, proceeding like a thoroughbred Sindhi horse striking step upon step with a measured gait, explaining one and the same word again and again in many ways—his talk is called 'rounded' because it is completely perfect in every way: in Dhamma, in meaning, in connection, in what comes before and after, and in what has been learned from the teachers. It is with reference to such a talk that it is said, 'with rounded words and syllables.'

Guṇaparipuṇṇabhāvena pure bhavāti porī, tassa bhikkhuno tenetaṃ bhāsitabbaṃ atthassa guṇaparipuṇṇabhāvena pure puṇṇabhāve bhavāti attho. Pure vā bhavattā poriyā nāgarikitthiyā sukhumālattanena sadisāti porī, pure saṃvaḍḍhanārī viya sukumārāti attho. Purassa esātipi porī, purassa esāti nagaravāsīnaṃ kathāti attho. Nagaravāsino hi yuttakathā honti pitimattaṃ “pitā”ti, bhātimattaṃ “bhātā”ti vadanti. Evarūpī hi kathā bahuno janassa kantā hoti manāpā, tāya poriyā.

She is 'porī' because she is in a state of fullness (`pure`) due to the completeness of her virtues. For that monk, this should be said: the meaning is that she is in a state of fullness due to the completeness of her virtues. Or, she is 'porī' because of being in the city (`pure`). She is 'porī' because she is like a city woman in her delicacy; the meaning is, she is delicate like a woman raised in the city. Also, 'porī' comes from 'purassa esā' (this is of the city); the meaning is, this is the speech of city-dwellers. For city-dwellers indeed have appropriate speech: they call one who is of the measure of a father 'father,' and one who is of the measure of a brother 'brother.' Indeed, such speech is pleasing and agreeable to many people. By that 'porī' speech.

Vissaṭṭhāyāti pittasemhādīhi apalibuddhāya sandiṭṭhavilambitādidosarahitāya. Atha vā nātisīghaṃ nātisaṇikaṃ nirantaraṃ ekarasañca katvā parisāya ajjhāsayānurūpaṃ dhammaṃ kathentassa vācā vissaṭṭhā nāma. Yo hi bhikkhu dhammaṃ kathento suttaṃ vā jātakaṃ vā ārabhitvā āraddhakālato paṭṭhāya turitaturito araṇiṃ manthento viya uṇhakhādanīyaṃ khādanto viya pāḷiyā anusandhipubbāparesu gahitaṃ gahitameva, aggahitaṃ aggahitameva katvā purāṇapaṇṇantaresu caramānaṃ godhaṃ uṭṭhāpento viya tattha tattha paharanto osāpetvā uṭṭhāya gacchati[V 3.0038]. Purāṇapaṇṇantaresu hi paripātiyamānā godhā kadāci dissati kadāci na dissati, evamekaccassa atthavaṇṇanā katthaci dissati katthaci na dissati. Yopi dhammaṃ kathento kālena sīghaṃ, kālena saṇikaṃ, kālena mandaṃ, kālena mahāsaddaṃ, kālena khuddakasaddaṃ karoti, yathā nijjhāmataṇhikapetassa [M 3.0042] mukhato niccharaṇakaaggi kālena jalati kālena nibbāyati, evaṃ petadhammakathiko nāma hoti, parisāya uṭṭhātukāmāya puna ārabhati. Yopi kathento tattha tattha vitthāyati, appaṭibhānatāya āpajjati, kenaci rogena nitthunanto viya kandanto viya katheti, imesaṃ sabbesampi kathā vissaṭṭhā nāma na hoti sukhena appavattabhāvato. Yo pana suttaṃ āharitvā ācariyehi dinnanaye ṭhito ācariyuggahaṃ amuñcanto yathā ca ācariyā taṃ taṃ suttaṃ saṃvaṇṇesuṃ, teneva nayena saṃvaṇṇento nātisīghaṃ nātisaṇikantiādinā vuttanayena kathāpabandhaṃ avicchinnaṃ katvā nadīsoto viya pavatteti, ākāsagaṅgāto bhassamānaudakaṃ viya nirantarakathaṃ pavatteti, tassa kathā vissaṭṭhā nāma hoti. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “vissaṭṭhāyā”ti.

'Clear' means unobstructed by bile, phlegm, and the like, and free from faults such as being indistinct or delayed. Alternatively, the speech of one who teaches the Dhamma to an assembly in a manner suited to their disposition—neither too fast nor too slow, uninterrupted, and of a single character—is called 'clear'. For a certain monk, when teaching the Dhamma, begins a sutta or a jātaka and from the very start rushes hurriedly, like one rubbing a fire-stick or eating hot food; in the Pāli, its connections, and its sequence, he treats what is grasped as grasped and what is not grasped as not grasped, and proceeds by striking here and there, like one flushing out a monitor lizard moving among old leaves; then, having concluded, he rises and departs. Just as a monitor lizard moving among old leaves is sometimes seen and sometimes not, so too, for a certain person, the explanation of the meaning is sometimes apparent and sometimes not. And another, when teaching the Dhamma, is at times fast, at times slow, at times soft, at times loud, at times with a small sound; just as the fire issuing from the mouth of a hungry ghost afflicted by burning thirst at times blazes and at times is extinguished, so too is this one; he is called a 'ghostly Dhamma teacher'. When the assembly wishes to rise, he begins again. And another, while speaking, gets stuck here and there, and falters due to a lack of ready wit; he speaks as if groaning or weeping from some ailment. The speech of all of these is not called 'clear', because it does not proceed with ease. But as for the one who, having brought up a sutta, stands in the method given by the teachers, not abandoning what has been learned from the teachers, and explains that sutta in the very same way the teachers explained it, making the thread of discourse unbroken in the manner described as 'neither too fast nor too slow', causing it to proceed like a river's current, causing the uninterrupted speech to proceed like water falling from the celestial Ganges—his speech is called 'clear'. It is with reference to this that it is said, 'clear'.

Anelagaḷāyāti elagaḷavirahitāya. Kassaci hi kathentassa elaṃ gaḷati, lālā paggharati, kheḷaphusitāni vā nikkhamanti, tassa vācā elagaḷā nāma hoti, tabbiparītāyāti attho. Atthassa viññāpaniyāti ādimajjhapariyosānaṃ pākaṭaṃ katvā bhāsitatthassa viññāpanasamatthatāya atthañāpane sādhanāya.

'Not slobbering' means free from slobbering. For when a certain person speaks, saliva drips, drool flows, or flecks of spittle issue forth; his speech is called 'slobbering'. The meaning is the opposite of that. 'Making the meaning known' means that, by making the beginning, middle, and end apparent, it is capable of making known the spoken meaning, and is an instrument for knowing the meaning.

Vācāva karaṇanti vākkaraṇaṃ, udāhāraghoso. Kalyāṇaṃ madhuraṃ vākkaraṇaṃ assāti kalyāṇavākkaraṇo. Tenevāha “madhurassaro”ti. Hīḷetīti avajānāti. Mātugāmoti sambandho. Manaṃ apāyati vaḍḍhetīti manāpo. Tenāha “manavaḍḍhanako”ti. Vaṭṭabhayena tajjetvāti yobbanamadādimattā bhikkhuniyo saṃsārabhayena tāsetvā. Gihikāleti attano gihikāle. Bhikkhuniyā methunena bhikkhunīdūsako hotīti bhikkhuniyā kāyasaṃsaggameva vadati. Sikkhamānāsāmaṇerīsu pana methunenapi bhikkhunīdūsako na hotīti āha “sikkhamānāsāmaṇerīsu methunadhamma”nti. “Kāsāyavatthavasanāyā”ti vacanato dussīlāsu bhikkhunīsikkhamānāsāmaṇerīsu garudhammaṃ ajjhāpannapubbo paṭikkhittoyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tassā bhikkhuniyā abhāvepi yā yā tassā vacanaṃ assosuṃ, tā tā tatheva maññantīti āha “mātugāmo hī”tiādi.

'Speech itself is the instrument' (`vācā eva karaṇaṃ`), hence `vākkaraṇaṃ`, the sound of utterance. 'He has speech (`vākkaraṇaṃ`) that is lovely and sweet', hence `kalyāṇavākkaraṇo`. Therefore, it is said, 'one with a sweet voice'. 'Despises' (`hīḷeti`) means disparages. The connection is with 'woman' (`mātugāmo`). 'It increases the mind' (`manaṃ vaḍḍheti`), hence `manāpo` (agreeable). Therefore, it is said, 'one who increases delight'. 'Having threatened with the fear of the round of existence' means having scared nuns who are intoxicated with youthfulness and so on with the fear of saṃsāra. 'In his household life' means in his own time as a householder. One becomes a 'defiler of nuns' through sexual intercourse with a nun; this refers to bodily contact with a nun. But with female probationers and novice nuns, one is not a 'defiler of nuns' even through sexual intercourse; therefore, it is said, 'sexual intercourse with female probationers and novice nuns'. From the phrase 'because of wearing the ochre robe', it should be understood that one who has previously transgressed a grave rule with immoral nuns, female probationers, or novice nuns is rejected. Even in the absence of that nun, whichever nuns heard her word, they think of him in that same way. Therefore, it is said, 'a woman despises,' and so on.

Idāni [M 3.0043] aṭṭha aṅgāni samodhānetvā dassetuṃ “ettha cā”tiādi āraddhaṃ. Imehi pana aṭṭhahaṅgehi [V 3.0039] asamannāgataṃ ñatticatutthena kammena sammannento dukkaṭaṃ āpajjati, bhikkhu pana sammatoyeva hoti.

Now, to show the eight factors in combination, the passage beginning 'And here...' is introduced. However, one who appoints a person not endowed with these eight factors by means of an act consisting of a motion and three announcements incurs an offense of wrong-doing; the monk, however, is indeed validly appointed.

148. Garukehīti garukātabbehi. Ekatoupasampannāyāti upayogatthe bhummavacanaṃ. “Ovadatī”ti vā imassa “vadatī”ti atthe sati sampadānavacanampi yujjati. Bhikkhūnaṃ santike upasampannā nāma parivattaliṅgā vā pañcasatasākiyāniyo vā.

148. 'By the respected' (`garukehi`) means by those who should be respected. The phrase 'by one ordained on one side' (`ekatoupasampannāya`) is a locative in the sense of relation. Or, when `ovadati` (admonishes) has the meaning of `vadati` (speaks to), the dative case is also suitable. 'Ordained in the presence of the monks' refers to those who have undergone a change of gender or the five hundred Sakyan ladies.

149. Āsanaṃ paññapetvāti ettha “sace bhūmi manāpā hoti, āsanaṃ apaññāpetumpi vaṭṭatī”ti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Mātugāmaggahaṇena bhikkhunīpi saṅgahitāti āha “dhammadesanāpattimocanattha”nti. Sammatassa bhikkhuno santikaṃ pāṭipade ovādatthāya sabbāhi bhikkhunīhi āgantabbato “samaggāttha bhaginiyo”ti iminā sabbāsaṃ āgamanaṃ pucchatīti āha “sabbā āgatātthā”ti. Gilānāsu anāgatāsupi gilānānaṃ anāgamanassa anuññātattā āgantuṃ samatthāhi ca sabbāhi āgatattā “samaggāmhayyā”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭati. Antogāme vātiādīsu yattha pañca aṅgāni bhūmiyaṃ patiṭṭhāpetvā vandituṃ na sakkā hoti, tattha ṭhitāya eva kāyaṃ purato nāmetvā “vandāmi ayyā”ti añjaliṃ paggayha gantumpi vaṭṭati. Antaragharanti katthaci nagaradvārassa bahiindakhīlato paṭṭhāya antogāmo vuccati, katthaci gharummārato paṭṭhāya antogehaṃ. Idha pana “antogāme vā”ti visuṃ vuttattā “antaraghare vā”ti antogehaṃ sandhāya vuttanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Yattha katthacīti antogāmādīsu yattha katthaci.

149. Regarding 'Having prepared a seat': here, it is said in all three commentaries that 'if the ground is pleasant, it is permissible not to prepare a seat.' By the inclusion of 'woman,' nuns are also included; hence it is said, 'for the purpose of teaching the Dhamma and releasing from offenses.' Since all nuns should come to the presence of an appointed monk on the first day of the fortnight for the purpose of receiving advice, the phrase 'are the sisters assembled?' inquires whether all have arrived; hence it is said, 'have you all come?' Even if some are sick and have not come, since the absence of the sick is permitted, and all who are able to come have come, it is appropriate to say, 'we are assembled, venerable sir.' In the case of 'within the village,' etc., where it is not possible to pay respects by placing the five limbs on the ground, there it is permissible to stand, bend the body forward, raise joined palms, say, 'I pay respects, venerable sirs,' and then go. Regarding 'Inside the house': in some cases, the area starting from the outer gate-post of the city is called 'within the village,' while in others, the area starting from the threshold of a house is called 'inside the house.' Here, however, since 'within the village' is mentioned separately, 'inside the house' should be understood as referring to the interior of a house. 'Wherever' means wherever it may be in places such as within the village, etc.

Vaṭṭatīti “vasatha ayye, mayaṃ bhikkhū ānessāmā”ti vuttavacanaṃ saddahantīhi vasituṃ vaṭṭati. Na nimantitā hutvā gantukāmāti manussehi nimantitā hutvā gantukāmā na hontīti attho, tattheva vassaṃ upagantukāmā hontīti adhippāyo. Yatoti bhikkhunupassayato. Yācitvāti “tumhehi ānītaovādeneva mayampi vasissāmā”ti yācitvā. Tatthāti tasmiṃ bhikkhunupassaye. Āgatānaṃ santike ovādena vasitabbanti pacchimikāya vassaṃ vasitabbaṃ. Abhikkhukāvāse vasantiyā āpattīti codanāmukhena sāmaññato āpattippasaṅgaṃ vadati, na pana tassā [M 3.0044] āpatti. Vassacchedaṃ katvā gacchantiyāpi āpattīti vassānupagamamūlaṃ āpattiṃ vadati. Itarāya āpattiyā anāpattikāraṇasabbhāvato “sā rakkhitabbā”ti vuttaṃ, sā vassānupagamamūlā āpatti rakkhitabbāti attho, abhikkhukepi āvāse īdisāsu āpadāsu vassaṃ upagantabbanti adhippāyo. Tenāha “āpadāsu hi…pe… anāpatti vuttā”ti. Itarāya [V 3.0040] pana āpattiyā anāpatti, kāraṇe asati pacchimikāyapi vassaṃ na upagantabbaṃ. Santesu hi bhikkhūsu vassaṃ anupagacchantiyā āpatti. Tattha gantvā pavāretabbanti ettha apavārentīnaṃ āpattisambhavato. Sace dūrepi bhikkhūnaṃ vasanaṭṭhānaṃ hoti, sakkā ca hoti navamiyaṃ gantvā pavāretuṃ, tattha gantvā pavāretabbaṃ. Sace pana navamiyaṃ nikkhamitvā sampāpuṇituṃ na sakkā hoti, agacchantīnaṃ anāpatti.

Regarding 'It is permissible': it is permissible to stay for those who believe the statement, 'Stay, venerable ladies, we will bring the bhikkhus.' 'They do not wish to go after being invited' means they do not wish to go after being invited by people; the intention is that they wish to undertake the rains-residence right there. 'From where' refers to the bhikkhunīs' dwelling. 'Having requested' means having asked, 'We too will spend the rains-residence by means of the very exhortation brought by you.' 'There' means in that bhikkhunīs' dwelling. 'One should reside with the exhortation in the presence of those who have come' means the later rains-residence should be undertaken. 'For one staying in a residence without bhikkhus, there is an offense'—this speaks of the liability to an offense in general terms by way of reproach, but there is no actual offense for her. 'For one who breaks the rains-residence and goes, there is also an offense'—this refers to an offense rooted in not undertaking the rains-residence. Because there can be a reason for no offense with regard to the other offense, it is said, 'That one should be guarded against.' The meaning is that this offense rooted in not undertaking the rains-residence should be guarded against. The intention is that even in a residence without bhikkhus, one should undertake the rains-residence in such emergencies. Therefore, it is said, 'In emergencies... no offense is declared.' But regarding the other offense, there is no offense if there is a reason; if there is no reason, one should not undertake the rains-residence even in the later part. For if bhikkhus are present and one does not undertake the rains-residence, there is an offense. 'There, one should go and perform the pavāraṇā'—this is because an offense can arise for those who do not perform the pavāraṇā. If the bhikkhus' dwelling place is far away, but it is possible to go and perform the pavāraṇā on the ninth day, one should go there and perform it. But if it is not possible to leave on the ninth day and arrive, there is no offense for those who do not go.

Uposathassa pucchanaṃ uposathapucchā, sāyeva ka-ppaccayaṃ rassattañca katvā uposathapucchakanti vuttāti āha “uposathapucchana”nti. Uposatho pucchitabboti “kadā, ayya, uposatho”ti pucchitabbo. Bhikkhunāpi “sve, bhagini, uposatho”ti vattabbaṃ. Bhikkhū kadāci kenaci kāraṇena pannarasikaṃ vā cātuddasīuposathaṃ, cātuddasikaṃ vā pannarasīuposathaṃ karonti, yasmiñca divase bhikkhūhi uposatho kato, tasmiṃyeva bhikkhunīhipi uposatho kātabboti adhippāyena “pakkhassa terasiyaṃyeva gantvā”tiādi vuttaṃ. Evaṃ pucchitena bhikkhunā sace cātuddasiyaṃ uposathaṃ karonti, “cātuddasiko bhaginī”ti vattabbaṃ. Sace pana pannarasiyaṃ karonti, “pannarasiko bhaginī”ti ācikkhitabbaṃ. Ovādatthāyāti ovādayācanatthāya. Pāṭipadadivasato pana paṭṭhāya dhammasavanatthāya gantabbanti pāṭipadadivase ovādaggahaṇatthāya dutiyadivasato paṭṭhāya antarantarā dhammasavanatthāya gantabbaṃ. Ovādaggahaṇampi hi “dhammasavanamevā”ti abhedena vuttaṃ. Nirantaraṃ vihāraṃ upasaṅkamiṃsūti yebhuyyena upasaṅkamanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vuttañhetantiādinā yathānusiṭṭhaṃ paṭipajjissāmāti sabbāsaṃyeva bhikkhunīnaṃ upasaṅkamanadīpanatthaṃ pāḷi nidassitā. Ovādaṃ gacchatīti ovādaṃ yācituṃ gacchati. Dve tissoti dvīhi tīhi. Karaṇatthe cetaṃ paccattavacanaṃ.

Asking about the Uposatha is 'Uposathapucchā.' By adding a ka-suffix and shortening it, it is called 'Uposathapucchaka'; hence it is said, 'Uposathapucchana.' The Uposatha should be asked about thus: 'Venerable sir, when is the Uposatha?' A monk should also say, 'Sister, tomorrow is the Uposatha.' Monks sometimes, for some reason, observe the fifteenth-day Uposatha as a fourteenth-day Uposatha, or the fourteenth-day Uposatha as a fifteenth-day Uposatha. On whatever day the monks observe the Uposatha, the nuns should also observe it on that same day—this is the intention behind the statement, 'going on the thirteenth day of the fortnight,' etc. When asked in this way by a nun, if the monks observe the Uposatha on the fourteenth, the monk should say, 'Sister, it is on the fourteenth.' But if they observe it on the fifteenth, he should inform her, 'Sister, it is on the fifteenth.' 'For the purpose of instruction' means for the sake of requesting instruction. 'From the first day of the fortnight onward, they should go for the purpose of hearing the Dhamma' means that on the first day of the fortnight they should go for the purpose of receiving instruction, and from the second day onward, they should go from time to time to hear the Dhamma. For receiving instruction is also spoken of as 'hearing the Dhamma' without distinction. 'They approached the monastery without interruption'—this is said with reference to their general practice of approaching. The Pali text is cited, beginning with 'Vuttañhetaṃ,' to clarify that all the nuns approach, meaning, 'We will practice as instructed.' 'She goes for instruction' means she goes to request instruction. 'Two or three' (dve tisso) means 'by two or by three' (dvīhi tīhi). This is a nominative/accusative form used in an instrumental sense.

Pāsādikenāti pasādajanakena niddosena kāyakammādinā. Sampādetūti tividhaṃ sikkhaṃ sampādetu. Sace pātimokkhuddesakaṃyeva disvā [M 3.0045] tāhi bhikkhunīhi ovādo yācito bhaveyya, tena kiṃ kātabbanti? Uposathagge sannipatite bhikkhusaṅghe pubbakiccavasena “atthi kāci bhikkhuniyo ovādaṃ yācamānā”ti pucchiyamāne “evaṃ vadehī”ti ovādapaṭiggāhakena vattabbavacanaṃ aññena bhikkhunā kathāpetvā pātimokkhuddesakena vattabbavacanaṃ attanā vatvā puna sayameva gantvā bhikkhunīnaṃ ārocetabbaṃ, aññena vā bhikkhunā tasmiṃ divase pātimokkhaṃ uddisāpetabbaṃ. Etaṃ vuttanti “tāhī”ti etaṃ bahuvacanaṃ vuttaṃ.

If, upon seeing only the Pātimokkha reciter, those bhikkhunīs were to request instruction from him, what should be done? When the Saṅgha of bhikkhus has assembled in the Uposatha hall and, as a preliminary duty, it is asked, 'Are there any bhikkhunīs requesting instruction?', the Pātimokkha reciter should have another bhikkhu say the words that are to be said by the designated receiver of the exhortation, namely 'Speak thus.' Then, having said the words that are to be said by the Pātimokkha reciter himself, he should go himself and inform the bhikkhunīs, or he should have another bhikkhu recite the Pātimokkha on that day. This is what is meant; therefore, the plural form 'tāhī' is used.

Ekā bhikkhunī vāti idaṃ bahūhi bhikkhunupassayehi ekāya eva bhikkhuniyā sāsanapaṭiggahaṇaṃ [V 3.0041] sandhāya vuttaṃ, na pana dutiyikāya abhāvaṃ sandhāya. Bahūhi bhikkhunupassayehīti antarāmagge vā tasmiṃyeva vā gāme bahūhi bhikkhunupassayehi. “Bhikkhunisaṅgho ca ayya bhikkhuniyo ca bhikkhunī cā”ti iminā nānāupassayehi sāsanaṃ gahetvā āgatabhikkhuniyā vattabbavacanaṃ dasseti. Idañca ekena pakārena mukhamattanidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ, tasmiṃ tasmiṃ pana bhikkhunupassaye bhikkhunīnaṃ pamāṇaṃ sallakkhetvā tadanurūpena nayena vattabbaṃ. Bhikkhusaṅghassa ayyānaṃ ayyassāti idaṃ saṅkhipitvā vuttaṃ.

'A single bhikkhunī' (Ekā bhikkhunī): this is said with reference to the acceptance of the message by a single bhikkhunī from many bhikkhunī residences, not with reference to the absence of a companion. 'From many bhikkhunī residences' (Bahūhi bhikkhunupassayehi) means either along the way or in that very village, from many bhikkhunī residences. The phrase 'The Saṅgha of bhikkhunīs, and the venerable bhikkhunīs, and the bhikkhunī...' (Bhikkhunisaṅgho ca ayya bhikkhuniyo ca bhikkhunī ca) shows the statement to be made by a bhikkhunī who has come having received the message from various residences. And this is said in one way merely to show the general principle; but in each bhikkhunī residence, the number of bhikkhunīs should be considered, and one should speak in accordance with that method. 'For the Bhikkhu Saṅgha, for the venerable ones, for the venerable one' (Bhikkhusaṅghassa ayyānaṃ ayyassa) — this is stated concisely.

Pātimokkhuddesakenapīti idaṃ saṅghuposathavaseneva dassitaṃ. Yattha pana tiṇṇaṃ dvinnaṃ vā vasanaṭṭhāne pātimokkhuddeso natthi, tatthāpi ñattiṭhapanakena itarena vā bhikkhunā imināva nayena vattabbaṃ. Ekapuggalenapi uposathadivase ovādayācanaṃ sampaṭicchitvā pāṭipade āgatānaṃ bhikkhunīnaṃ “natthi kocī”tiādi vattabbameva. Sace sayameva, “sammato aha”nti vattabbaṃ. Imaṃ vidhiṃ ajānanto idha bāloti adhippeto.

“Pātimokkhuddesakenapi” (even by the Pātimokkha reciter) is shown here only in the context of the Saṅgha's Uposatha. But where there is no Pātimokkha recitation in a dwelling place of three or two bhikkhus, even there, it should be spoken in this same manner by a bhikkhu who establishes a motion or by another bhikkhu. Even by a single individual, having accepted the request for instruction on the Uposatha day, it should be said to the bhikkhunīs who have come on the day after the Uposatha, “There is no one,” and so on. If he himself is the appointed one, he should say, “I am appointed.” One who does not know this procedure is here intended as a fool.

150. Adhammakamme adhammakammasaññī vaggaṃ bhikkhunisaṅghaṃ vaggasaññī ovadati, āpatti pācittiyassātiādīsu vijjamānesupi vaggādibhāvanimittesu dukkaṭesu adhammakammamūlakaṃ pācittiyameva pāḷiyaṃ sabbattha vuttanti āha “adhammakamme dvinnaṃ navakānaṃ vasena aṭṭhārasa pācittiyānī”ti. Sesamettha uttānameva. Asammatatā, bhikkhuniyā paripuṇṇūpasampannatā, ovādavasena aṭṭhagarudhammabhaṇananti imāni panettha tīṇi aṅgāni.

150. In such cases as 'If, perceiving an act as unlawful, he advises a factional bhikkhunī Saṅgha, perceiving it as a faction, there is an offense of pācittiya,' even though there are dukkaṭa offenses which are the causes for being a faction and so on, it is only the pācittiya rooted in the unlawful act that is mentioned everywhere in the Pāḷi text. Therefore, it is said: “In an unlawful act, there are eighteen pācittiya offenses based on two sets of nine.” The rest here is self-explanatory. The three factors here are: being unappointed, the bhikkhunī being fully ordained, and the recitation of the eight weighty rules by way of instruction.

Ovādasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning exhortation is concluded.

2. Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning the Setting of the Sun

153. Dutiye [M 3.0046] kusalānaṃ dhammānaṃ sātaccakiriyāyāti pubbabhāgappaṭipattivasena vuttaṃ. Munātīti jānāti. Tena ñāṇenāti tena arahattaphalapaññāsaṅkhātena ñāṇena. Pathesūti upāyamaggesu. Arahato pariniṭṭhitasikkhattā āha “idañca…pe… vutta”nti. Atha vā “appamajjato sikkhato”ti imesaṃ padānaṃ hetuatthatā daṭṭhabbā, tasmā appamajjanahetu sikkhanahetu ca adhicetasoti attho. Sokāti cittasantāpā. Ettha ca adhicetasoti iminā adhicittasikkhā, appamajjatoti iminā adhisīlasikkhā, munino monapathesu sikkhatoti etehi adhipaññāsikkhā, muninoti vā etena adhipaññāsikkhā, monapathesu sikkhatoti etena [V 3.0042] tāsaṃ lokuttarasikkhānaṃ pubbabhāgappaṭipadā, sokā na bhavantītiādīhi sikkhāpāripūriyā ānisaṃsā pakāsitāti veditabbaṃ.

153. In the second verse, 'the sustained effort in wholesome qualities' is stated in the sense of preliminary practice. “He knows” means he understands. “By that knowledge” refers to the knowledge designated as the wisdom of the fruition of arahantship. “On the paths” means on the paths of means. Because the arahant has completed the training, it is said, “And this...is stated.” Alternatively, the causal sense of the words “not being negligent” and “training” should be understood; therefore, “of heightened mind” means because of heedfulness and because of training. “Sorrow” means mental anguish. And here, it should be understood that by “of heightened mind” is meant the training in higher mind; by “not being negligent” is meant the training in higher virtue; by “the sage trains on the paths of sagacity” is meant the training in higher wisdom; or, by “the sage” is meant the training in higher wisdom, and by “training on the paths of sagacity” is meant the preliminary practice for those supramundane trainings; and by “sorrows do not arise” and so on, the benefits of the fulfillment of the training are shown.

Kokanudanti padumavisesanaṃ yathā “kokāsaya”nti, taṃ kira bahupattaṃ vaṇṇasampannaṃ ativiya sugandhañca hoti. “Kokanudaṃ nāma setapaduma”ntipi vadanti. Pātoti pageva. Ayañhettha attho – yathā kokanudasaṅkhātaṃ padumaṃ pāto sūriyuggamanavelāyaṃ phullaṃ vikasitaṃ avītagandhaṃ siyā virocamānaṃ, evaṃ sarīragandhena guṇagandhena ca sugandhaṃ saradakāle antalikkhe ādiccamiva attano tejasā tapantaṃ aṅgehi niccharaṇajutitāya aṅgīrasaṃ sammāsambuddhaṃ passāti.

“Kokanuda” is a specific kind of lotus, like “kokāsaya,” which is said to have many petals, excellent color, and a very pleasant fragrance. Some also say, “Kokanuda is a white lotus.” “At dawn” means early in the morning. The meaning here is: just as the lotus called kokanuda, at dawn at the time of sunrise, would be blooming, fully open, its fragrance undiminished, and shining brilliantly, so too should one see the Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, the Aṅgīrasa, fragrant with the scent of his body and the scent of virtue, blazing with his own power like the sun in the autumn sky, by the radiance emanating from his limbs.

Abhabboti paṭipattisāramidaṃ sāsanaṃ, paṭipatti ca pariyattimūlikā, tvañca pariyattiṃ uggahetuṃ asamattho, tasmā abhabboti adhippāyo. Suddhaṃ pilotikakhaṇḍanti iddhiyā abhisaṅkhataṃ parisuddhaṃ coḷakhaṇḍaṃ. Tadā kira bhagavā “na sajjhāyaṃ kātuṃ asakkonto mama sāsane abhabbo nāma hoti, mā soci bhikkhū”ti taṃ bāhāyaṃ gahetvā vihāraṃ pavisitvā iddhiyā pilotikakhaṇḍaṃ abhinimminitvā “handa, bhikkhu, imaṃ parimajjanto ‘rajoharaṇaṃ rajoharaṇa’nti punappunaṃ sajjhāyaṃ karohī”ti vatvā adāsi tattha pubbekatādhikārattā.

“Incapable” means this teaching has practice as its essence, and practice is rooted in learning. Since you are incapable of learning, therefore “incapable” is the intended meaning. “A clean piece of rag cloth” refers to a piece of cloth made pure by psychic power. At that time, it is said, the Blessed One, thinking, “One who is unable to recite is not called incapable in my teaching; do not grieve, monk,” took him by the arm, entered the monastery, created a piece of rag cloth by psychic power, and said, “Here, monk, while wiping this, recite ‘dust-remover, dust-remover’ repeatedly,” and gave it to him because of his past meritorious actions.

So kira pubbe rājā hutvā nagaraṃ padakkhiṇaṃ karonto nalāṭato sede muccante parisuddhena sāṭakena nalāṭaṃ puñchi, sāṭako kiliṭṭho ahosi[M 3.0047]. So “imaṃ sarīraṃ nissāya evarūpo parisuddhasāṭako pakatiṃ jahitvā kiliṭṭho jāto, aniccā vata saṅkhārā”ti aniccasaññaṃ paṭilabhati, tena kāraṇenassa rajoharaṇameva paccayo jāto. Rajaṃ haratīti rajoharaṇaṃ. Saṃvegaṃ paṭilabhitvāti asubhasaññaṃ aniccasaññañca upaṭṭhapento saṃvegaṃ paṭilabhitvā. So hi yoniso ummajjanto “parisuddhaṃ vatthaṃ, natthettha doso, attabhāvassa panāyaṃ doso”ti asubhasaññaṃ aniccasaññañca paṭilabhitvā nāmarūpapariggahādinā pañcasu khandhesu ñāṇaṃ otāretvā kalāpasammasanādikkamena vipassanaṃ vaḍḍhetvā udayabbayañāṇādipaapāṭiyā vipassanaṃ anulomagotrabhusamīpaṃ pāpesi. Taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ “vipassanaṃ ārabhī”ti. Obhāsagāthaṃ abhāsīti obhāsavissajjanapubbakabhāsitagāthā obhāsagāthā, taṃ abhāsīti attho.

It is said that previously, when he was a king, while circumambulating the city, sweat dripped from his forehead. He wiped his forehead with a clean cloth, and the cloth became soiled. He gained the perception of impermanence, reflecting, “Dependent on this body, such a clean cloth has abandoned its natural state and become soiled. Indeed, conditioned formations are impermanent!” For that reason, the 'dust-remover' itself became a condition for him. It removes dust (rajaṃ), therefore it is a 'dust-remover' (rajoharaṇaṃ). 'Having gained a sense of urgency' means having gained a sense of urgency by establishing the perception of foulness and the perception of impermanence. Indeed, while wiping it with wise attention, he gained the perception of foulness and the perception of impermanence, thinking, “The cloth is pure, there is no fault in it; this fault, however, belongs to this individuality.” Then, by applying knowledge to the five aggregates through the comprehension of name-and-form and so on, and developing insight through the sequence beginning with the comprehension of groups, he brought his insight, through the progression of knowledges beginning with the knowledge of arising and passing away, near to conformity-knowledge and change-of-lineage-knowledge. With reference to this, it was said, “he began insight.” “He uttered an illumination-verse” means: an illumination-verse is a verse spoken preceded by the emission of light; he uttered that—this is the meaning.

Ettha ca “adhicetasoti imaṃ obhāsagāthaṃ abhāsī”ti idheva vuttaṃ. Visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 2.386) pana [V 3.0043] dhammapadaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (dha. pa. aṭṭha. 1.cūḷapanthakattheravatthu) theragāthāsaṃvaṇṇanāyañca (theragā. aṭṭha. 2.566) –

And here, it is stated only in this text: “With heightened mind... he spoke this illumination-verse.” However, in the Visuddhimagga (Visuddhimagga 2.386), the Dhammapada Commentary (Dhammapadaṭṭhakathā 1, Cūḷapanthaka Thera’s Story), and the Theragāthā Commentary (Theragāthā Aṭṭhakathā 2.566) –

“Rāgo rajo na ca pana reṇu vuccati;

Rāgassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ rajoti;

Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā paṇḍitā;

Viharanti te vigatarajassa sāsane.

“Lust is dust, though it is not called fine powder; ‘Dust’ is a designation for lust. Having abandoned this dust, the wise dwell in the teaching of the one free from dust.”

“Doso…pe… sāsane.

“Hatred... in the teaching.”

“Moho rajo na ca pana reṇu vuccati;

Mohassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ rajoti;

Etaṃ rajaṃ vippajahitvā paṇḍitā;

Viharanti te vigatarajassa sāsaneti. –

“Delusion is dust, though it is not called fine powder; ‘Dust’ is a designation for delusion. Having abandoned this dust, the wise dwell in the teaching of the one free from dust.”

Imā tisso obhāsagāthā abhāsī”ti vuttaṃ. Adhicetasoti ca ayaṃ cūḷapanthakattherassa udānagāthāti imissāyeva pāḷiyā āgataṃ. Theragāthāyaṃ pana cūḷapanthakattherassa udānagāthāsu ayaṃ anāruḷhā, “ekudāniyattherassa pana ayaṃ udānagāthā”ti (theragā. aṭṭha. 1.ekudāniyattheragāthāvaṇṇanā) tattha vuttaṃ. Evaṃ santepi imissā pāḷiyā aṭṭhakathāya ca evamāgatattā cūḷapanthakattherassapi ayaṃ [M 3.0048] udānagāthā obhāsagāthāvasena ca bhagavatā bhāsitāti gahetabbaṃ. Arahattaṃ pāpuṇīti abhiññāpaṭisambhidāparivāraṃ arahattaṃ pāpuṇi. Abhabbo tvantiādivacanato anukampāvasena saddhivihārikādiṃ saṅghikavihārā nikkaḍḍhāpentassa anāpatti viya dissati. Abhabbo hi thero sañcicca taṃ kātuṃ, nikkaḍḍhanasikkhāpade vā apaññatte therena evaṃ katanti gahetabbaṃ.

It is said, “He spoke these three illumination-verses.” And “Adhicetaso…”—this verse is found in this very Pāḷi text as the inspired utterance of the Elder Cūḷapanthaka. However, in the Theragāthā, this verse is not included among the inspired utterances of the Elder Cūḷapanthaka; it is said there, “This is the inspired utterance of the Elder Ekudāniya” (Theragāthā Aṭṭhakathā, Commentary on the verse of the Elder Ekudāniya). Even so, since it is found thus in this Pāḷi text and its commentary, it should be understood that this inspired utterance is also the Elder Cūḷapanthaka's, and was spoken by the Blessed One as an illumination-verse. “He attained arahantship” means he attained arahantship accompanied by the supernormal knowledges and analytical insights. From the statement “You are incapable,” etc., it appears that there is no offense for one who has a co-resident, etc., expelled from a Saṅgha monastery out of compassion. For the Elder is incapable of doing that intentionally; or it should be understood that the Elder did so when the training rule on expulsion had not yet been laid down.

156. Ovadantassa pācittiyanti atthaṅgate sūriye garudhammehi vā aññena vā dhammeneva ovadantassa sammatassapi pācittiyaṃ. Sesamettha uttānameva. Atthaṅgatasūriyatā, paripuṇṇūpasampannatā, ovadananti imāni panettha tīṇi aṅgāni.

156. “For one who instructs, there is a pācittiya offense” means: when the sun has set, for one instructing with the weighty rules or with any other Dhamma, there is a pācittiya offense even if he is authorized. The rest here is self-explanatory. The three factors here are: the sun having set, being fully ordained, and the act of instructing.

Atthaṅgatasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning the Setting of the Sun is finished.

3. Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

3. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning a Bhikkhunī's Residence

162. Tatiyaṃ [V 3.0044] uttānatthameva. Upassayūpagamanaṃ, paripuṇṇūpasampannatā, samayābhāvo, garudhammehi ovadananti imāni panettha cattāri aṅgāni.

162. The third is of straightforward meaning. Approaching the bhikkhunīs' residence, being fully ordained, the absence of a proper occasion, and advising with the weighty principles—these are the four factors here.

Bhikkhunupassayasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning a bhikkhunī's residence is concluded.

4. Āmisasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

4. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Material Gain

164. Catutthe “upasampannaṃ…pe… bhikkhunovādaka”nti imesaṃ “maṅkukattukāmo”ti iminā sambandho. “Avaṇṇaṃ kattukāmo ayasaṃ kattukāmo”ti imesaṃ pana vasena “upasampanna”ntiādīsu “upasampannassā”ti vibhattivipariṇāmo kātabboti imamatthaṃ sandhāya “ujjhāpanake vuttanayenevattho veditabbo”ti vuttaṃ. “Cīvarahetu ovadatī”tiādinā bhaṇantassa ekekasmiṃ vacane niṭṭhite pācittiyaṃ veditabbaṃ. “Upasampannaṃ saṅghena asammata”nti pāḷivacanato “sammatena vā saṅghena vā bhāraṃ katvā ṭhapito”ti aṭṭhakathāvacanato ca aṭṭhahi aṅgehi samannāgato sammatena vā vippavasitukāmena “yāvāhaṃ āgamissāmi, tāva [M 3.0049] te bhāro hotū”ti yācitvā ṭhapito tassābhāvato saṅghena vā tatheva bhāraṃ katvā ṭhapito aṭṭhahi garudhammehi aññena vā dhammena ovadituṃ labhatīti veditabbaṃ. Tasmā “yo pana, bhikkhu, asammato bhikkhuniyo ovadeyya, pācittiya”nti idaṃ pageva bhāraṃ katvā aṭṭhapitaṃ sandhāya vuttanti gahetabbaṃ.

164. In the fourth, the connection of 'fully ordained…pe… an adviser to bhikkhunīs' is with 'intending to cause discontent.' However, by means of 'intending to cause dispraise, intending to cause disrepute,' the case ending in 'fully ordained,' and so on, should be changed to 'of the fully ordained one.' With this meaning in mind, it was said, 'The meaning should be understood according to the method stated in the section on instigation.' For one who speaks, saying, 'He advises for the sake of a robe,' and so on, a pācittiya offense should be understood upon the completion of each statement. From the Pāḷi text, 'a fully ordained one not authorized by the Saṅgha,' and from the commentary, 'or one appointed by an authorized person or by the Saṅgha, having been entrusted with the duty,' it should be understood that one who is endowed with the eight factors—whether appointed by an authorized person wishing to depart, having been requested, 'Let this be your responsibility until I return,' or, in that one's absence, similarly appointed by the Saṅgha—is permitted to advise according to the eight weighty principles or another rule. Therefore, it should be understood that the rule, 'Whatever bhikkhu, being unauthorized, should advise the bhikkhunīs, it is a pācittiya offense,' is stated in reference to one who has not been previously entrusted with this duty.

168. Anāpatti pakatiyā cīvarahetu…pe… ovadantaṃ bhaṇatīti ettha āmisahetu ovadantaṃ “āmisahetu ovadatī”ti saññāya evaṃ bhaṇantassa anāpatti, “na āmisahetu ovadatī”ti saññino pana dukkaṭaṃ, na āmisahetu ovadantaṃ pana “āmisahetu ovadatī”ti saññāya bhaṇantassapi anāpatti sacittakattā sikkhāpadassa. Sesamettha uttānameva. Upasampannatā, dhammena laddhasammutitā, anāmisantaratā, avaṇṇakāmatāya evaṃ bhaṇananti imāni panettha cattāri aṅgāni.

168. There is no offense: in speaking of one who is in fact advising for the sake of a robe…pe… Here, for one who speaks of a person advising for material gain with the perception, 'He is advising for material gain,' there is no offense. But for one who speaks thus while perceiving, 'He is not advising for material gain,' there is a dukkaṭa offense. Furthermore, for one who speaks of a person who is not advising for material gain, but does so with the perception, 'He is advising for material gain,' there is also no offense, because the training rule is intentional. The rest here is of straightforward meaning. Being fully ordained, having obtained authorization according to the Dhamma, not having material gain as an intervening factor, and speaking thus with a desire to cause dispraise—these are the four factors here.

Āmisasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule concerning material gain is concluded.

169. Pañcamaṃ uttānatthameva.

169. The fifth is of straightforward meaning.

6. Cīvarasibbāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

6. Explanation of the Training Rule on Having a Robe Sewn

175. Chaṭṭhe [V 3.0045] sace sā bhikkhunī taṃ cīvaraṃ āditova pārupeyya, aññā bhikkhuniyo disvā ujjhāpeyyuṃ, tato mahājano passituṃ na labhatīti maññamāno “yathāsaṃhaṭaṃ haritvā nikkhipitvā”tiādimāha.

175. In the sixth, thinking, 'If that bhikkhunī were to wear that robe from the very beginning, other bhikkhunīs, upon seeing it, might complain, and then the general populace would not get a chance to see it,' the Blessed One said, 'Having taken it as it was folded and having put it away,' and so on.

176. Nīharatīti sakiṃ nīharati. Yepi tesaṃ nissitakāti sambandho. Kathinavattanti “sabrahmacārīnaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti itikattabbatāvasena sūcikammakaraṇaṃ. Ācariyupajjhāyānaṃ dukkaṭanti akappiyasamādānavasena dukkaṭaṃ. Vañcetvāti “tava ñātikāyā”ti avatvā “ekissā bhikkhuniyā”ti ettakameva vatvā. “Ekissā bhikkhuniyā”ti sutvā te aññātikasaññino bhaveyyunti āha “akappiye niyojitattā”ti[M 3.0050]. “Idaṃ te mātu cīvara”ntiādīni avatvāpi “idaṃ cīvaraṃ sibbehī”ti suddhacittena sibbāpentassapi anāpatti.

176. 'He brings it out' means he brings it out once. The connection is 'also those who are their dependents.' 'The duty of the kathina' means performing needlework by way of what ought to be done, based on the principle, 'It is proper to do for fellow monastics.' 'A dukkaṭa for teachers and preceptors' means a dukkaṭa offense by way of causing to undertake what is improper. 'Having deceived' means not saying, 'It is for your relative,' but saying only this much: 'It is for a certain bhikkhunī.' He said, 'because of being engaged in what is improper,' because upon hearing, 'for a certain bhikkhunī,' they might perceive her as being unrelated. Even without saying, 'This is your mother's robe,' and so on, for one who has this robe sewn by saying, 'Sew this robe,' with a pure mind, there is no offense.

179. Upāhanatthavikādinti ādi-saddena yaṃ cīvaraṃ nivāsetuṃ vā pārupituṃ vā na sakkā hoti, tampi saṅgaṇhāti. Sesamettha uttānameva. Aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā santakatā, nivāsanapārupanūpagatā, vuttanayena sibbanaṃ vā sibbāpanaṃ vāti imāni panettha tīṇi aṅgāni.

179. 'A bag for sandals, etc.': by the word 'etc.,' any cloth that cannot be worn as a lower garment or draped as an upper garment is also included. The rest here is of straightforward meaning. Being the property of an unrelated bhikkhunī, being suitable for wearing as a lower garment or for draping as an upper garment, and sewing it or having it sewn in the manner described—these are the three factors here.

Cīvarasibbāpanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the training rule on having a robe sewn is concluded.

7. Saṃvidahanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

7. The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Making an Arrangement

181. Sattame “pacchā gacchantīnaṃ corā acchindiṃsū”ti ettha “pattacīvara”nti pāṭhasesoti āha “pacchā gacchantīnaṃ pattacīvara”nti. Tā bhikkhuniyoti pacchā gacchantiyo bhikkhuniyo. “Pacchā gacchantīna”nti ca vibhattivipariṇāmenettha sambandho veditabbo. Pāḷiyaṃ “gacchāma bhagini, gacchāma ayyā”ti bhikkhupubbakaṃ saṃvidhānaṃ vuttaṃ, “gacchāma ayya, gacchāma bhaginī”ti bhikkhunīpubbakaṃ. Ekaddhānamagganti ekaṃ addhānasaṅkhātaṃ maggaṃ, ekato vā addhānamaggaṃ. Hiyyoti suve. Pareti tatiyadivase.

181. In the seventh, regarding the phrase, 'Thieves robbed those going behind,' he said that 'bowl and robe' is the remainder of the text to be supplied, thus: 'the bowl and robe of those going behind.' 'Those bhikkhunīs' means the bhikkhunīs who were going behind. And 'of those going behind' should be understood as connected here by a change of case ending. In the Pāḷi, 'Let us go, sister; let us go, venerable sir,' is stated as an arrangement initiated by a bhikkhu, while 'Let us go, venerable sir; let us go, sister,' is one initiated by a bhikkhunī. 'A single-stage road' means a road reckoned as one stage, or a road for traveling together. 'Hiyyo' means tomorrow. 'Pare' means on the third day.

182-183. Dvidhā vuttappakāroti pādagamanavasena pakkhagamanavasena vāti dvidhā vuttappabhedo[V 3.0046]. Catunnaṃ maggānaṃ sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ catukkaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ maggānaṃ sambandhaṭṭhānaṃ siṅghāṭakaṃ. “Gāmantare gāmantare”ti ettha añño gāmo gāmantaranti āha “nikkhamane anāpatti…pe… bhikkhuno pācittiya”nti. “Saṃvidhāyā”ti pāḷiyaṃ avisesena vuttattā “neva pāḷiyā sametī”ti vuttaṃ, “etthantare saṃvidahitepi bhikkhuno dukkaṭa”nti vuttattā “na sesaaṭṭhakathāya sametī”ti vuttaṃ. Addhayojanaṃ atikkamantassāti asati gāme addhayojanaṃ atikkamantassa. Yattha hi addhayojanabbhantare añño gāmo na hoti, taṃ idha agāmakaṃ araññanti adhippetaṃ, addhayojanabbhantare pana gāme sati gāmantaragaṇanāya eva āpatti.

'Of a kind stated in two ways' means a division stated in two ways: by way of going on foot or by way of going by wing. A 'four-road junction' is the meeting point of four roads; a 'three-road junction' is the meeting point of three roads. Here, regarding 'in an intervening village,' another village is an 'intervening village'; thus he said, 'There is no offense on departure…pe… for a bhikkhu, it is a pācittiya offense.' Because 'having made an arrangement' is stated in the Pāḷi without distinction, it is said, 'This does not accord with the Pāḷi.' Because it is stated, 'Even if an arrangement is made in the interim, there is a dukkaṭa offense for the bhikkhu,' it is said, 'This does not accord with the other commentaries.' 'For one who exceeds half a yojana' means for one who exceeds half a yojana when there is no village. For where there is no other village within half a yojana, that is intended here as a 'villageless wilderness.' But if there is a village within half a yojana, the offense is incurred by the count of intervening villages.

185. Raṭṭhabhedeti raṭṭhavilope. Cakkasamāruḷhāti iriyāpathacakkaṃ sakaṭacakkaṃ vā samāruḷhā. Sesaṃ uttānameva. Dvinnampi saṃvidahitvā maggappaṭipatti[M 3.0051], avisaṅketaṃ, samayābhāvo, anāpadā, gāmantarokkamanaṃ vā addhayojanātikkamo vāti imāni panettha pañca aṅgāni. Ekatoupasampannādīhi saddhiṃ gacchantassa pana mātugāmasikkhāpadena āpatti.

185. 'In the breaking of the country' means in the plunder of the country. 'Mounted on a wheel' means mounted on the 'wheel of posture' or a cart-wheel. The rest is of straightforward meaning. Having made an arrangement for both parties and setting out on the road, keeping the appointment, the absence of a proper occasion for exemption, the absence of danger, and entering an intervening village or exceeding half a yojana—these are the five factors here. However, for one traveling together with those ordained in one Sangha, there is an offense under the training rule concerning traveling with a woman.

Saṃvidahanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rule Concerning Making an Arrangement is concluded.

8. Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

8. Explanation of the Training Rule on Embarking on a Boat

188. Aṭṭhame lokassādamittasanthavavasena kīḷāpurekkhārā saṃvidahitvāti ayaṃ viseso “evamime…pe… bhikkhunīhi saddhiṃ nāvāya kīḷantī”ti iminā “uddhaṃgāminiṃ vā adhogāminiṃ vā”ti iminā ca siddho.

188. In the eighth, this specific point—'having made an arrangement with play as the foremost intention, by way of worldly pleasure and friendly intimacy'—is established by the phrase, 'thus these…pe… playing in a boat together with bhikkhunīs,' and by the phrase, 'going upstream or going downstream.'

189. Nadiyā kuto gāmantaranti āha “yassā nadiyā”tiādi. “Tassā sagāmakatīrapassena…pe… addhayojanagaṇanāyāti ekekapasseneva gamanaṃ sandhāya vuttattā tādisikāya nadiyā majjhena gacchantassa gāmantaragaṇanāya addhayojanagaṇanāya ca āpattī”ti vadanti. Sabbaaṭṭhakathāsūtiādinā attanā vuttamevatthaṃ samattheti. “Kīḷāpurekkhāratāya bhikkhuniyā saddhiṃ saṃvidhāya nāvaṃ abhiruhantassa nadiyaṃyeva pācittiyassa vuttattā vāpisamuddādīsu kīḷāpurekkhāratāya dukkaṭameva, na pācittiya”nti vadanti. “Lokassādamittasanthavavasena kīḷāpurekkhārā saṃvidahitvā”ti vacanato keci “imaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ akusalacittaṃ lokavajja”nti vadanti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Kīḷāpurekkhāratāya hi abhiruhitvāpi gāmantarokkamane addhayojanātikkame vā kusalābyākatacittasamaṅgīpi hutvā āpattiṃ āpajjati[V 3.0047]. Yadi hi so saṃvegaṃ paṭilabhitvā arahattaṃ vā sacchikareyya, niddaṃ vā okkameyya, kammaṭṭhānaṃ vā manasi karonto gaccheyya, kuto tassa akusalacittasamaṅgitā, yenidaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ akusalacittaṃ lokavajjanti vuccati, tasmā paṇṇattivajjaṃ ticittanti siddhaṃ. Sesamettha uttānameva.

189. ‘From where is the village beyond the river?’ He says, ‘From whichever river,’ and so on. ‘By the side of that river where the village is located…and so on…by the calculation of half a yojana.’ Since the going is stated with reference to only one side, they say that for one going through the middle of such a river, an offense is incurred by the calculation of another village and by the calculation of half a yojana. He supports the meaning he has stated himself with ‘in all the commentaries,’ and so on. They say, ‘Because, for one boarding a boat having arranged with a bhikkhunī with play as the foremost intention, a pācittiya offense is stated only for the river itself; in lakes, the sea, and so on, due to the intention to play, it is only a dukkaṭa, not a pācittiya.’ Based on the statement ‘having arranged with play as the foremost intention, by way of worldly pleasure and friendly intimacy,’ some say, ‘this training rule is a worldly fault of unwholesome mind.’ That should not be accepted. For even having boarded with play as the foremost intention, when descending into another village or exceeding half a yojana, even being endowed with a wholesome or indeterminate mind, one incurs an offense. If indeed he were to gain a sense of urgency and realize arahantship, or fall asleep, or go while applying his mind to a meditation subject—how could he be endowed with an unwholesome mind, whereby this training rule is said to be a worldly fault of unwholesome mind? Therefore, it is established that it is a regulatory offense applicable to the three types of mind. The rest here is self-evident.

Nāvābhiruhanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule on boarding a boat is concluded.

9. Paripācitasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

9. Commentary on the Training Rule on Prepared Food

194. Navame [M 3.0052] paṭiyāditanti bhikkhūnaṃ atthāya sampāditaṃ. Ñātakā vā honti pavāritā vāti ettha sacepi bhikkhuno aññātakā appavāritā ca siyuṃ, bhikkhuniyā ñātakā pavāritā ce, vaṭṭati.

194. In the ninth, 'prepared' (paṭiyādita) means arranged for the benefit of the bhikkhus. Regarding 'they are relatives or invited': here, even if they are not relatives of the bhikkhu and he is not invited, if they are relatives of the bhikkhunī or she is invited, it is allowable.

197. Pāpabhikkhūnaṃ pakkhupacchedāya idaṃ paññattaṃ, tasmā pañcabhojaneyeva āpatti vuttā. Pañca bhojanāni ṭhapetvā sabbattha anāpattīti idaṃ pana iminā sikkhāpadena anāpattidassanatthaṃ vuttaṃ. Viññattiyā uppannaṃ paribhuñjantassa hi aññattha vuttanayena dukkaṭaṃ. Sesaṃ uttānameva. Bhikkhuniparipācitabhāvo, jānanaṃ, gihisamārambhābhāvo, odanādīnaṃ aññataratā, tassa ajjhoharaṇanti imāni panettha pañca aṅgāni.

197. This was laid down to cut off the support of wicked bhikkhus; therefore, an offense is stated only in connection with the five kinds of food. However, the statement 'excluding the five kinds of food, there is no offense in all cases' is said for the purpose of showing non-offense by this training rule. For one who consumes what was obtained through a request, there is indeed a dukkaṭa offense according to the method stated elsewhere. The rest is self-evident. The state of having been prepared by a bhikkhunī, knowing this, the absence of an undertaking by a householder, its being one of the foods such as cooked rice, and the act of swallowing it—these are the five factors here.

Paripācitasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning prepared food is concluded.

10. Rahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

10. Commentary on the Training Rule on Secluded Sitting

198. Dasame upanandassa catutthasikkhāpadenāti appaṭicchanne mātugāmena saddhiṃ rahonisajjasikkhāpadaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Kiñcāpi taṃ acelakavagge pañcamasikkhāpadaṃ hoti, upanandattheraṃ ārabbha paññattesu pana catutthabhāvato “upanandassa catutthasikkhāpadenā”ti vuttaṃ. Catutthasikkhāpadassa vatthuto imassa sikkhāpadassa vatthuno paṭhamaṃ uppannattā idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ paṭhamaṃ paññattaṃ. Iminā ca sikkhāpadena kevalaṃ bhikkhuniyā eva rahonisajjāya āpatti paññattā, upari mātugāmena saddhiṃ rahonisajjāya āpatti visuṃ paññattāti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

198. In the tenth, 'by the fourth training rule of Upananda' is stated with reference to the training rule on secluded sitting with a woman in an unconcealed place. Although that is the fifth training rule in the Acelaka Section, it is said 'by the fourth training rule of Upananda' because it is the fourth among those laid down in connection with the Elder Upananda. Because the story of this training rule arose before the story of that fourth training rule, this training rule was laid down first. And it should be understood that by this training rule an offense is laid down only for secluded sitting with a bhikkhunī, whereas an offense for secluded sitting with a woman is laid down separately later on.

Rahonisajjasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule on secluded sitting is concluded.

Niṭṭhito bhikkhunivaggo tatiyo.

The third Bhikkhunī Section is concluded.

4. Bhojanavaggo

4. The Section on Food

1. Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

1. Commentary on the Training Rule Concerning Alms-food at a Public Rest House

206. Bhojanavaggassa [M 3.0053][V 3.0048] paṭhamasikkhāpade addhayojanaṃ vā yojanaṃ vā gantuṃ sakkotīti ettha tattakaṃ gantuṃ sakkontassapi tāvatakaṃ gantvā aladdhabhikkhassa ito bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. Imesaṃyevāti imesaṃ pāsaṇḍānaṃyeva. Ettakānanti imasmiṃ pāsaṇḍe ettakānaṃ. Ekadivasaṃ bhuñjitabbanti ekadivasaṃ sakiṃyeva bhuñjitabbaṃ. “Ekadivasaṃ bhuñjitabba”nti vacanato pana ekasmiṃ divase punappunaṃ bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti na gahetabbaṃ. Puna ādito paṭṭhāya bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭatīti iminā paṭhamaṃ bhuttaṭṭhānesu puna ekasmimpi ṭhāne bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭatīti dasseti.

206. In the first training rule of the Section on Food, regarding 'is able to go half a yojana or a yojana,' here, even for one who is able to go that far, if, having gone that far, he has not obtained alms-food, it is allowable to eat from here. 'Of these' means of these sectarians. 'So many' means so many in this sect. 'Should be eaten in one day' means it should be eaten only once in one day. However, from the statement 'should be eaten in one day,' it should not be understood that it is allowable to eat repeatedly in one day. By the phrase 'it is not allowable to eat again starting from the beginning,' it shows that it is not allowable to eat again in even one of the places where one has eaten before.

208. “Gacchanto vā āgacchanto vāti idaṃ addhayojanavasena gahetabba”nti vadanti. Antarāmagge gataṭṭhāneti ekasseva santakaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Āgacchantepi eseva nayo”ti saṅkhepena vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāvento “gantvā paccāgacchanto”tiādimāha. Āpattiṭṭhāneyeva puna bhuñjantassa anāpatti vattabbāti gamane āgamane ca paṭhamaṃ bhojanaṃ avatvā antarāmagge ekadivasaṃ gataṭṭhāne ca ekadivasanti punappunaṃ bhojanameva dassitaṃ, gamanadivase pana āgamanadivase ca “gamissāmi āgamissāmī”ti bhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Suddhacittena punappunaṃ bhuñjantassapi punappunaṃ bhojane anāpatti. Aññassatthāya uddisitvā paññattaṃ bhikkhuno gahetumeva na vaṭṭatīti āha “bhikkhūnaṃyeva atthāyā”ti. Sesamettha uttānameva. Āvasathapiṇḍatā, agilānatā, anuvasitvā bhojananti imāni panettha tīṇi aṅgāni.

208. They say, '“Going or coming” should be understood in terms of half a yojana.' 'At a place on the road' is stated with reference to what belongs to only one person. Clarifying the meaning of what was concisely stated as 'the same principle applies when returning,' he says, 'having gone and returning,' and so on. It should be stated that there is no offense for one who eats again at the very place of an offense; therefore, regarding going and coming, without mentioning the first meal, only repeated eating is shown by 'on the road for one day' and 'at the place one has gone for one day.' However, on the day of departure and on the day of return, it is indeed allowable to eat with the thought, 'I will go, I will return.' For one who eats repeatedly with a pure mind, there is no offense in repeated eating. He says 'for the benefit of the bhikkhus themselves' because it is not allowable for a bhikkhu to even take what is designated and prepared for the benefit of another. The rest here is self-evident. The nature of being alms-food from a public rest house, not being ill, and eating without having stayed over—these are the three factors here.

Āvasathapiṇḍasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the training rule concerning alms-food at a public rest house is concluded.

2. Gaṇabhojanasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

2. Commentary on the Training Rule on Group Meals

209. Dutiye abhimāreti abhigantvā bhagavato māraṇatthāya niyojite dhanuddhare. Guḷhapaṭicchannoti apākaṭo. Pavijjhīti vissajjesi. Nanu rājānampi mārāpesīti vacanato idaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ ajātasattuno kāle paññattanti siddhaṃ, evañca sati parato anupaññattiyaṃ –

209. In the second, 'abhimāreti' refers to the archers who, having approached, were appointed for the purpose of killing the Blessed One. 'Guḷhapaṭicchanno' means not manifest. 'Pavijjhīti' means he released. From the statement, 'Did you not also cause the king to be killed?' it is established that this training rule was laid down during the time of Ajātasattu. This being the case, regarding a subsequent enactment later on—

“Tena [M 3.0054][V 3.0049] kho pana samayena rañño māgadhassa seniyassa bimbisārassa ñātisālohito ājīvakesu pabbajito hoti. Atha kho so ājīvako yena rājā māgadho seniyo bimbisāro tenupasaṅkami, upasaṅkamitvā rājānaṃ māgadhaṃ seniyaṃ bimbisāraṃ etadavoca…pe… kukkuccāyantā nādhivāsentī”ti –

“At that time, a relative and blood relation of King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha had gone forth among the Ājīvakas. Then that Ājīvaka approached King Seniya Bimbisāra of Magadha and said to him: …being scrupulous, they did not accept it.”

Idaṃ kasmā vuttanti? So kira ājīvako taṃ dānaṃ dento bimbisārakālato paṭṭhāya adāsi, pacchā ajātasattukāle sikkhāpadapaññattito paṭṭhāya bhikkhū kukkuccāyantā taṃ dānaṃ na paṭiggaṇhiṃsu, tasmā ādito paṭṭhāya taṃ vatthu dassitanti veditabbaṃ. “Atha kho so ājīvako bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesī”ti idañca tato pabhuti so ājīvako antarantarā bhikkhū nimantetvā dānaṃ dento ajātasattukāle sikkhāpade paññatte yaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ santike dūtaṃ pāhesi, taṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

Why was this said? It is said that this Ājīvaka had been giving that donation from the time of Bimbisāra. Later, from when the training rule was laid down in the time of Ajātasattu, the bhikkhus, being scrupulous, did not accept that donation. Therefore, it should be understood that the story was shown from the beginning. And the statement, 'Then that Ājīvaka sent a messenger to the bhikkhus,' was said with reference to the messenger he sent to the bhikkhus when the training rule was laid down in the time of Ajātasattu, since from that time onward that Ājīvaka had been giving donations, inviting the bhikkhus from time to time.

215. Aññamaññavisiṭṭhattā visadisaṃ rajjaṃ virajjaṃ, tato āgatā, tattha vā jātā, bhavāti vā verajjā, te eva verajjakā. Te pana yasmā gottacaraṇādivibhāgena nānappakārā, tasmā vuttaṃ “nānāverajjake”ti. Aṭṭhakathāyaṃ pana nānāvidhehi aññarajjehi āgateti rajjānaṃyeva vasena nānappakāratā vuttā.

215. Because they are mutually distinct, a dissimilar realm is a 'virajjaṃ'. Those who have come from there, or were born there, or exist there are 'verajjā'; they themselves are the 'verajjakā'. And since they are of various kinds due to divisions such as lineage and conduct, it is therefore said 'nānāverajjake'. In the Commentary, however, their diversity is explained in terms of the realms themselves, stating that they have come from various other realms.

217-218. Imassa sikkhāpadassa viññattiṃ katvā bhuñjanavatthusmiṃ paññattattā viññattito gaṇabhojanaṃ vatthuvaseneva pākaṭanti taṃ avatvā “gaṇabhojanaṃ nāma yattha…pe… nimantitā bhuñjantī”ti nimantanavaseneva padabhājane gaṇabhojanaṃ vuttaṃ. “Kiñci pana sikkhāpadaṃ vatthuananurūpampi siyāti padabhājane vuttanayena nimantanavaseneva gaṇabhojanaṃ hotīti kesañci āsaṅkā bhaveyyā”ti taṃnivattanatthaṃ “taṃ panetaṃ gaṇabhojanaṃ dvīhākārehi pasavatī”ti vuttaṃ. Pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvāti ettha “bhojanaṃ gaṇhathāti vuttepi gaṇabhojanaṃ hotiyevā”ti vadanti. “Heṭṭhā addhānagamanavatthusmiṃ nāvābhiruhanavatthusmiñca ‘idheva, bhante, bhuñjathā’ti vutte yasmā kukkuccāyantā na paṭiggaṇhiṃsu, tasmā ‘bhuñjathā’ti vuttepi [M 3.0055] gaṇabhojanaṃ na hotiyevā”ti tīsupi gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. “Pañcannaṃ bhojanānaṃ nāmaṃ gahetvā nimantetī”ti vuttattā pana “odanaṃ bhuñjathā”ti vā “bhattaṃ bhuñjathā”ti vā bhojananāmaṃ gahetvāva vutte gaṇabhojanaṃ hoti, na aññathā. “Idheva, bhante, bhuñjathā”ti etthāpi “odana”nti vā “bhatta”nti vā vatvāva te evaṃ nimantesunti gahetabbaṃ.
