Just as when a seed exists, a tree grows dependent on that seed, conditioned by the seed, and having grown, stands filling the sky with branches and foliage, in the same way, when the female faculty, designated as womanhood, exists, female characteristics and so on come into being. For indeed, the female faculty is like the seed, and just as a tree, having grown dependent on the seed, stands filling the sky, so too the female characteristics and so on arise in the course of existence, dependent on the female faculty. Herein, the female faculty is not cognizable by the eye, but only by the mind. The female characteristics and so on, however, are cognizable both by the eye and by the mind.”

Tenevāha “tattha vicāraṇakkamo vitthārato aṭṭhasāliniyā dhammasaṅgahaṭṭhakathāya veditabbo”ti.

Therefore he said, “The method of investigation there should be understood in detail from the Aṭṭhasālinī, the commentary on the Dhammasaṅgaṇī.”

Ubhatobyañjanakavatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Topic Concerning Those of Dual Gender is concluded.

Anupajjhāyakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Those Beginning with One Without a Preceptor

117. Sikkhāpadaṃ [V 3.0239] apaññattaṃ hotīti idheva paññattaṃ sikkhāpadaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Upajjhaṃ aggāhāpetvāti “upajjhāyo me, bhante, hohī”ti evaṃ upajjhaṃ aggāhāpetvā. Kammavācāya pana upajjhāyakittanaṃ kataṃyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Aññathā “puggalaṃ na parāmasatī”ti vuttakammavipattisambhavato kammaṃ kuppeyya, teneva “upajjhāyaṃ akittetvā”ti avatvā “upajjhaṃ aggāhāpetvā”icceva vuttaṃ. Yathā ca aparipuṇṇapattacīvarassa upasampādanakāle kammavācāya “paripuṇṇassa pattacīvara”nti asantavatthuṃ kittetvā kammavācāya katāyapi upasampadā ruhati, evaṃ “ayaṃ buddharakkhito āyasmato dhammarakkhitassa upasampadāpekkho”ti asantaṃ puggalaṃ kittetvā kevalaṃ santapadanīhārena kammavācāya katāya upasampadā ruhatiyevāti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenevāha “kammaṃ pana na kuppatī”ti. “Na, bhikkhave, anupajjhāyako upasampādetabbo, yo upasampādeyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti ettakameva vatvā “so ca puggalo anupasampanno”ti avuttattā kammavipattilakkhaṇassa ca asambhavato “taṃ na gahetabba”nti vuttaṃ. “Pañcavaggakaraṇañce, bhikkhave, kammaṃ paṇḍakapañcamo kammaṃ kareyya, akammaṃ na ca karaṇīya”ntiādivacanato (mahāva. 390) paṇḍakādīnampi ubhatobyañjanakapariyantānaṃ gaṇapūrakabhāveyeva kammaṃ kuppati, na aññathāti āha “ubhatobyañjanakupajjhāyapariyosānesupi eseva nayo”ti.

117. “The training rule has not been established”—this is said with reference to the training rule established right here. “Having secured a preceptor” means having secured a preceptor by saying, “Venerable sir, be my preceptor.” But it should be understood that the declaration of the preceptor has already been made in the formal act. Otherwise, since it was stated, “One should not focus on an individual,” the formal act could be invalidated due to the possibility of a flawed procedure. Therefore, instead of saying, “without declaring the preceptor,” it is simply said, “having secured a preceptor.” Just as, at the time of ordination for one whose bowl and robes are incomplete, even if the formal act is performed by declaring, “He has a complete bowl and robes,” despite it being untrue, the ordination is still valid—similarly, even if the formal act is performed by falsely declaring, “This Venerable Buddharakkhita is seeking ordination under Venerable Dhammarakkhita,” when no such person exists, the ordination is valid solely by the utterance of the established phrases of the formal act. Hence, it is said, “But the formal act is not invalidated.” “Monks, one without a preceptor should not be ordained. Whoever ordains such a person commits an offense of wrongdoing”—having stated only this much, since it was not said, “That person is not ordained,” and because the defining characteristic of a flawed formal act does not apply, it is said, “that is not to be accepted.” From the statement, “Monks, if a group of five performs a formal act with a paṇḍaka as the fifth, the act is invalid and should not be done” (Mahāvagga 390), it is clear that even in cases involving paṇḍakas and those up to hermaphrodites, the formal act is invalidated only when they complete the group, not otherwise. Therefore, it is said, “The same principle applies even in cases ending with a preceptor who is a hermaphrodite.”

Anupajjhāyakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of Those Beginning with One Without a Preceptor is concluded.

Apattakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Those Beginning with One Who Has Committed an Offense

118. Aññe [M 3.0264] vā bhikkhū dātukāmā hontīti sambandho. Anāmaṭṭhapiṇḍapātanti aggahitaaggaṃ piṇḍapātaṃ. Sāmaṇerabhāgasamako āmisabhāgoti ettha kiñcāpi sāmaṇerānaṃ āmisabhāgassa samakameva diyyamānattā visuṃ sāmaṇerabhāgo nāma natthi, heṭṭhā gacchantaṃ pana bhattaṃ kadāci mandaṃ bhaveyya, tasmā upari aggahetvā sāmaṇerapāḷiyāva gahetvā dātabboti adhippāyo. Niyatapabbajjasseva cāyaṃ bhāgo dīyati. Teneva “apakkaṃ patta”ntiādi vuttaṃ.

118. “Or other monks may wish to give”—this is the connection. “Untouched almsfood” means almsfood from which the top portion has not been taken. Regarding “a material portion equal to a novice’s share”: here, although what is given is exactly equal to the material portion for novices, there is no separate portion called the novice’s share. However, the food passed down the line may sometimes be meager; therefore, the intention is that, without taking from the top, it should be taken from the novice's row and given. And this portion is given only to one destined for ordination. Hence, “an unbaked bowl,” etc., is said.

Apattakādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of Those Beginning with One Who Has Committed an Offense is concluded.

Hatthacchinnādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Those Beginning with One Whose Hand is Cut Off

119. Ajapadaketi [V 3.0240] ajapadasaṇṭhāne padese. Brahmujugattoti brahmā viya ujugatto. Avaseso sattoti iminā lakkhaṇena rahitasatto. Etena ṭhapetvā mahāpurisaṃ cakkavattiñca itare sattā khujjapakkhikāti dasseti. Yebhuyyena hi sattā khandhe kaṭiyaṃ jāṇūsūti tīsu ṭhānesu namanti. Te kaṭiyaṃ namantā pacchato namanti, itaresu dvīsu ṭhānesu namantā purato namanti. Dīghasarīrā pana ekena passena vaṅkā honti, eke mukhaṃ unnāmetvā nakkhattāni gaṇayantā viya caranti, eke appamaṃsalohitā sūlasadisā honti, eke purato pabbhārā honti, pavedhamānā gacchanti. Parivaṭumoti samantato vaṭṭalo.

119. “Ajapadaka” means in a place shaped like a goat’s footprint. “Brahmujugatta” means straight-bodied like a Brahmā. “The remaining beings” refers to beings lacking these characteristics. By this, it is shown that, except for the Great Man and the Wheel-Turning Monarch, other beings are hunchbacked. For the most part, beings bend at three places: the shoulders, the waist, and the knees. Those who bend at the waist lean backward; those who bend at the other two places lean forward. Some with long bodies are crooked on one side; some walk with their faces raised as if counting stars; some are extremely lean like stakes; some have their fronts bent forward, and they walk trembling. “Parivaṭuma” means rounded all around.

Aṭṭhisirācammasarīroti aṭṭhisirācammamattasarīro. Kappasīsoti dvidhābhūtasīso. Kekaroti tiriyaṃ passanto. “Udakatārakā nāma udakapubbuḷa”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Akkhitārakāti akkhibhaṇḍakā. Nippakhumakkhīti akkhidalalomehi virahitaakkhiko. Pakhuma-saddo hi loke akkhidalalomesu niruḷho. Paṭaṅgamaṇḍūko nāma mahāmukhamaṇḍūko. Eḷamukhoti niccapaggharaṇakalālamukho. Sabbañcetanti “kacchugatto vā”tiādiṃ sandhāya vadati. Vātaṇḍikoti aṇḍakesu vuddhirogena samannāgato. Vikaṭoti tiriyaṃ gamanapādehi samannāgato, yassa ca caṅkamato [M 3.0265] jāṇukā bahi gacchanti. Paṇhoti pacchato parivattapādehi samannāgato, yassa caṅkamato jāṇukā anto pavisanti.

“Aṭṭhisirācammasarīra” means a body consisting only of bones, sinews, and skin. “Kappasīsa” means a head split in two. “Kekara” means looking sideways. “Udakatārakā” refers to water bubbles, as mentioned in the commentaries. “Akkhitārakā” means the eyeballs. “Nippakhumakkhi” means an eye devoid of eyelashes. The term “pakhuma” is commonly used for eyelashes. “Paṭaṅgamaṇḍūka” refers to a large-mouthed frog. “Eḷamukha” means a mouth constantly dripping saliva. “Sabbañceta” refers to “like a scabby body,” etc. “Vātaṇḍika” means afflicted with a disease causing swelling in the testicles. “Vikaṭa” means having feet suited for walking sideways, and whose knees protrude outward when walking. “Paṇha” means having feet turned backward, and whose knees bend inward when walking.

Kudaṇḍapādatāya kāraṇaṃ vibhāveti “majjhe saṅkuṭitapādattā”ti. Agge saṅkuṭitapādattāti kuṇḍapādatāya kāraṇanidassanaṃ. Kuṇḍapādasseva gamanasabhāvaṃ vibhāveti “piṭṭhipādaggena caṅkamanto”ti. Mammananti khalitavacanaṃ. Yo ekameva akkharaṃ catupañcakkhattuṃ vadati, tassetaṃ adhivacanaṃ.

The reason for kudaṇḍapādatā is explained as “having feet bent in the middle.” “Having feet bent at the front” is an example of the reason for kuṇḍapādatā. The manner of walking of one with kuṇḍapāda is explained as “walking on the tips of the heels.” “Mammana” means faltering speech. This is a designation for one who speaks a single syllable four or five times.

Hatthacchinnādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Story of Those Beginning with One Whose Hand is Cut Off is concluded.

Alajjīnissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Matter Concerning Dependence on the Shameless

120. Nissayapaṭisaṃyuttavatthūsu bhikkhūhi samāno sīlādiguṇabhāgo assāti bhikkhusabhāgo, tassa bhāvo bhikkhusabhāgatā. Dve tīṇi divasāni vasitvā gantukāmena anissitena [V 3.0241] vasitabbanti ettha “yāva bhikkhusabhāgataṃ jānāmī”ti ābhogaṃ vināpi anissitena vasituṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo. Bhikkhusabhāgataṃ pana jānanto “sve gamissāmi, kiṃ me nissayenā”ti aruṇaṃ uṭṭhapetuṃ na labhati. “Purāruṇā uṭṭhahitvāva gamissāmī”ti ābhogena sayantassa sace aruṇo uggacchati, vaṭṭati. “Sattāhaṃ vasissāmī”ti ālayaṃ karontena pana nissayo gahetabboti “sattāhamattaṃ vasissāmi, kiṃ bhikkhusabhāgatājānanenā”ti jānane dhuraṃ nikkhipitvā vasituṃ na labhati, bhikkhusabhāgataṃ upaparikkhitvā nissayo gahetabboti attho.

120. Regarding the matters connected with dependence: Bhikkhusabhāga means having a share of qualities such as virtue, etc., equal to that of monks; the state of being such is bhikkhusabhāgatā. Here, the meaning is that if one has stayed for two or three days and wishes to depart, it is permissible to dwell without dependence even without reflecting, 'Until I know the bhikkhusabhāgatā.' However, one who knows the bhikkhusabhāgatā is not permitted to let dawn break while thinking, 'I will leave tomorrow; what need do I have for dependence?' If one who intends to rise before dawn and depart falls asleep and dawn breaks, it is permissible. But if one resolves, 'I will stay for seven days,' then dependence must be taken. One cannot dwell having abandoned the duty of knowing, thinking, 'I will stay only seven days; what need is there to know the bhikkhusabhāgatā?' The meaning is that after examining the bhikkhusabhāgatā, dependence must be taken.

Gamikādinissayavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Matter Concerning Dependence for Travelers and So Forth

121. Antarāmagge vissamanto vā…pe… anāpattīti asati nissayadāyake anāpatti. Tassa nissāyāti pāḷianurūpato vuttaṃ, taṃ nissāyāti attho. Sace pana āsāḷhīmāse…pe… tattha gantabbanti ettha sace so vassūpanāyikāya āsannāya gantukāmo suṇāti “asuko mahāthero āgamissatī”ti, tañce āgameti, vaṭṭati. Āgamentasseva [M 3.0266] ce vassūpanāyikadivaso hoti, hotu, gantabbaṃ tattha, yattha nissayadāyakaṃ labhati. Keci pana “sace so gacchanto jīvitantarāyaṃ brahmacariyantarāyaṃ vā passati, tattheva vasitabba”nti vadanti.

121. If one rests along the way... there is no offense if there is no one to give dependence. The phrase 'tassa nissāya' is stated in accordance with the Pāli; its meaning is 'depending on that'. But if in the month of Āsāḷha... one should go there. Here, if one who wishes to depart when the rains residence is near hears, 'Such and such a senior monk will come,' and if he awaits that monk, it is permissible. Even if the day of the rains residence arrives while he is awaiting him, so be it; one should go where someone to give dependence can be found. Some, however, say, 'If while going, one encounters danger to life or danger to the holy life, one should stay right there.'

Gottena anussāvanānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Account of Permitting the Announcement by Clan.

122. “Itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato”ti nāmakittanassa anussāvanāya āgatattā “nāhaṃ ussahāmi therassa nāmaṃ gahetu”nti vuttaṃ, “āyasmato pippalissa upasampadāpekkho”ti evaṃ nāmaṃ gahetuṃ na ussahāmīti attho. “Gottenapi anussāvetu”nti vacanato yena vohārena voharati, tena vaṭṭatīti siddhaṃ. “Konāmo te upajjhāyo”ti puṭṭhenapi gottameva nāmaṃ katvā vattabbanti siddhaṃ hoti, tasmā catubbidhesu nāmesu yena kenaci nāmena anussāvanā kātabbāti vadanti. Ekassa bahūni nāmāni honti, tattha ekaṃ nāmaṃ ñattiyā, ekaṃ anussāvanāya kātuṃ na vaṭṭati, atthato byañjanato ca abhinnāhi anussāvanāhi bhavitabbanti. Kiñcāpi “itthannāmo itthannāmassa āyasmato”ti pāḷiyaṃ “āyasmato”ti padaṃ pacchā vuttaṃ, kammavācāpāḷiyaṃ pana “ayaṃ buddharakkhito āyasmato dhammarakkhitassā”ti paṭhamaṃ likhitanti taṃ uppaṭipāṭiyā vuttanti na paccetabbaṃ. Pāḷiyañhi “itthannāmo itthannāmassa [V 3.0242] āyasmato”ti atthamattaṃ dassitaṃ, tasmā pāḷiyaṃ avuttopi “ayaṃ buddharakkhito āyasmato dhammarakkhitassā”ti kammavācāpāḷiyaṃ payogo dassito. “Na me diṭṭho ito pubbe iccāyasmā sāriputto”ti ca “āyasmā sāriputto atthakusalo”ti ca paṭhamaṃ “āyasmā”ti payogassa dassanatoti vadanti. Katthaci “āyasmato buddharakkhitattherassā”ti vatvā katthaci kevalaṃ “buddharakkhitassā”ti sāveti, sāvanaṃ hāpetīti na vuccati nāmassa ahāpitattāti eke. Sace katthaci “āyasmato buddharakkhitassā”ti vatvā katthaci “buddharaakhatassāyasmato”ti sāveti, pāṭhānurūpattā khettameva otiṇṇantipi eke. Byañjanabhedappasaṅgato anussāvanānaṃ taṃ na vaṭṭatīti vadanti. Sace pana sabbaṭṭhānepi eteneva pakārena vadati, vaṭṭati.

122. Because the phrase 'Such and such is the name of the Venerable so-and-so' is stated for the purpose of announcing the name, it is said, 'I do not dare to take the elder’s name.' The meaning is, 'I do not dare to take the name thus: “…the ordination-seeker of the venerable Pippali.”' From the statement, 'Let him announce by clan name too,' it is established that it is permissible to use whatever designation one uses. Even when asked, 'What is the name of your preceptor?' it is established that one should answer by giving the clan name as the name. Therefore, they say that of the four kinds of names, the announcement should be made by any name. One person may have many names. In such cases, it is not permissible to use one name for the motion and another for the announcement; the announcements must be identical in meaning and wording. Although in the Pāli text, the word 'venerable' is placed afterward—'such and such is the name of the venerable so-and-so'—in the Pāli of the formal act, it is written first: 'This Buddharakkhita is of the venerable Dhammarakkhita.' This should not be accepted as stated in reverse order. For in the Pāli text, only the meaning is shown—'such and such is the name of the venerable so-and-so'—so even though it is not stated in the Pāli, the usage 'This Buddharakkhita is of the venerable Dhammarakkhita' is shown in the Pāli of the formal act. They say that in phrases like, 'I have not seen the venerable Sāriputta before,' and, 'The venerable Sāriputta is skilled in meaning,' the usage of 'venerable' first is shown. In some cases, one says, 'of the venerable elder Buddharakkhita,' and in others, simply announces, 'of Buddharakkhita.' This is not called an omission of the announcement, because the name is not omitted—so say some. If in some places one says, 'of the venerable Buddharakkhita,' and in others, 'of Buddharakkhita, the venerable,' some say this is merely a variation in phrasing that has entered the usage. However, they say that due to the possibility of variations in wording, such variations are not permissible for announcements. If, however, one speaks in this same manner in all instances, it is permissible.

Dveupasampadāpekkhādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Account of Matters Concerning the Two Ordination-Seekers and So Forth.

123. Ekānussāvaneti [M 3.0267] ettha ekato anussāvanaṃ etesanti ekānussāvanāti asamānādhikaraṇavisayo bāhiratthasamāsoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Tenevāha “dve ekatoanussāvane”ti. Tattha ekatoti ekakkhaṇeti attho, vibhattialopena cāyaṃ niddeso. Purimanayeneva ekatoanussāvane kātunti “ekena ekassa, aññena itarassā”tiādinā pubbe vuttanayena dvīhi vā tīhi vā ācariyehi ekena vā ekatoanussāvane kātuṃ.

123. Here, 'ekānussāvana' means 'proclamation together for these'; thus, 'ekānussāvana' should be understood as a bahubbīhi compound with a different case relation, referring to an external object. Therefore, it is said, 'two proclamations together.' Here, 'ekato' means 'at one moment,' and this expression is due to the elision of the case ending. In the same manner as before, the proclamations together are to be made, as stated previously, by one teacher for one person and by another for the other, or by two or three teachers, or by one teacher making the proclamations together.

Upasampadāvidhikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Account of the Procedure for Ordination.

126. Vajjāvajjaṃ upanijjhāyatīti upajjhāti iminā upajjhāyasaddasamānattho upajjhāsaddopīti dasseti.

126. One who contemplates what is blameworthy and what is not blameworthy is called an 'upajjhā'. This indicates that the word 'upajjhā' also has a meaning similar to the word 'upajjhāya'.

Cattāronissayādikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Account of the Four Supports and So Forth.

130. Sambhogeti dhammasambhoge āmisasambhoge ca. Anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāseti ettha ca ayamadhippāyo – yasmā ayaṃ osāraṇakammassa katattā pakatattaṭṭhāne ṭhito, tasmā na ukkhittakena saddhiṃ sambhogādipaccayā pācittiyaṃ, nāpi alajjinā saddhiṃ paribhogapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ alajjīlakkhaṇānupapattito. Yo hi ucchurasakasaṭānaṃ sattāhakālikayāvajīvikattā vaṭṭati vikāle ucchu khāditunti saññaṃ uppādetvā taṃ khāditvā tappaccayā pācittiyaṃ na passati [V 3.0243] “vaṭṭatī”ti tathāsaññitāya, yo vā pana āpattimāpannabhāvaṃ paṭijānitvā “na paṭikaromī”ti abhinivisati, ayaṃ –

130. 'Sambhoga' (communion) refers to both communion in the Dhamma and communion in material things. Regarding 'There is no offense in communion and dwelling together,' the intended meaning here is this: because this person, having undergone the act of rehabilitation, is established in his normal state, there is no Pācittiya offense due to communion and so forth with one who has been suspended, nor is there a Dukkaṭa offense due to using things in common with a shameless person, because the characteristic of shamelessness does not apply. For one who, thinking that because sugarcane juice and greens are items allowable for seven days or for life, it is permissible to eat sugarcane at the wrong time, then eats it and does not see a Pācittiya offense arising from that act, due to his perception that 'it is permissible'; or someone who, having acknowledged incurring an offense, insists, 'I will not make amends'—this is the person referred to in the following verse.

“Sañcicca āpattiṃ āpajjati, āpattiṃ parigūhati;

Agatigamanañca gacchati, ediso vuccati alajjīpuggalo”ti. (pari. 359) –

“Knowingly he commits an offense, he conceals the offense; and he goes a wrong course—such a person is called shameless.” (Pari. 359)

Vuttalakkhaṇe apatanato alajjī nāma na hoti. Tasmā yathā pubbe yāva ukkhepanīyakammaṃ kataṃ, tāva tena saddhiṃ sambhoge saṃvāse ca anāpatti, evamidhāpīti sabbathā anāpattiṭṭhāneyeva anāpatti vuttāti veditabbaṃ[M 3.0268]. Na hi bhagavā alajjinā saddhiṃ sambhogapaccayā āpattisambhave sati “anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse”ti vadati. Tato yamettha kenaci “anāpatti sambhoge saṃvāse”ti iminā pācittiyena anāpatti vuttā, “alajjīparibhogapaccayā dukkaṭaṃ pana āpajjatiyevā”ti vatvā bahudhā papañcitaṃ, na taṃ sārato paccetabbaṃ. Sesamettha uttānameva.

Because he does not fall into the stated characteristics, he is not called shameless. Therefore, just as before, until the act of suspension is performed, there is no offense in communion and dwelling together with him; so too here, it should be understood that 'no offense' is stated in a case where there is in every way no offense. For the Blessed One would not say, 'There is no offense in communion and dwelling together,' if an offense were to arise due to communion with a shameless person. Therefore, whatever has been extensively elaborated here by some—saying that by 'no offense in communion and dwelling together' no Pācittiya offense is stated, but 'one does incur a Dukkaṭa offense due to using what belongs to a shameless person'—that should not be accepted as the essential meaning. The rest here is straightforward.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya sāratthadīpaniyaṃ

Thus, in the Sāratthadīpanī, a sub-commentary to the Vinaya commentary Samantapāsādikā.

Mahākhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Great Chapter is concluded.

2. Uposathakkhandhakaṃ

2. The Uposatha Chapter

Sannipātānujānanādikathāvaṇṇanā

Commentary on the Account of Permitting Assemblies and Other Topics

132. Uposathakkhandhake [M 3.0269][V 3.0244] taranti plavanti ettha bālāti titthaṃ. Itoti imasmiṃ sāsane laddhito. Taṃ kathentīti “imasmiṃ nāma divase muhutte vā idaṃ kattabba”ntiādinā kathenti.

132. In the Uposatha Chapter, 'tittha' (ford) is so called because 'here the foolish cross over, they float' (taranti plavanti ettha bālāti). This is so because it is obtained in this Dispensation. They declare it thus: 'On such and such a day or at such and such a time, this should be done,' and so on.

134. “Suṇātu me bhante”tiādīsu yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) vitthārato āgatamevāti na idha vitthārayissāma, atthikehi pana tatoyeva gahetabbaṃ.

134. Regarding such phrases as, "Listen to me, venerable sirs," what should be said has already been explained in detail in the Mātikā Commentary (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Nidānavaṇṇanā), so we will not elaborate on it here. But those who are interested should take it from there.

135. Āpajjitvā vā vuṭṭhitoti ettha ārocitāpi āpatti asantī nāma hotīti veditabbaṃ. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) vuttaṃ “yassa pana evaṃ anāpannā vā āpatti āpajjitvā ca pana vuṭṭhitā vā desitā vā ārocitā vā, tassa sā āpatti asantī nāma hotī”ti. Musāvādo nāma vacībhedapaccayā hotīti āha “na musāvādalakkhaṇenā”ti. Bhagavato pana vacanenāti sampajānamusāvāde kiṃ hoti? “Dukkaṭaṃ hotī”ti iminā vacanena. Vacīdvāre akiriyasamuṭṭhānā āpatti hotīti yasmā yassa bhikkhuno adhammikāya paṭiññāya tuṇhībhūtassa nisinnassa manodvāre āpatti nāma natthi, yasmā pana āvi kātabbaṃ na āvi akāsi, tenassa vacīdvāre akiriyasamuṭṭhānā āpatti hoti.

135. Regarding "or having committed and emerged," here it should be understood that even an offense that has been reported is considered nonexistent. Therefore, it is stated in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā (Kaṅkhā. Aṭṭha. Nidānavaṇṇanā): "But for one for whom an offense has not been committed, or having been committed has been emerged from, confessed, or reported, for him that offense is considered nonexistent." False speech occurs because of the condition of a verbal utterance—thus it is said, "not by the characteristic of false speech." But according to the word of the Blessed One, what is the result in the case of deliberate false speech? "It results in a dukkaṭa offense"—by this statement. An offense arises through the door of speech due to inaction. For a monk who sits remaining silent during an unlawful declaration, there is no offense arising through the mind-door. However, because he did not disclose what should have been disclosed, an offense arises for him through the door of speech due to inaction.

Vācāti [V 3.0245] vācāya, ya-kāralopenāyaṃ niddeso. Kenaci manujena vācāya anālapantoti yojetabbaṃ. Giraṃ no ca pare bhaṇeyyāti “ime sossantī”ti parapuggale sandhāya saddampi na nicchāreyya. Āpajjeyya vācasikanti vācato samuṭṭhitaṃ āpattiṃ āpajjeyya.

The word 'vācā' is explained as 'vācāya'; this is a designation by elision of the letter 'ya'. It should be construed as 'not conversing with any person by speech'. Regarding "Nor should one utter a word to others," this means that, with other persons in mind, thinking, "These will hear," one should not even emit a sound. Regarding "one would incur a verbal offense," this means one would incur an offense originating from speech.

Antarāyakaroti vippaṭisāravatthutāya pāmojjādisambhavaṃ nivāretvā paṭhamajjhānādīnaṃ adhigamāya antarāyakaro. Tassa bhikkhuno phāsu hotīti [M 3.0270] avippaṭisāramūlakānaṃ pāmojjādīnaṃ vasena tassa bhikkhuno sukhā paṭipadā sampajjatīti attho.

'It obstructs' means that, being a basis for regret, it prevents the arising of joy and so forth, and thus obstructs the attainment of the first jhāna and so on. 'It is comfortable for that monk' means that, by means of joy and so forth rooted in non-regret, that monk's practice proceeds pleasantly.

Sannipātānujānanādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The exposition of the discourse on the approval of assemblies, and so forth, is finished.

Sīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Approving Boundaries

138. Itaropīti suddhapaṃsupabbatādiṃ sandhāya vadati. Hatthippamāṇo nāma pabbato heṭṭhimakoṭiyā aḍḍhaṭṭhamaratanubbedho. Tasmāti yasmā ekena na vaṭṭati, tasmā. Dvattiṃsapalaguḷapiṇḍappamāṇatā thūlatāya gahetabbā, na tulagaṇanāya. Antosāramissakānanti antosārarukkhehi missakānaṃ. Sūcidaṇḍakappamāṇoti sīhaḷadīpe lekhanadaṇḍappamāṇoti vadanti, so ca kaniṭṭhaṅguliparimāṇoti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Etanti navamūlasākhāniggamanaṃ. Parabhāge kittetuṃ vaṭṭatīti bahi nikkhamitvā ṭhitesu aṭṭhasu maggesu ekissā disāya ekaṃ, aparāya ekanti evaṃ catūsu ṭhānesu kittetuṃ vaṭṭati.

138. 'And other' refers to mounds of pure sand and the like. A mountain the size of an elephant means its lower portion is seven and a half ratanas in height. 'Therefore' means: because one alone is not suitable, therefore. The size of a lump of jaggery of thirty-two palas should be taken by its thickness, not by weight or counting. 'Mixed with heartwood' means mixed with trees containing heartwood. 'The size of a needle's shaft' is said to be the size of a writing stick in Sri Lanka, which should be regarded as the size of the little finger. 'This' refers to the emergence of the nine roots and branches. 'It is fit to proclaim in the outer part' means, having gone outside, on the eight paths that are standing there, one in one direction, one in another—thus, it is fit to proclaim in four places.

Yattha katthaci uttarantiyā bhikkhuniyā antaravāsako temiyatīti sikkhākaraṇīyaṃ āgatalakkhaṇena timaṇḍalaṃ paṭicchādetvā antaravāsakaṃ anukkhipitvā titthena vā atitthena vā uttarantiyā bhikkhuniyā ekadvaṅgulamattampi antaravāsako temiyati. Bhikkhuniyā eva gahaṇañcettha bhikkhunīvibhaṅge bhikkhuniyā vasena nadīlakkhaṇassa pāḷiyaṃ āgatattā teneva nayena dassanatthaṃ kataṃ. Sīmaṃ bandhantānaṃ nimittaṃ hotīti ayaṃ vuttalakkhaṇā nadī samuddaṃ vā pavisatu taḷākaṃ vā, pabhavato paṭṭhāya nimittaṃ hoti. Ajjhottharitvā āvaraṇaṃ pavattatiyevāti āvaraṇaṃ ajjhottharitvā sandatiyeva. Appavattamānāti asandamānudakā. Āvaraṇañhi patvā nadiyā yattake padese udakaṃ asandamānaṃ santiṭṭhati, tattha nadīnimittaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭati. Upari sandamānaṭṭhāneyeva vaṭṭati, asandamānaṭṭhāne pana udakanimittaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Ṭhitameva hi udakanimitte vaṭṭati, na sandamānaṃ. Tenevāha “pavattanaṭṭhāne nadīnimittaṃ, appavattanaṭṭhāne udakanimittaṃ [V 3.0246] kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Nadiṃ bhinditvāti mātikāmukhadvārena nadīkūlaṃ bhinditvā. Ukkhepimanti kūpato viya ukkhipitvā gahetabbaṃ.

The characteristic of a river is that wherever a nun crosses, her under-robe gets wet. This means that for a nun crossing at a ford or not at a ford, having covered the three circles according to the prescribed characteristic and without hitching up her under-robe, even one or two finger-breadths of her under-robe gets wet. The mention of a nun here is made in order to explain it by that same method, because in the Bhikkhunīvibhaṅga the characteristic of a river is given in the Pāli in relation to a nun. For those binding a boundary, it becomes a marker. This river with the stated characteristic, whether it enters the sea or a lake, is a marker from its source. 'Having overcome a barrier, it still flows' means having overcome a barrier, it indeed flows. 'Not flowing' means non-flowing water. For wherever the water, having reached a barrier in the river, stands without flowing, it is not suitable to make a river-marker there. It is only suitable in a place where it flows above. But in a place where it does not flow, it is suitable to make a water-marker. For in the case of a water-marker, only still water is suitable, not flowing water. Therefore, it is said: "In a place of flowing, a river-marker is suitable; in a place of non-flowing, a water-marker is suitable." 'Having broken the river' means having broken the riverbank by means of the opening of a water-channel. 'To be drawn up' means it should be taken by drawing it up as from a well.

Siṅghāṭakasaṇṭhānāti [M 3.0271] tikoṇaracchāsaṇṭhānā. Mudiṅgasaṇṭhānāti mudiṅgabherī viya majjhe vitthatā ubhosu koṭīsu saṅkoṭitā hoti. Upacāraṃ ṭhapetvāti pacchā sīmaṃ bandhantānaṃ sīmāya okāsaṃ ṭhapetvā. Antonimittagatehi panāti ekassa gāmassa upaḍḍhaṃ anto kattukāmatāya sati sabbesaṃ āgamane payojanaṃ natthīti katvā vuttaṃ. Āgantabbanti ca sāmīcivasena vuttaṃ, nāyaṃ niyamo “āgantabbamevā”ti. Tenevāha “āgamanampi anāgamanampi vaṭṭatī”ti. Abaddhāya hi sīmāya nānāgāmakhettānaṃ nānāsīmasabhāvattā tesaṃ anāgamanepi vaggakammaṃ na hoti, tasmā anāgamanampi vaṭṭati. Baddhāya pana sīmāya ekasīmabhāvato puna aññasmiṃ kamme kariyamāne anto sīmagatehi āgantabbamevāti āha “avippavāsasīmā…pe… āgantabba”nti. Nimittakittanakāle asodhitāyapi sīmāya nevatthi doso nimittakittanassa apalokanādīsu aññatarābhāvato.

'Having the shape of a siṅghāṭaka' means having the shape of a triangular road junction. 'Having the shape of a mudiṅga' is like a mudiṅga drum, broad in the middle and tapering at both ends. 'Having set aside the approach' means leaving space for the boundary for those establishing the boundary later. 'But by those within the boundary markers' refers to when there is a desire to include half of a village within, there is no purpose for everyone to come, hence it is said. 'And they should come' is said as a matter of propriety; there is no strict rule that 'they must come.' Therefore, it is said, 'both coming and not coming are permissible.' For an unbound boundary, since the fields of different villages have the nature of separate boundaries, even if they do not come, the formal act is not incomplete; thus, not coming is also permissible. But for a bound boundary, because it is a single boundary, when another formal act is being performed, those within the boundary must come—hence it is said, 'for a boundary of common residence... they should come.' At the time of proclaiming the markers, even if the boundary has not been purified, there is no fault in the proclamation of the markers, because it is not one of the formal acts like 'apalokana' and so forth.

Bhaṇḍukammāpucchanaṃ sandhāya pabbajjā-gahaṇaṃ. Sukhakaraṇatthanti sabbesaṃ sannipātanaparissamaṃ pahāya appatarehi sukhakaraṇatthaṃ. Ekavīsati bhikkhū gaṇhātīti vīsativaggakaraṇīyaparamattā saṅghakammassa kammārahena saddhiṃ ekavīsati bhikkhū gaṇhāti. Idañca nisinnānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ. Heṭṭhimantato hi yattha ekavīsati bhikkhū nisīdituṃ sakkonti, tattake padese sīmaṃ bandhituṃ vaṭṭati. Na sakkhissantīti avippavāsasīmāya baddhabhāvaṃ asallakkhetvā “samānasaṃvāsakameva samūhanissāmā”ti vāyamantā na sakkhissanti. Baddhāya hi avippavāsasīmāya taṃ asamūhanitvā “samānasaṃvāsakasīmaṃ samūhanissāmā”ti katāyapi kammavācāya asamūhatāva hoti sīmā. Paṭhamañhi avippavāsaṃ samūhanitvā pacchā sīmā samūhanitabbā. Ekaratanappamāṇā suviññeyyatarā hotīti katvā vuttaṃ “ekaratanappamāṇā vaṭṭatī”ti. Ekaṅgulamattāpi sīmantarikā vaṭṭatiyeva. Tattakenapi hi sīmā asambhinnāva hoti.

'For the purpose of ease' means for the purpose of making it easy with fewer people, abandoning the effort of gathering all. 'He takes twenty-one monks' means that, because the maximum for a Sangha act to be done is a group of twenty, he takes twenty-one monks, including one who is competent for the act. And this is said with regard to those seated. For at a minimum, wherever twenty-one monks can sit, it is permissible to establish a boundary in that area. 'They will not be able to'—not having taken into account that the boundary of common residence is established, those striving, thinking, 'We will abolish only the boundary of co-residence,' will not succeed. For if a boundary of common residence is already established, without having abolished it, even if a formal act is performed declaring, 'We will abolish the boundary of co-residence,' the boundary remains unabolished. First, the boundary of common residence must be abolished, and only afterward can the other boundary be abolished. 'It is more easily recognizable if it is the size of one ratana'—for this reason it is said, 'a size of one ratana is suitable.' Even a boundary-interval of just a finger's width is suitable. For even with that much, the boundary remains unmixed.

Avasesanimittānīti mahāsīmāya bāhirapasse nimittāni. Khaṇḍasīmato paṭṭhāya bandhanaṃ āciṇṇaṃ, āciṇṇakaraṇeneva ca sammoho na hotīti āha “khaṇḍasīmatova paṭṭhāya bandhitabbā”ti. Kuṭigeheti kuṭighare, bhūmighareti attho. Udukkhalanti khuddakāvāṭaṃ. Nimittaṃ na kātabbanti taṃ rājiṃ vā udukkhalaṃ vā nimittaṃ na kātabbaṃ.

'The remaining markers' means the markers on the outer side of the great boundary. Binding starting from a broken boundary is the customary practice, and because of doing what is customary there is no confusion. Thus it is said: "It should be bound starting from the broken boundary." 'In a kuṭigeha' means in a hut, that is, a house on the ground. 'Udukkhala' means a small pit. 'A marker should not be made' means that that line or pit should not be made into a marker.

Heṭṭhā [M 3.0272][V 3.0247] na otaratīti bhittito oraṃ nimittāni ṭhapetvā kittitattā heṭṭhā ākāsappadesaṃ na otarati. Heṭṭhāpi otaratīti sace heṭṭhā antobhittiyaṃ ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāso hoti, otarati. Otaramānā ca uparisīmappamāṇena na otarati, samantā bhittippamāṇena otarati. Otaraṇānotaraṇaṃ vuttanayeneva veditabbanti sace heṭṭhā ekavīsatiyā bhikkhūnaṃ okāso hoti, otarati. No ce, na otaratīti adhippāyo. Sabbo pāsādo sīmaṭṭho hotīti uparimatalena saddhiṃ ekābaddhabhittiko vā hotu mā vā, sabbopi pāsādo sīmaṭṭhova hoti.

It does not descend below: because the boundaries have been declared by placing markers inward from the wall, it does not descend into the space below. It does descend below: if below, inside the wall, there is space for twenty-one monks, it descends. And while descending, it does not descend according to the measure of the upper boundary; it descends according to the measure of the wall all around. The descending and non-descending should be understood in the stated manner: if below there is space for twenty-one monks, it descends; if not, it does not—this is the meaning. The entire building is within the boundary: whether it has a single connecting wall with the upper floor or not, the entire building is indeed within the boundary.

Tālamūlakapabbateti tālamūlasadise pabbate. So ca heṭṭhā mahanto hutvā anupubbena tanuko hotīti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Paṇavasaṇṭhāno majjhe tanuko hoti mūle agge ca vitthato. Heṭṭhā vā majjhe vāti mudiṅgasaṇṭhānassa heṭṭhā paṇavasaṇṭhānassa majjhe. Ākāsapabbhāranti bhittiyā aparikkhittapabbhāraṃ. Antoleṇaṃ hotīti pabbatassa anto leṇaṃ hoti. Sīmāmāḷaketi khaṇḍasīmāmāḷake. Mahāsīmaṃ sodhetvā vā kammaṃ kātabbanti mahāsīmagatā bhikkhū hatthapāsaṃ vā ānetabbā, sīmato vā bahi kātabbāti adhippāyo. Gaṇṭhipadesu pana “mahāsīmagatehi bhikkhūhi taṃ sākhaṃ vā pārohaṃ vā anāmasitvā ṭhātabbanti adhippāyo”ti vuttaṃ, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ. Purimanayepīti khaṇḍasīmāya uṭṭhahitvā mahāsīmāya oṇatarukkhepi. Ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti khaṇḍasīmāya anto ṭhitattā rukkhassa tattha ṭhito hatthapāsaṃyeva ānetabboti ukkhipāpetvā kātuṃ na vaṭṭati.

Tālamūlakapabbata: a mountain resembling the base of a palm tree. And it should be understood that it is large at the bottom and gradually becomes slender. Shaped like a paṇava-drum, it is narrow in the middle and broad at the base and top. Either at the bottom or in the middle: for a mudiṅga-shaped one, at the bottom; for a paṇava-shaped one, in the middle. Ākāsapabbhāra: an overhang not enclosed by a wall. Antoleṇaṃ: there is a cave inside the mountain. Sīmāmāḷake: on a platform for a partial boundary. Or the formal act should be performed after purifying the great boundary: the meaning is that the monks who have gone into the great boundary should be brought within arm's reach, or they should be made to go outside the boundary. But in the Ganthipadas it is said: 'The meaning is that monks who have gone into the great boundary should stand without touching that branch or shoot,' but that should not be accepted. As in the previous method: also in the case of a tree that has grown up in a partial boundary and bent down into the great boundary. It is not permissible to perform the act after having it lifted: because the tree stands within the partial boundary, one standing there should only be brought within arm's reach; therefore, it is not permissible to perform the act by having it lifted.

140. Pārayatīti ajjhottharati. Pārāti sīmāpekkho itthiliṅganiddeso. Assāti bhaveyya. Idhādhippetanāvāya pamāṇaṃ dassento āha “yā sabbantimena paricchedena…pe… tayo jane vahatī”ti. Iminā ca vuttappamāṇato khuddakā nāvā vijjamānāpi idha asantapakkhaṃ bhajatīti dīpeti. Avassaṃ labbhaneyyā dhuvanāvāva hotīti sambandho. Rukkhaṃ chinditvā katoti pāṭhaseso. Paratīre sammukhaṭṭhāneti orimatīre sabbapariyantanimittassa sammukhaṭṭhāne. Sabbanimittānaṃ anto ṭhite bhikkhū hatthapāsagate katvāti ettha sace ekaṃ gāmakhettaṃ hoti, ubhosu tīresu sabbanimittānaṃ anto ṭhite bhikkhū hatthapāsagate katvā [M 3.0273] sammannitabbā. Nānāgāmakkhettaṃ ce, samānasaṃvāsakasīmābandhanakāle anāgantumpi vaṭṭati. Avippavāsasīmāsammutiyaṃ pana āgantabbameva. Yasmā ubhosu tīresu nimittakittanamattena dīpako saṅgahito nāma na hoti, tasmā dīpakepi nimittāni visuṃ kittetabbānevāti āha “dīpakassa [V 3.0248] orimante ca pārimante ca nimittaṃ kittetabba”nti. Dīpakasikharanti dīpakamatthakaṃ. Pabbatasaṇṭhānāti dīpakassa ekato adhikatarattā vuttaṃ.

140. Pārayati means it covers over. Pārā is a feminine gender designation with reference to the boundary. Assa means 'it would be'. Here, showing the measure of the intended boat, he says: 'that which by its utmost limit... carries three people.' And by this, he indicates that even though smaller boats than the stated measure exist, here they fall into the category of non-existent. The connection is: 'it must be a permanent boat that is necessarily obtainable'. 'Made after cutting down a tree' is the remainder of the text. At a place on the opposite shore: at a place facing the very last marker on this shore. Regarding 'having made the monks standing within all the markers to be within arm's reach': here, if it is one village-territory, the boundary should be designated after having made the monks standing within all the markers on both shores to be within arm's reach. If it is different village-territories, at the time of binding a boundary for common residence, it is permissible even not to come. But for the designation of a non-separation boundary, one must indeed come. Because an island is not included merely by the declaration of markers on both shores, therefore he said that markers must be declared separately on the island too: 'A marker should be declared on the near side and the far side of the island.' Dīpakasikharaṃ: the top of the island. Shaped like a mountain: this is said because the island is higher on one side.

Sīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Authorization of Boundaries is concluded.

Uposathāgārādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Uposatha Hall and so forth.

142. Vatthuvasena vuttanti “mayañcamhā asammatāya bhūmiyā nisinnā pātimokkhaṃ assumhā”ti vatthumhi pātimokkhasavanassa āgatattā vuttaṃ. Uposathappamukhaṃ nāma uposathāgārassa sammukhaṭṭhānaṃ. Pāḷiyaṃ “paṭhamaṃ nimittā kittetabbā”ti ettakameva vatvā sīmāsammutiyaṃ viya “pabbatanimittaṃ pāsāṇanimitta”ntiādinā visesetvā nimittānaṃ adassitattā “khuddakāni vā…pe… yāni kānici nimittānī”ti vuttaṃ. Kittetuṃ vaṭṭatīti iminā sambandho.

142. It is stated by way of the story: it is stated because the hearing of the Pātimokkha is mentioned in the story, 'We, sitting on unconsecrated ground, heard the Pātimokkha.' Uposathappamukhaṃ is the name for the place in front of the Uposatha hall. In the Pāli text, since only this much was said—'First, the markers should be declared'—and the markers were not shown in detail by specifying 'a mountain as a marker, a stone as a marker,' and so on, as in the designation of a boundary, it is therefore said: 'small ones... or whatever markers there may be.' The connection is with 'it is permissible to declare'.

Avippavāsasīmānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Authorization of the Non-Separation Boundary.

144. Assāti bhikkhunisaṅghassa. Dvepi sīmāyoti paṭhamaṃ vuttā avippavāsasīmā samānasaṃvāsakasīmā ca. Na kammavācaṃ vaggaṃ karontīti kammavācaṃ na bhindanti, kammaṃ na kopentīti adhippāyo. Etthāti “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”ti ettha. Gāmañca gāmūpacārañca na ottharatīti “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañcā”ti vuttattā. Sīmāsaṅkhyameva gacchatīti avippavāsasīmāsaṅkhaṃ gacchati. Ekampi kulaṃ paviṭṭhaṃ vāti abhinavakatagehesu sabbapaṭhamaṃ ekampi kulaṃ paviṭṭhaṃ atthi. Agataṃ vāti porāṇakagāme aññesu gehāni chaḍḍetvā gatesu ekampi kulaṃ agataṃ atthi.

144. 'Assa' means 'of the Bhikkhunī Saṅgha'. Both boundaries: the non-separation boundary and the common-residence boundary mentioned first. 'They do not make the formal act incomplete' means they do not break the formal act, they do not spoil the formal act; this is the meaning. 'Here' refers to 'except for the village and its vicinity.' It does not cover the village and its vicinity, because it was stated 'except for the village and its vicinity.' 'It goes only to the count of a boundary' means it is counted as a non-separation boundary. 'Or even one family has entered' means: in newly built houses, there is even one family that has entered first of all. 'Or has not gone' means: in an old village, when others have abandoned their houses and gone, there is even one family that has not gone.

Avippavāsasīmā na samūhantabbāti mahāsīmaṃ sandhāya vadati. Nirāsaṅkaṭṭhānesu ṭhatvāti cetiyaṅgaṇādīnaṃ khaṇḍasīmāya anokāsattā vuttaṃ. Khaṇḍasīmañhi bandhantā tādisaṃ ṭhānaṃ pahāya aññasmiṃ vivitte okāse bandhanti[M 3.0274]. Appeva nāma samūhanituṃ sakkhissantīti avippavāsasīmaṃyeva samūhanituṃ sakkhissanti, na khaṇḍasīmaṃ. Paṭibandhituṃ pana na sakkhissantevāti khaṇḍasīmāya aññātattā na sakkhissanti. Na samūhanitabbāti khaṇḍasīmaṃ ajānantehi [V 3.0249] na samūhanitabbā. Uposathassa visuṃ gahitattā avasesakammavasena samānasaṃvāsatā veditabbā.

'A non-separation boundary should not be abolished': he says this with reference to a great boundary. 'Standing in places free from doubt': this is said because there is no space for a partial boundary in places such as shrine courtyards. For when binding a partial boundary, they abandon such a place and bind it in another secluded space. 'Perhaps they will be able to abolish it' means they will be able to abolish only the non-separation boundary, not the partial boundary. 'But they will certainly not be able to obstruct it' means they will not be able because of not knowing the partial boundary. 'It should not be abolished' means it should not be abolished by those who do not know the partial boundary. Since the Uposatha is taken separately, common residence should be understood by way of the remaining formal acts.

Gāmasīmādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Village Boundary and so forth.

147. Aparicchinnāyāti baddhasīmāvasena akataparicchedāya. Yena kenaci khaṇitvā akatoti antamaso tiracchānenapi khaṇitvā akato. Tassa antohatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhito kammaṃ kopetīti iminā bahiparicchedato yattha katthaci ṭhito kammaṃ na kopetīti dīpeti. Yaṃ pana vuttaṃ mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) “paricchedabbhantare hatthapāsaṃ vijahitvā ṭhitopi paricchedato bahi aññaṃ tattakaṃyeva paricchedaṃ anatikkamitvā ṭhitopi kammaṃ kopeti, idaṃ sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu sanniṭṭhāna”nti, tattha “aññaṃ tattakaṃyeva paricchedaṃ anatikkamitvā ṭhitopi kammaṃ kopetī”ti idaṃ neva pāḷiyaṃ, na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ upalabbhati. Yadi cetaṃ dvinnaṃ saṅghānaṃ visuṃ uposathādikammakaraṇādhikāre vuttattā udakukkhepato bahi aññaṃ udakukkhepaṃ anatikkamitvā uposathādikaraṇatthaṃ ṭhito saṅgho sīmāsambhedasambhavato kammaṃ kopetīti iminā adhippāyena vuttaṃ siyā, evaṃ sati yujjeyya. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāya līnatthappakāsaniyaṃ vuttaṃ “aññaṃ tattakaṃyeva paricchedanti dutiyaṃ udakukkhepaṃ anatikkantopi kopeti. Kasmā? Attano udakukkhepasīmāya paresaṃ udakukkhepasīmāya ajjhotthaṭattā sīmāsambhedo hoti, tasmā kopetī”ti. “Idaṃ sabbaaṭṭhakathāsu sanniṭṭhāna”nti ca iminā adhippāyena vuttanti gahetabbaṃ sabbāsupi aṭṭhakathāsu sīmāsambhedassa anicchitattā. Teneva hi “attano ca aññesañca udakukkhepaparicchedassa antarā añño udakukkhepo sīmantarikatthāya ṭhapetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Aññe panettha aññathāpi papañcenti, taṃ na gahetabbaṃ.

147. 'Aparicchinnāya' means not delimited by means of a fixed boundary. 'Yena kenaci khaṇitvā akato' means not having been dug by anyone, even by an animal. The statement 'standing having left a hand's reach within it, one invalidates the act' indicates that by standing anywhere outside the boundary, the act is not invalidated. However, regarding what is stated in the Mātikāṭṭhakathā (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī, Aṭṭhakathā, Nidānavanṇanā)—'Even if one stands having left a hand's reach within the boundary, if one does not cross another boundary of the same extent outside the boundary, the act is still invalidated. This is the settled conclusion in all commentaries'—of this, the part 'if one does not cross another boundary of the same extent outside the boundary, the act is still invalidated' is found in neither the Pāli Canon nor the commentaries. If this were stated with the intention that, in the context of two Saṅghas performing separate Uposatha and other acts, a Saṅgha standing outside a water-boundary, without crossing another water-boundary, for the purpose of performing Uposatha and other acts, invalidates the act due to the possibility of boundary mingling, then it would be consistent. Therefore, in the Līnatthappakāsanī of the Mātikāṭṭhakathā, it is stated: '“Not crossing another boundary of the same extent” means that even if one does not cross a second water-boundary, one invalidates the act. Why? Because by one's own water-boundary overlapping another's water-boundary, there is mingling of boundaries; therefore, one invalidates the act.' And the statement, 'This is the settled conclusion in all commentaries,' should be understood with this intention, since mingling of boundaries is undesired in all commentaries. Therefore, it is said: 'Another water-boundary should be established between one's own and others' water-boundary division, for the purpose of a boundary interval.' Others, however, elaborate differently on this point, but that should not be accepted.

Sabbattha saṅgho nisīdatīti hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā nisīdati. Udakukkhepasīmākammaṃ natthīti yasmā sabbopi nadīpadeso bhikkhūhi ajjhotthaṭo[M 3.0275], tasmā samantato nadiyā abhāvā udakukkhepe payojanaṃ natthi. Udakukkhepappamāṇā sīmantarikā suviññeyyatarā hoti, sīmāsambhedasaṅkā na ca siyāti sāmīcidassanatthaṃ “añño udakukkhepo sīmantarikatthāya ṭhapetabbo”ti vuttaṃ. Yattakena pana sīmāsambhedo na hoti, tattakaṃ ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatiyeva. Tenevāhu porāṇā “yattakena sīmāsaṅkaro na hoti, tattakampi ṭhapetuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti. Ūnakaṃ pana na vaṭṭatīti idampi udakukkhepasīmāya parisavasena vaḍḍhanato sīmāsambhedasaṅkā siyāti taṃnivāraṇatthameva vuttaṃ.

'The Saṅgha sits everywhere' means it sits without abandoning a hand's reach. 'There is no act of establishing a water-boundary' means that since the entire river area is occupied by the bhikkhus, there is no river on all sides, and thus there is no purpose in a water-boundary. A boundary interval of the measure of a water-boundary is more easily discernible, and there would be no apprehension of boundary mingling; to show what is proper, it is said, 'Another water-boundary should be established for the purpose of a boundary interval.' However, it is certainly fitting to establish an interval of such an extent that boundary mingling does not occur. Therefore, the ancients said, 'It is fitting to establish even such an extent that boundary confusion does not occur.' But it is not fitting to establish less than that; this too was said for the very purpose of preventing the apprehension of boundary mingling, since there might be apprehension of boundary mingling from the expansion of the water-boundary by means of the assembly.

Gacchantiyā [V 3.0250] pana nāvāya kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti ettha udakukkhepamanatikkamitvā parivattamānāya kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti veditabbaṃ. Sīmaṃ vā sodhetvāti ettha sīmasodhanaṃ nāma gāmasīmādīsu ṭhitānaṃ hatthapāsānayanādi. “Nadiṃ vināsetvā taḷākaṃ karontī”ti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāveti “heṭṭhā pāḷi baddhā”ti, heṭṭhānadiṃ āvaritvā pāḷi baddhāti attho. Chaḍḍitamodakanti taḷākarakkhaṇatthaṃ ekamantena chaḍḍitamudakaṃ. Deve avassanteti dubbuṭṭhikāle vassānepi deve avassante. Uppatitvāti uttaritvā. Gāmanigamasīmaṃ ottharitvā pavattatīti vuttappakāre vassakāle cattāro māse abbocchinnā pavattati. Vihārasīmanti baddhasīmaṃ sandhāya vadati.

'When a boat is moving, it is not permissible to do it': here it should be understood that it is permissible to do it when the boat is turning around without exceeding the water-boundary. 'Or having cleared the boundary': here, clearing the boundary refers to bringing within hand's reach those standing in village boundaries, and so forth. 'Having destroyed a river, they make a pond' clarifies the meaning stated there as 'a dam is built below,' meaning a dam is built obstructing the lower river. 'Discarded water' means water discarded to one side for the purpose of protecting the pond. 'When the gods do not send rain' means when the gods do not send rain during a time of drought, even in the rainy season. 'Having risen' means having ascended. 'Having inundated the village or town boundary, it flows' means that in the manner described, it flows continuously for the four months of the rainy season. 'Monastery boundary' is said with reference to a fixed boundary.

Agamanapatheti yattha tadaheva gantvā paccāgantuṃ na sakkā hoti, tādise padese araññasīmāsaṅkhameva gacchatīti sattabbhantarasīmaṃ sandhāya vadati. Tesanti macchabandhānaṃ. Gamanapariyantassa oratoti gamanapariyantassa orimabhāge dīpakaṃ pabbatañca sandhāya vuttaṃ, na samuddappadesaṃ.

'In a path of no return' means that in such a place where one cannot go and return on the same day, it attains the designation of a forest boundary; this is said with reference to a boundary of seven abbhantaras. 'Tesaṃ' means 'of the fishermen.' 'On the near side of the limit of travel' is said with reference to the island and the mountain on the near side of the limit of travel, not the region of the sea.

148. Saṃsaṭṭhaviṭapāti iminā aññamaññassa āsannataṃ dīpeti. Baddhā hotīti pacchimadisābhāge sīmaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Tassā padesanti yattha ṭhatvā bhikkhūhi kammaṃ kātuṃ sakkā hoti, tādisaṃ padesaṃ. Yattha pana ṭhitehi kammaṃ kātuṃ na sakkā hoti, tādisaṃ padesaṃ antokaritvā bandhantā sīmāya sīmaṃ sambhindanti nāma. Dvinnaṃ sīmānaṃ nimittaṃ hotīti nimittassa sīmato bāhirattā sīmāsambhedo na hotīti vuttaṃ. Sīmāsaṅkaraṃ karotīti vaḍḍhitvā sīmappadesaṃ paviṭṭhe dvinnaṃ sīmānaṃ gataṭṭhānassa duviññeyyattā vuttaṃ, na pana tattha kammaṃ kātuṃ na vaṭṭatīti dassanatthaṃ. Na hi sīmā tattakena [M 3.0276] asīmā hoti, dve pana sīmā pacchā vaḍḍhitena rukkhena ajjhotthaṭattā ekābaddhā honti, tasmā ekattha ṭhatvā kammaṃ karontehi itaraṃ sodhetvā kātabbaṃ.

148. 'With branches intermingled' indicates their proximity to each other. The phrase 'is bound' is stated with reference to the boundary in the western direction. By 'its area' is meant such a place where bhikkhus can stand and perform an act. But if, when establishing a boundary, they include a place where they cannot stand to perform an act, they are said to mingle boundary with boundary. The phrase 'it is a marker for two boundaries' is stated because, since the marker is outside the boundary, there is no boundary mingling. The phrase 'it causes boundary confusion' is stated because, when a tree has grown and entered the boundary area, the respective locations of the two boundaries become difficult to discern; it is not, however, stated to illustrate that performing an act there is not permissible. For the boundary does not become a non-boundary just by that much, but because the two boundaries are later overgrown by the grown tree, they become bound as one. Therefore, those performing an act in one place should clear the other before proceeding.

Gāmasīmādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the section on village boundaries and so on is finished.

Uposathabhedādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section on the Divisions of the Uposatha and so on

149. Adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammanti ettha yattha cattāro vasanti, tattha pātimokkhuddeso anuññāto. Yattha dve vā tayo vā vasanti, tattha pārisuddhiuposatho. Idha pana [V 3.0251] tathā akatvā catunnaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne pārisuddhiuposathassa katattā tiṇṇaṃ vasanaṭṭhāne ca pātimokkhassa uddiṭṭhattā “adhammenā”ti vuttaṃ. Yasmā sabbeva na sannipatiṃsu, chandapārisuddhi ca saṅghamajjhaṃyeva āgacchati, na gaṇamajjhaṃ, tasmā “vagga”nti vuttaṃ.

149. Here, concerning 'an Uposatha act that is unlawful and factional': where four bhikkhus reside, the recitation of the Pātimokkha is permitted. Where two or three reside, a purity Uposatha is performed. But here, because they did not do so, performing the purity Uposatha in a place where four reside, and reciting the Pātimokkha in a place where three reside, it is therefore called 'unlawful.' Because they did not all assemble, and the declaration of consent and purity comes only to the midst of the Saṅgha, not to the midst of a group, it is therefore called 'factional.'

Pātimokkhuddesakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section on the Recitation of the Pātimokkha

150. Evametaṃ dhārayāmīti “sutā kho panāyasmantehī”ti ettha “evametaṃ dhārayāmī”ti vatvā “uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidānaṃ, sutā kho panāyasmantehi cattāro pārājikā dhammā”ti vattabbaṃ. Teneva mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) “tatthāyasmante pucchāmi kaccittha parisuddhā, dutiyampi pucchāmi…pe… tasmā tuṇhī, evametaṃ dhārayāmīti vatvā ‘uddiṭṭhaṃ kho āyasmanto nidāna’ntiādinā nayena avasese sutena sāvite uddiṭṭho hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Sutenāti sutapadena. Savarabhayanti vanacarakabhayaṃ. Tenāha “aṭavimanussabhaya”nti. “Avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabba”nti vacanato nidānuddese aniṭṭhite sutena sāvetabbaṃ nāma natthīti āha “dutiyādīsu uddesesū”ti. Uddiṭṭhauddesāpekkhañhi avasesaggahaṇaṃ, tasmā nidāne uddiṭṭhe pārājikuddesādīsu yasmiṃ vippakate antarāyo uppajjati, tena saddhiṃ avasesaṃ sutena sāvetabbaṃ.

150. Here, regarding 'Have you, venerable sirs, heard?', having said, 'Thus I will remember this,' it should be stated: 'Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited. Have the four pārājika rules been heard by you, venerable sirs?' For that reason, in the commentary on the Mātikā (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Nidānavanṇanā), it is said: 'Therein I ask you, venerable sirs: are you pure in this? A second time I ask… Therefore you are silent. Thus I will remember this.' Having said this, the remainder is recited, having been announced by the word 'heard,' according to the method beginning with, 'Venerable sirs, the introduction has been recited.' 'By what is heard' means by the word 'heard.' `Savarabhaya` means the fear of forest-dwellers. Therefore, he said, 'fear of forest people.' Because of the statement, 'The remainder should be announced by the word "heard",' he said that when the recitation of the introduction is not finished, there is nothing to be announced by the word 'heard'; hence, 'in the second and subsequent recitations.' For the taking up of the remainder is dependent on the recitation that has been recited. Therefore, when the introduction has been recited, in the recitation of the pārājikas and so on, if an obstacle arises regarding that which is unfinished, the remainder should be announced by the word 'heard' along with that.

Tīhipi [M 3.0277] vidhīhīti osāraṇakathanasarabhaññehi. Ettha ca atthaṃ bhaṇitukāmatāya suttassa osāraṇā osāraṇaṃ nāma. Tasseva atthappakāsanā kathanaṃ nāma. Suttassa tadatthassa vā sarena bhaṇanaṃ sarabhaññaṃ nāma. Sajjhāyaṃ adhiṭṭhahitvāti “sajjhāyaṃ karomī”ti cittaṃ uppādetvā. Osāretvā pana kathentenāti paṭhamaṃ ussāretvā pacchā atthaṃ kathentena. Manussānaṃ pana “bhaṇāhī”ti vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti ettha uccatare nisinnenapi manussānaṃ bhaṇāhīti visesetvāyeva vattuṃ vaṭṭati, avisesetvā pana na vaṭṭati. Sajjhāyaṃ karontenāti yattha katthaci nisīditvā sajjhāyaṃ karontena. Theroti yo koci attanā vuḍḍhataro. Ekaṃ āpucchitvāti ekaṃ vuḍḍhataraṃ āpucchitvā. Aparo āgacchatīti aparo tatopi vuḍḍhataro āgacchati.

'By three methods' means by formal recitation, explanation, and chanting. Here, the formal recitation of the sutta with the intention of speaking its meaning is called 'formal recitation.' The exposition of that meaning is called 'explanation.' The vocal recitation of the sutta or its meaning is called 'chanting.' 'Having resolved to recite' means generating the thought, 'I will do recitation.' 'But by one who explains after reciting' means by one who first recites aloud and then explains the meaning. Here, concerning the statement 'it is proper to say "Speak!" to humans,' even one seated higher should say 'Speak!' specifically to humans; it is not proper to say it without specifying. 'While reciting' means by one sitting anywhere and doing recitation. 'An elder' refers to anyone older than oneself. 'Having asked one' means having asked one who is older. 'Another arrives' means another, even older, arrives.

Pātimokkhuddesakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Pātimokkha Recitation is concluded.

Pātimokkhuddesakaajjhesanādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Pātimokkha Reciter, the Request, and so forth.

155. Codanāvatthu [V 3.0252] nāma ekaṃ nagaraṃ. Saṅghauposathādibhedena navavidhanti saṅghe uposatho gaṇe uposatho puggale uposathoti evaṃ kārakavasena tayo, suttuddeso pārisuddhiuposatho adhiṭṭhānuposathoti evaṃ kattabbākāravasena tayo, cātuddasiko pannarasiko sāmaggīuposathoti evaṃ divasavasena tayoti navavidhaṃ. Catubbidhaṃ uposathakammanti adhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, adhammena samaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, dhammena vaggaṃ uposathakammaṃ, dhammena samaggaṃ uposathakammanti evaṃ catubbidhampi uposathakammaṃ. Duvidhaṃ pātimokkhanti bhikkhupātimokkhaṃ bhikkhunīpātimokkhanti duvidhaṃ pātimokkhaṃ. Navavidhaṃ pātimokkhuddesanti bhikkhūnaṃ pañca uddesā, bhikkhunīnaṃ ṭhapetvā aniyatuddesaṃ avasesā cattāroti navavidhaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ.

155. Codanāvatthu is the name of a city. The Uposatha is of nine kinds: Uposatha of the Saṅgha, Uposatha of a group, and Uposatha of an individual—thus three kinds based on the agent; recitation of the Sutta, purity Uposatha, and determination Uposatha—thus three kinds based on the manner of performance; fourteenth-day Uposatha, fifteenth-day Uposatha, and concord Uposatha—thus three kinds based on the day, making nine kinds in total. The Uposatha ceremony is of four kinds: an unlawful Uposatha ceremony with a divided assembly, an unlawful Uposatha ceremony with a united assembly, a lawful Uposatha ceremony with a divided assembly, and a lawful Uposatha ceremony with a united assembly—thus the Uposatha ceremony is of four kinds. The Pātimokkha is of two kinds: the Bhikkhu Pātimokkha and the Bhikkhunī Pātimokkha—thus the Pātimokkha is of two kinds. The recitation of the Pātimokkha is of nine kinds: five recitations for the bhikkhus, and for the bhikkhunīs, excluding the Aniyata recitation, the remaining four—thus the recitation of the Pātimokkha is of nine kinds.

Pakkhagaṇanādiuggahaṇānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Permission to Learn the Counting of Fortnights, and so forth.

158-161. Samannāharathāti sallakkhetha. Pariyesitabbānīti bhikkhācārena pariyesitabbāni.

158-161. 'You should consider' means you should discern. 'What should be sought' means what should be sought through the alms round.

Disaṃgamikādivatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Topic of Traveling to a Region, and so forth.

163. Utuvasseyevāti [M 3.0278] hemantagimhesuyeva.

163. 'In the season itself' means only in winter and summer.

Pārisuddhidānakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Giving of Purity.

164. Yena kenaci aṅgapaccaṅgena viññāpetīti manasā cintetvā hatthappayogādinā yena kenaci viññāpeti. Saṅgho nappahotīti dvinnaṃ dvinnaṃ antarā hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā paṭipāṭiyā ṭhātuṃ nappahoti. Itarā pana biḷālasaṅkhalikapārisuddhi nāmāti ettha keci vadanti “biḷālasaṅkhalikā baddhāva hoti antogehe eva sampayojanattā, yathā sā na katthaci gacchati, tathā sāpi na gacchatīti adhippāyo. Itarathā visesanaṃ niratthakaṃ hotī”ti. Apare pana “yathā bahūhi manussehi ekassa biḷālassa attano attano saṅkhalikā gīvāya ābaddhā biḷāle gacchante gacchanti ābaddhattā, na aññasmiṃ biḷāle gacchante gacchanti anābaddhattā, evamevassa bhikkhussa bahūhi saṅkhalikasadisā chandapārisuddhi dinnā, sā tasmiṃ bhikkhusmiṃ gacchante [V 3.0253] gacchati tasmiṃ saṅkhalikā viya ābaddhattā, na aññasmiṃ anābaddhattā”ti vadanti. Sabbampetaṃ na sārato paccetabbaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha sāro – yathā saṅkhalikāya paṭhamavalayaṃ dutiyaṃyeva valayaṃ pāpuṇāti, na tatiyaṃ, evamayampi pārisuddhidāyakena yassa dinnā, tato aññattha na gacchatīti saṅkhalikasadisattā “biḷālasaṅkhalikā”ti vuttā. Biḷālasaṅkhalikagahaṇañcettha yāsaṃ kāsañci saṅkhalikānaṃ upalakkhaṇamattanti daṭṭhabbaṃ.

164. 'To make known by any limb or minor limb' means to communicate by any means, such as through hand gestures, after having intended with the mind. 'The Saṅgha is unable' means that the Saṅgha cannot stand in order without leaving a hand's span between every two monks. 'The other is called the purity of the cat's chain.' Here, some say: 'A cat's chain is always bound within the house itself due to its being secured; just as the cat does not go anywhere else, so too this purity does not go elsewhere—that is the meaning. Otherwise, the qualification would be meaningless.' Others say: 'Just as when many people each tie their own chain around a single cat's neck, the chains go wherever the cat goes because they are tied to it, but they do not go where another cat moves because they are not tied to it—in the same way, many consent-purities, similar to chains, have been given to this monk. They go wherever that monk goes, like chains tied to him, but not elsewhere because they are not tied to another.' All this should not be taken as the essence. Here, however, is the essence: Just as the first link of a chain reaches only the second link, not the third, so too this purity given by the donor does not go elsewhere from the one to whom it was given—thus, because of its resemblance to a chain, it is called 'the cat's chain.' The mention of a cat's chain here should be understood merely as a general illustration of any kind of chain.

Chandadānakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Giving of Consent.

165. “Santi saṅghassa karaṇīyānī”ti vattabbe vacanavipallāsena “karaṇīya”nti vuttaṃ. Tassa sammutidānakiccaṃ natthi. “Hatthapāsaṃ ānetabboyevā”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ.

165. When it should be said, 'There are duties for the Saṅgha,' due to a reversal of speech, it was said as 'duty.' For this, there is no act of formal conferral. 'It must indeed be brought within arm's reach'—this was stated in the explanatory notes.

Saṅghuposathādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on the Saṅgha Uposatha and so forth.

168. Saṅghasannipātato paṭhamaṃ kātabbaṃ pubbakaraṇanti vuttaṃ, pubbakaraṇato pacchā kātabbampi uposathakammato paṭhamaṃ kātabbattā pubbakiccanti vuttaṃ. Ubhayampi cetaṃ uposathakammato paṭhamaṃ kattabbattā katthaci pubbakiccamicceva voharīyati “kiṃ saṅghassa pubbakicca”ntiādīsu viya.

168. It is said that the preliminary act (pubbakaraṇa) is what should be done first, prior to the gathering of the Saṅgha. And what is to be done after the preliminary act is also called 'preliminary duty' (pubbakicca) because it is to be done before the Uposatha ceremony. Both of these, because they are to be done before the Uposatha ceremony, are sometimes simply referred to as 'preliminary duty,' as in expressions such as 'What is the Saṅgha's preliminary duty?' and so on.

Uposathoti [M 3.0279] tīsu uposathadivasesu aññataradivaso. Tasmiñhi sati idaṃ saṅghassa uposathakammaṃ pattakallaṃ nāma hoti, nāsati. Yathāha “na ca, bhikkhave, anuposathe uposatho kātabbo”ti (mahāva. 183). Yāvatikā ca bhikkhū kammappattāti yattakā bhikkhū tassa uposathakammassa pattā yuttā anurūpā sabbantimena paricchedena cattāro bhikkhū pakatattā, te ca kho hatthapāsaṃ avijahitvā ekasīmāyaṃ ṭhitā. Sabhāgāpattiyo ca na vijjantīti ettha yaṃ sabbo saṅgho vikālabhojanādinā sabhāgavatthunā lahukāpattiṃ āpajjati, evarūpā “vatthusabhāgā”ti vuccanti. Etāsu hi avijjamānāsu visabhāgāsu vijjamānāsupi pattakallaṃ hotiyeva.

'Uposatha' means one of the three Uposatha days. When that is present, this Uposatha act of the Saṅgha is called 'timely'; when it is not, it is not. As it is said: 'Monks, the Uposatha should not be performed on a non-Uposatha day' (Mahāvagga 183). 'And as many bhikkhus as are qualified for the act' means as many bhikkhus as are suitable, appropriate, and qualified for that Uposatha act—with the ultimate determination being at least four bhikkhus of normal status, and who are standing within a single boundary without leaving the range of hand-reach. 'And no shared offenses exist' means that whatever minor offense the entire Saṅgha incurs through a shared basis, such as eating at the wrong time, such offenses are called 'basis-shared offenses.' For when these are absent, even if dissimilar offenses are present, it is still timely.

Vajjanīyā ca puggalā tasmiṃ na hontīti “na, bhikkhave, sagahaṭṭhāya parisāyā”ti (mahāva. 154) vacanato gahaṭṭho, “na, bhikkhave, bhikkhuniyā nisinnaparisāya pātimokkhaṃ uddisitabba”ntiādinā (mahāva. 183) nayena vuttā bhikkhunī sikkhamānā sāmaṇero sāmaṇerī [V 3.0254] sikkhāpaccakkhātako antimavatthuajjhāpannako āpattiyā adassane ukkhittako āpattiyā appaṭikamme ukkhittako pāpikāya diṭṭhiyā appaṭinissagge ukkhittako paṇḍako theyyasaṃvāsako titthiyapakkantako tiracchānagato mātughātako pitughātako arahantaghātako bhikkhunīdūsako saṅghabhedako lohituppādako ubhatobyañjanakoti ime vīsati cāti ekavīsati puggalā vajjanīyā nāma, te hatthapāsato bahikaraṇavasena vajjetabbā. Etesu hi tividhe ukkhittake sati uposathaṃ karonto saṅgho pācittiyaṃ āpajjati, sesesu dukkaṭaṃ. Ettha ca tiracchānagatoti yassa upasampadā paṭikkhittā, sova adhippeto, titthiyā gahaṭṭheneva saṅgahitā. Etepi hi vajjanīyā. Evaṃ pattakallaṃ imehi catūhi aṅgehi saṅgahitanti veditabbaṃ.

And individuals who are to be avoided are not present there—thus, 'Bhikkhus, not in an assembly with a householder' (Mahāvagga 154), referring to a householder; 'Bhikkhus, the Pātimokkha should not be recited in an assembly where a bhikkhunī is seated' (Mahāvagga 183), and in accordance with this principle, a bhikkhunī, a female probationer, a male novice, a female novice, one who has renounced the training, one who has committed a terminal offense, one suspended for not seeing an offense, one suspended for not making amends for an offense, one suspended for not relinquishing a wrong view, a eunuch, one who lives in communion by theft, one who has gone over to another sect, an animal, a matricide, a patricide, a murderer of an Arahant, one who has violated a bhikkhunī, a schismatic, one who has drawn the blood of a Buddha, and a hermaphrodite—these twenty-one individuals are called 'those to be avoided,' and they must be avoided by being kept out of hand's reach. For among these, if any of the three types of suspended individuals are present while the Uposatha is being performed, the Saṅgha incurs a pācittiya offense; in the case of the others, a dukkaṭa offense. Here, 'an animal' refers to one whose higher ordination has been rejected—that is the intended meaning—while adherents of other sects are included under householders. These too are to be avoided. Thus, it should be understood that the occasion is fit when it is complete with these four factors.

Ajja me uposatho pannarasotipīti pi-saddena pāḷiyaṃ āgatanayeneva “ajja me uposatho”tipi vattuṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Mātikāṭṭhakathāyaṃ (kaṅkhā. aṭṭha. nidānavaṇṇanā) pana “ajja me uposatho cātuddasoti vā pannarasoti vā vatvā adhiṭṭhāmīti vattabba”nti vuttaṃ.

The particle 'pi' in 'Today is my Uposatha, the fifteenth' indicates that it is also permissible to say simply 'Today is my Uposatha,' in the same way it appears in the Pāḷi. In the Mātikāṭṭhakathā (Kaṅkhāvitaraṇī Aṭṭhakathā, Nidānavannanā), however, it is stated: 'One should say, “Today is my Uposatha, the fourteenth,” or “the fifteenth,” and then make the determination.'

Saṅghuposathādikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Saṅgha Uposatha and Other Matters is concluded.

Āpattipaṭikammavidhikathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Method for Making Amends for an Offense.

169. Nanu [M 3.0280] ca “na, bhikkhave, sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo, yo kareyya, āpatti dukkaṭassā”ti evaṃ sāpattikassa uposathakaraṇe visuṃ paññattā āpatti na dissati, tasmā bhagavatā paññattaṃ “na sāpattikena uposatho kātabbo”ti idaṃ kasmā vuttanti āha “yassa siyā āpatti…pe… paññattaṃ hotīti veditabba”nti. Kiñcāpi visuṃ paññattā āpatti na dissati, atha kho “yassa siyā āpatti, so āvikareyyā”tiādiṃ vadantena atthato paññattāyevāti adhippāyo.

169. But is it not said, 'Bhikkhus, the Uposatha should not be performed by one who has an offense; should one do so, there is an offense of wrong-doing'? Thus, a separately laid down offense for performing the Uposatha while having an offense is not seen. Therefore, why was this declared by the Blessed One: 'The Uposatha should not be performed by one who has an offense'? To this, it is said: 'It should be understood that it is laid down by the words, “Whosoever may have an offense…”' Although a separately laid down offense is not seen, the intention is that by saying, 'Whosoever may have an offense should reveal it,' and so on, it is indeed laid down in meaning.

Pārisuddhidānapaññāpanena cāti imināva “sāpattikena pārisuddhipi na dātabbā”ti dīpitaṃ hoti. Na hi sāpattiko samāno “pārisuddhiṃ dammi, pārisuddhiṃ me hara, pārisuddhiṃ me ārocehī”ti vattumarahati. Tasmā pārisuddhiṃ dentena paṭhamaṃ santī āpatti desetabbā “ahaṃ, āvuso, itthannāmāya āpattiyā vematiko, yadā nibbematiko bhavissāmi, tadā taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissāmī”ti vatvā uposatho kātabbo. “Pātimokkhaṃ sotabba”nti vacanato yāva [V 3.0255] nibbematiko na hoti, tāva sabhāgāpattiṃ paṭiggahetuṃ na labhati, aññesañca kammānaṃ parisuddho nāma hoti. “Puna nibbematiko hutvā desetabbaṃ na cā”ti neva pāḷiyaṃ na aṭṭhakathāyaṃ atthi, desite pana doso natthi. “Ito vuṭṭhahitvā paṭikarissāmīti etthāpi eseva nayo”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Yathā sabbo saṅgho sabhāgāpattiṃ āpajjitvā “suṇātu me bhante, saṅgho…pe… paṭikarissatī”ti ñattiṃ ṭhapetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ labhati, evaṃ tīhi “suṇantu me āyasmantā, ime bhikkhū sabhāgaṃ āpattiṃ āpannā. Yadā aññaṃ bhikkhuṃ suddhaṃ anāpattikaṃ passissanti, tadā tassa santike taṃ āpattiṃ paṭikarissantī”ti gaṇañattiṃ ṭhapetvā, dvīhi aññamaññaṃ ārocetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Ekenapi “parisuddhaṃ labhitvā paṭikarissāmī”ti ābhogaṃ katvā kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti ca vadanti.

And by the laying down of the giving of purity, it is shown that 'one with an offense should not give purity.' For one who has an offense is not fit to say, 'I give purity, take my purity, announce my purity.' Therefore, one giving purity should first disclose an existing offense, saying: 'Friend, I am uncertain about such-and-such an offense. When I am free from uncertainty, I will make amends for that offense.' Having said this, the Uposatha should be performed. In accordance with the statement, 'The Pātimokkha should be heard,' as long as one is not free from uncertainty, one is not permitted to receive a confession for a similar offense, yet one is considered pure for other formal acts of the Saṅgha. That one must confess again after becoming free from uncertainty is not found in either the Pāḷi or the commentary, but there is no fault in confessing. In the glosses it is said, 'In the case of “Having risen from this, I will make amends,” this is the same method.' Just as the entire Saṅgha, having incurred a similar offense, is permitted to perform the Uposatha after passing a motion, 'Venerable sirs, let the Saṅgha listen to me… they will make amends,' so too is it proper for three monks to perform the Uposatha after passing a group motion, 'Venerable sirs, let them listen to me. These bhikkhus have incurred a similar offense. When they see another bhikkhu who is pure and without offense, they will make amends for that offense in his presence,' and for two monks after informing one another. And some say that it is also proper for a single monk to perform it after making the reflection, 'Having found a pure one, I will make amends.'

Āpattipaṭikammavidhikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Method for Making Amends for an Offense is concluded.

Liṅgādidassanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on Seeing the Signs, and so forth.

179. Ācārasaṇṭhānanti [M 3.0281] ācārasaṇṭhiti. Ākarīyati pakāsīyati etenāti ākāro. Līnaṃ gamayati bodhetīti liṅgaṃ. Nimiyanti paricchijja ñāyanti etenāti nimittaṃ. Uddisīyanti apadisīyanti etenāti uddeso. “Amhākaṃ ida”nti aññātaṃ aviditanti aññātakaṃ. Tañca atthato parasantakaṃyevāti āha “aññesaṃ santaka”nti.

179. ‘Ācārasaṇṭhāna’ means the establishment of conduct. ‘Ākāra’ is that by which something is done or revealed. ‘Liṅga’ is that which conveys or makes known what is hidden. ‘Nimitta’ is that by which something is measured, distinguished, and known. ‘Uddesa’ is that by which something is pointed out or specified. ‘Aññātaka’ means what is unknown or unrecognized as ‘this is ours.’ And that, in meaning, is indeed the property of others, hence it is said, ‘belonging to others.’

180. Nānāsaṃvāsakabhāvanti laddhinānāsaṃvāsakabhāvaṃ. Tassa abhibhavo nāma tesaṃ laddhivissajjāpananti āha “taṃ diṭṭhiṃ na nissajjāpentīti attho”ti.

180. ‘The state of being of a different communion’ means the state of being of a different communion due to views. Overcoming that means causing them to abandon their views; hence it is said, ‘the meaning is that they do not cause them to relinquish that view.’

Nagantabbagantabbavārakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Section of What Should Not Be Gone To and What Should Be Gone To.

181. Uposathādhiṭṭhānatthaṃ sīmāpi nadīpi na gantabbāti garukaṃ pātimokkhuddesaṃ vissajjetvā lahukassa akattabbattā vuttaṃ. Āraññakenāpi bhikkhunāti ekacārikena āraññakabhikkhunā, yattha vā saṅghapahonakā bhikkhū na santi, tādise araññe vasantena. Tattha uposathaṃ katvāva gantabbanti tassa vasanaṭṭhāne saṅghuposathassa appavattanato vuttaṃ. Uposathantarāyoti attano uposathantarāyo.

181. ‘For the purpose of determining the Uposatha, one should not go to another boundary or river’—this is said because one should not do a lesser thing, having dismissed the weighty recitation of the Pātimokkha. ‘Even by a forest-dwelling bhikkhu’ means by a solitary forest-dwelling bhikkhu, or by one dwelling in such a wilderness where there are not enough bhikkhus for a Saṅgha. ‘One should go only after performing the Uposatha there’—this is said because the Saṅgha Uposatha does not take place in his dwelling. ‘An obstacle to the Uposatha’ means an obstacle to one’s own Uposatha.

Vajjanīyapuggalasandassanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on Pointing Out Individuals to Be Avoided.

183. Hatthapāsupagamanameva [V 3.0256] pamāṇanti bhikkhunīādayo ṭhitā vā hontu nisinnā vā, tesaṃ hatthapāsupagamanameva āpattiyā pamāṇanti adhippāyo, tasmā ekasīmāyampi hatthapāsaṃ jahāpetvā uposathaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sesamettha uttānameva.

183. ‘The measure is simply approaching within hand’s reach’—the intention is that whether bhikkhunīs and others are standing or sitting, approaching within their hand’s reach is the measure for the offense. Therefore, even within a single boundary, it is proper to perform the Uposatha after having them move out of hand’s reach. The rest here is self-evident.

Uposathakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Chapter on the Uposatha is concluded.

3. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhakaṃ

3. The Chapter on Entering the Rains Retreat

Vassūpanāyikānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Allowance for Entering the Rains Retreat.

184. Vassūpanāyikakkhandhake [M 3.0282][V 3.0257] idha-saddo nipātamattoti okāsaparidīpanassapi asambhavato atthantarassa abodhanato vuttaṃ. Aparajjugatāya assāti iminā asamānādhikaraṇavisayo bāhiratthasamāsoyanti dasseti. Aparajjūti āsāḷhīpuṇṇamito aparaṃ dinaṃ, pāṭipadanti attho. Assāti āsāḷhīpuṇṇamiyā.

184. In the Chapter on Entering the Rains Retreat, the word ‘idha’ is merely a particle; this is said because it is impossible for it to indicate a location and because it does not convey any other meaning. By the phrase ‘Aparajjugatāya assā,’ it shows that this is an external compound in the domain of unequal case relation. ‘Aparajju’ means the day after the full moon of Āsāḷha, that is, the first day of the lunar fortnight. ‘Assā’ refers to the full moon of Āsāḷha.

Vassāne cārikāpaṭikkhepādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Prohibition of Wandering During the Rains, and so forth.

185. Anapekkhagamanena vā aññattha aruṇaṃ uṭṭhāpanena vā āpatti veditabbāti ettha anapekkhagamanena upacārātikkame āpatti veditabbā, sāpekkhagamanena aññattha aruṇuṭṭhāpanena āpatti veditabbā.

185. ‘An offense should be understood as arising either by departing without intention to return, or by causing the dawn to rise elsewhere.’ Herein, an offense should be understood as arising by transgressing the precincts when departing without intention to return; an offense should be understood as arising by causing the dawn to rise elsewhere when departing with the intention to return.

Sattāhakaraṇīyānujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Discourse on the Allowance for a Seven-Day Matter.

187-189. Tīṇi parihīnānīti bhikkhunīnaṃ vaccakuṭiādīnaṃ paṭikkhittattā pahīnāni. Vāreyyanti āvāhavivāhamaṅgalaṃ. Suttantoti attano paguṇasuttanto. Na palujjatīti na vinassati na antaradhāyati.
