Vattanti katikavattaṃ. Tividhampīti pariyattipaṭipattipaṭivedhavasena tividhampi. Sodhetvā pabbājethāti bhabbe ācārakulaputte upaparikkhitvā pabbājetha. Dasavatthukakathā nāma appicchakathā santuṭṭhikathā pavivekakathā asaṃsaggakathā vīriyārambhakathā sīlakathā samādhikathā paññākathā vimuttikathā vimuttiñāṇadassanakathā.

'Observance' means the agreed-upon observance. 'Threefold' means threefold by way of learning, practice, and penetration. 'Having vetted, you should ordain' means you should carefully examine suitable sons from respectable families and then ordain them. The ten topics of discussion are: talk on having few desires, talk on contentment, talk on seclusion, talk on non-association, talk on the arousal of energy, talk on virtue, talk on concentration, talk on wisdom, talk on liberation, and talk on the knowledge and vision of liberation.

Viggahasaṃvattanikavacanaṃ viggāhikaṃ. Caturārakkhaṃ ahāpentāti buddhānussati mettā asubhaṃ maraṇassatīti imaṃ caturārakkhaṃ aparihāpentā. Dantakaṭṭhakhādanavattaṃ ācikkhitabbanti ettha dantakaṭṭhakhādanavattaṃ yo devasikaṃ saṅghamajjhe osarati, tena sāmaṇerādīhi āharitvā bhikkhūnaṃ yathāsukhaṃ paribhuñjanatthāya dantakaṭṭhamāḷake nikkhittesu dantakaṭṭhesu divase divase ekameva dantakaṭṭhaṃ gahetabbaṃ. Yo [M 3.0403] pana devasikaṃ na osarati, padhānaghare vasitvā dhammassavane vā uposathagge vā dissati, tena pamāṇaṃ sallakkhetvā cattāri pañca dantakaṭṭhāni attano vasanaṭṭhāne ṭhapetvā khāditabbāni. Tesu khīṇesu sace punapi dantakaṭṭhamāḷake bahūni hontiyeva, punapi āharitvā khāditabbāni. Yadi pana pamāṇaṃ asallakkhetvā āharati, tesu akhīṇesuyeva māḷake khīyati, tato keci therā “yehi gahitāni, te paṭiharantū”ti vadeyyuṃ, keci “khādantu, puna sāmaṇerā āharissantī”ti. Tasmā vivādaparihāratthaṃ pamāṇaṃ sallakkhetabbaṃ. Gahaṇe pana doso natthi, maggaṃ gacchantenapi ekaṃ vā dve vā thavikāya pakkhipitvā gantabbanti. Bhikkhācāravattaṃ vattakkhandhake piṇḍacārikavatte āvi bhavissati.

Speech that leads to dispute is 'viggāhika.' 'Not neglecting the four protections' means not abandoning these four protections: recollection of the Buddha, loving-kindness, the unattractive, and mindfulness of death. 'The practice of chewing toothwood should be explained': Here, regarding the practice of chewing toothwood, whoever attends the Saṅgha gathering daily should take only one piece of toothwood each day from the toothwood stand, where it has been placed by the novices and so forth after bringing it for the bhikkhus to use as they please. However, one who does not attend the Saṅgha gathering daily but resides in a meditation dwelling, or is seen at the Dhamma-listening or in the Uposatha hall, should estimate the amount and, having kept four or five pieces of toothwood in their own dwelling, chew them. When these are exhausted, if there are still many pieces in the toothwood stand, more may be brought and chewed. But if one brings toothwood without estimating the amount, and the stand runs out while theirs are not yet exhausted, some elders may say, 'Let those who took them return them,' while others may say, 'Let them chew them; the novices will bring more later.' Therefore, to avoid disputes, the amount should be estimated. There is no fault in taking it; even while traveling, one or two pieces may be put in a bag and taken. The practice of going on almsround will become clear in the Khandhaka on Observances, in the section on the alms-gatherer's observance.

Pattaṭṭhāneti [V 3.0368] vassaggena āgantukabhikkhuno pattaṭṭhāne. Tesaṃ chinnavassattā “sādiyantāpi hi te neva vassāvāsikassa sāmino”ti vuttaṃ, paṭhamaṃyeva katikāya katattā khīyantāpi ca āvāsikā neva adātuṃ labhantīti vuttaṃ. Bhatiniviṭṭhanti bhatiṃ katvā viya niviṭṭhaṃ pariyiṭṭhaṃ. Saṅghikaṃ pana apalokanakammaṃ katvā gāhitanti tatruppādaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paccayavasena gāhitanti dāyakānaṃ vassāvāsikapaccayavasena gāhitaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. “Idha, bhikkhave, vassaṃvuttho bhikkhu vibbhamati, saṅghasseveta”nti (mahāva. 374-375) vacanato “gataṭṭhāne…pe… saṅghikaṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Manusseti dāyakamanusse. Varabhāgaṃ sāmaṇerassāti paṭhamabhāgassa gāhitattā vuttaṃ.

“The place for the bowl” means the place for the bowl for an incoming monk according to seniority. Because their rains-residence is broken, it is said, “Even if they consent, they are by no means the owners of what pertains to the rains-residence.” And because the initial agreement was made, even if the residents are displeased, they cannot refuse to give. “Established as a wage” means established, sought after, as if by making a wage. However, what belongs to the Sangha is taken after performing the act of announcement—this is said referring to what arises there. “Taken by reason of requisites” is said referring to what is taken by donors by reason of the requisites for the rains-residence residents. From the statement, “Here, monks, a monk who has completed the rains wanders off; this belongs to the Sangha” (Mahāvagga 374-375), it is said, “In the place gone to… it belongs to the Sangha.” “People” means the donor people. “The best portion for the novice” is said because the first portion has been taken.

Senāsanaggāhāpakasammutikathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Exposition on the Appointment of an Allocator of Lodgings is Concluded.

Upanandavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Story of Upananda

319. Yaṃ tayā tattha senāsanaṃ gahitaṃ…pe… idha muttaṃ hotīti yaṃ tayā tattha gāmakāvāse pacchā senāsanaṃ gahitaṃ, taṃ te gaṇhanteneva idha sāvatthiyaṃ paṭhamagahitasenāsanaṃ muttaṃ hoti. Idha dānāhaṃ [M 3.0404] …pe… tatrāpi muttanti “idānāhaṃ, āvuso, imasmiṃ gāmakāvāse gahitasenāsanaṃ muñcāmī”ti vadantena tatrāpi gāmakāvāse gahitasenāsanaṃ muttaṃ.

319. “The lodging you took there... is released here” means that by the very act of taking the lodging you later took in that village dwelling, the first-taken lodging here in Sāvatthī is released. “Now I... release it there too” means that by saying, “Now, friend, I release the lodging taken in this village dwelling,” the lodging taken there in that village dwelling is also released.

320. Dīghāsanaṃ nāma mañcapīṭhavinimuttaṃ yaṃ kiñci ekato sukhaṃ nisīdituṃ pahoti. Hatthimhi nakho assāti hatthinakho. “Pāsādassa nakho nāma heṭṭhimaparicchedo, so ca hatthikumbhe patiṭṭhito”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Gihivikatanīhārena labbhantīti gihivikatanīhārena paribhuñjituṃ labbhanti, tehi attharitvā dinnāneva nisīdituṃ labbhanti, na sayaṃ atthatāni attharāpitāni vā.

320. A “long seat” is anything, apart from a bed or a bench, that enables one to sit comfortably together. “An elephant’s nail” is its tusk. It is stated in the glosses: “The ‘nail’ of a mansion is the lower boundary, and it is established on an elephant’s frontal boss.” “They are obtainable by the method of a householder’s arrangement” means they are to be used by the method of a householder’s arrangement; one may sit on them only when they have been spread and given by them, not on those spread by oneself or caused to be spread.

Avissajjiyavatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on Items That Cannot Be Alienated

321. Arañjaroti bahuudakagaṇhanakā mahācāṭi. Jalaṃ gaṇhituṃ alanti arañjaro. “Vaṭṭacāṭi viya hutvā thokaṃ dīghamukho majjhe paricchedaṃ dassetvā kato”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Pañcanimmalalocanoti maṃsadibbadhammabuddhasamantacakkhuvasena pañcalocano.

321. An “arañjara” is a large pot for holding much water. Because it is sufficient (alaṃ) for holding (gaṇhituṃ) water (jalaṃ), it is an “arañjara.” It is stated in the glosses: “Made like a round pot, with a slightly elongated mouth, showing a division in the middle.” “Five pure eyes” means the five eyes by way of the fleshly, divine, Dhamma, Buddha, and all-seeing eyes.

Thāvarena [V 3.0369] ca thāvaraṃ garubhaṇḍena ca garubhaṇḍanti ettha pañcasu koṭṭhāsesu purimadvayaṃ thāvaraṃ, pacchimattayaṃ garubhaṇḍanti veditabbaṃ. Jānāpetvāti bhikkhusaṅghaṃ jānāpetvā. Kappiyamañcā sampaṭicchitabbāti “saṅghassa demā”ti dinnaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Sace pana “vihārassa demā”ti vadanti, suvaṇṇarajatamayādiakappiyamañcepi sampaṭicchituṃ vaṭṭati. Na kevalaṃ…pe… parivattetuṃ vaṭṭantīti iminā athāvarena thāvarampi athāvarampi parivattetuṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. Thāvarena athāvarameva hi parivattetuṃ na vaṭṭati. Akappiyaṃ vā mahagghaṃ kappiyaṃ vāti ettha akappiyaṃ nāma suvaṇṇamayamañcādi akappiyabhisibimbohanāni ca. Mahagghaṃ kappiyaṃ nāma dantamayamañcādi pāvārādikappiyaattharaṇādīni ca.

“The stable with the stable, and the heavy goods with the heavy goods”—here, among the five divisions, the first two should be understood as stable property, and the last three as heavy goods. “Having informed” means having informed the community of monks. “An allowable bed should be accepted”—this is said with reference to what is given with the words, “We give it to the Sangha.” But if they say, “We give it to the monastery,” then even an unallowable bed made of gold, silver, or other materials can be accepted. “Not only… but it is also permissible to exchange”—by this, it is shown that it is permissible to exchange the unstable for the stable, and the unstable for the unstable. For it is not permissible to exchange the stable for the unstable. Regarding “what is unallowable or what is expensive but allowable”: here, “unallowable” refers to beds made of gold and the like, as well as unallowable sitting cloths and pillows. “Expensive but allowable” refers to beds made of ivory and the like, as well as allowable coverings such as fine cloths and so on.

Pārihāriyaṃ na vaṭṭatīti attano santakaṃ viya gahetvā pariharituṃ na vaṭṭati. “Gihivikatanīhāreneva paribhuñjitabba”nti iminā sace ārāmikādayo paṭisāmetvā paṭidenti, paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭatīti dasseti. “Paṇṇasūci nāma lekhanī”ti mahāgaṇṭhipade vuttaṃ.

“Personal use is not allowable” means it is not allowable to take and use it as if it were one's own possession. By “It should be used only in the manner of a householder’s arrangement,” it is shown that if monastery attendants, having put it away, offer it back, it is allowable to use it. “A ‘leaf-needle’ is a stylus,” is stated in the Mahāgaṇṭhipada.

“Aḍḍhabāhūti [M 3.0405] kapparato paṭṭhāya yāva aṃsakūṭa”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Aḍḍhabāhu nāma vidatthicaturaṅgulantipi vadanti. Tatthajātakāti saṅghikabhūmiyaṃ jātā. Aṭṭhaṅgulasūcidaṇḍamattoti dīghato aṭṭhaṅgulamatto pariṇāhato paṇṇasūcidaṇḍamatto. Muñjapabbajānaṃyeva pāḷiyaṃ visuṃ āgatattā “muñjaṃ pabbajañca ṭhapetvā”ti vuttaṃ. Aṭṭhaṅgulappamāṇoti dīghato aṭṭhaṅgulappamāṇo. Ghaṭṭanaphalakaṃ nāma yattha ṭhapetvā rajitacīvaraṃ hatthena ghaṭṭenti. Ghaṭṭanamuggaro nāma anuvātādighaṭṭanatthaṃ katoti vadanti. Ambaṇanti phalakehi pokkharaṇīsadisaṃ katapānīyabhājanaṃ. Rajanadoṇīti yattha pakkarajanaṃ ākiritvā ṭhapenti. Bhūmattharaṇaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatīti akappiyacammaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Paccattharaṇagatikanti iminā mañcapīṭhepi attharituṃ vaṭṭatīti dīpeti. Pāvārādipaccattharaṇampi garubhaṇḍanti eke, noti apare, vīmaṃsitvā gahetabbaṃ. Muṭṭhipaṇṇanti tālapaṇṇaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

It is stated in the glosses: “A ‘half-arm’ means from the elbow up to the shoulder joint.” Some say a half-arm is a span and four fingerbreadths. “Born there” means born on Sangha land. “The size of an eight-fingerbreadth needle-stick” means eight fingerbreadths in length and the thickness of a leaf-needle stick. Because “muñja grass and pabbaja grass” are mentioned separately in the Pāli, it is said, “excluding muñja and pabbaja.” “Eight fingerbreadths in measure” means eight fingerbreadths in length. A “beating board” is where they place a dyed robe and rub it with the hand. A “beating mallet,” they say, is made for beating against the wind and so on. An “ambaṇa” is a water vessel made with planks, like a lotus pond. A “dyeing trough” is where they pour prepared dye and keep it. “It is allowable to make a ground-covering” is said with reference to an unallowable hide. “Serving as a covering” indicates that it is also allowable to spread on beds and benches. Some say that coverings such as fine cloths are also heavy goods, while others say they are not—this should be adopted after investigation. “A fistful of leaves” is said with reference to palm leaves.

Navakammadānakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Gift for New Construction

323. Kiñcideva samādapetvā kāressatīti sāmikoyeva kañci bhikkhuṃ samādapetvā kāressati. Utukāle paṭibāhituṃ na labhatīti hemantagimhesu aññe sampattabhikkhū paṭibāhituṃ na labhati. Tibhāganti tatiyabhāgaṃ. Sace saddhivihārikānaṃ dātukāmo hotīti sace so saṅghassa bhaṇḍakaṭhapanaṭṭhānaṃ vā navakānaṃ vā vasanaṭṭhānaṃ dātuṃ na icchati, attano saddhivihārikānaññeva [V 3.0370] dātukāmo hotīti attho. Etañhi saddhivihārikānaṃ dātuṃ labhatīti etaṃ tatiyabhāgaṃ upaḍḍhabhāgaṃ vā dātuṃ labhati. Akataṭṭhāneti senāsanato bahi cayādīnaṃ akataṭṭhāne. Bahikuṭṭeti kuṭṭato bahi.

323. “Having encouraged someone to do something, he will have it done” means the owner himself, having encouraged some monk, will have it done. “He is not able to prevent them during the season” means that during the winter and summer seasons, he is not able to prevent other monks who have arrived. “A third part” means the third part. “If he wishes to give to his co-residents” means if he does not wish to give a place for storing the Sangha's goods or a dwelling place for new monks, but wishes to give it only to his own co-residents, this is the meaning. “For he is allowed to give this to his co-residents” means he is allowed to give this third part or a half part. “In an unmade place” means in an unmade place for heaps of sweepings and so on, outside the lodging. “Outside the wall” means outside the wall.

Aññatraparibhogapaṭikkhepādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Prohibition of Other Uses and So Forth

324. Cakkalikanti kambalādīhi veṭhetvā cakkasaṇṭhānena pādapuñchanayoggaṃ kataṃ. Paribhaṇḍakatā bhūmi nāma saṇhamattikāhi katā kāḷavaṇṇādibhūmi. Senāsanaṃ mañcapīṭhādi. Tatheva vaḷañjetuṃ vaṭṭatīti aññehi āvāsikabhikkhūhi paribhuttanīhārena paribhuñjituṃ vaṭṭati. “Nevāsikā pakatiyā anatthatāya bhūmiyā ṭhapenti ce, tesampi anāpattiyevā”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Dvārampītiādinā vuttadvāravātapānādayo aparikammakatāpi na apassayitabbā. Lomesūti lomesu phusantesu.

324. A ‘cakkalika’ is something suitable for wiping the feet, made in the shape of a wheel by wrapping it with blankets and so on. A ‘finished floor’ is a floor of black color and so on, made with fine clay. ‘Lodging’ means a bed, bench, and so on. “It is allowable to use it in the same way” means it is allowable to use it in the manner that other resident monks have used it. It is stated in the glosses: “If visiting monks place it on the ground out of natural inattentiveness, there is no offense for them either.” By “doors, etc.” is meant the aforementioned doors, windows, and so on, which, even if unfinished, should not be leaned against. “On the hairs” means when the hairs are touching.

Saṅghabhattādianujānanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on Allowing Sangha Meals and So Forth

325. Uddesabhattaṃ [M 3.0406] nimantananti imaṃ vohāraṃ pattānīti ettha iti-saddo ādiattho, “uddesabhattaṃ nimantana”ntiādivohāraṃ pattānīti ayamettha attho. Tampi anto katvāti āyatiṃ bhikkhūnaṃ kukkuccavinodanatthāya tampi saṅghabhattaṃ anto katvā.

325. Regarding “they have come to be designated ‘a meal by designation’ and ‘an invitation’”: here, the word ‘iti’ has the meaning of ‘and so forth.’ The meaning here is that they have come to be designated by terms such as ‘a meal by designation’ and ‘an invitation.’ “Including that as well” means including that Sangha meal as well, for the sake of dispelling the scruples of monks in the future.

Uddesabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition on the Meal by Designation

Attano vihāradvāreti vihārassa dvārakoṭṭhakasamīpaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Bhojanasālāyāti bhattuddesaṭṭhānabhūtāya bhojanasālāya. “Dinnaṃ panā”ti vatvā yathā so dāyako deti, taṃ vidhiṃ dassetuṃ “saṅghato bhante”tiādimāha. Antaraghareti antogehe. Antoupacāragatānanti ettha gāmadvāravīthicatukkesu dvādasahatthabbhantaraṃ antoupacāro nāma. Antaragharassa upacāre pana labbhamānavisesaṃ dassetuṃ “gharūpacāro cetthā”tiādimāha. Ekavaḷañjanti ekena dvārena vaḷañjitabbaṃ. Nānānivesanesūti nānākulassa nivesanesu. Lajjī pesalo agatigamanaṃ vajjetvā medhāvī ca upaparikkhitvā uddisissatīti āha “pesalo lajjī medhāvī icchitabbo”ti. Nisinnassapi niddāyantassapīti anādare sāmivacanaṃ. Ticīvaraparivāranti ettha “udakapattalābhī viya aññopi uddesabhattaṃ alabhitvā vatthādimanekappakārakaṃ labhati ce, tasseva [V 3.0371] ta”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Attano rucivasena yaṃ kiñci vatvā āharituṃ vissajjitattā vissaṭṭhadūto nāma. Yaṃ icchatīti “uddesapattaṃ dethā”tiādīni vadanto yaṃ icchati. Pucchāsabhāgenāti pucchāsadisena.

‘At the door of one’s own dwelling’ is said referring to the area near the door-chamber of the dwelling. ‘In the food hall’ means in the food hall that is the place for the distribution of meals. Having said, ‘But it is given,’ to show the procedure by which the donor gives, he says, ‘From the Sangha, venerable sir,’ and so forth. ‘Inside the house’ means in the inner house. Regarding ‘those who have entered the inner vicinity,’ here, the inner vicinity is what is within twelve hands at a village gate, street, or crossroads. To show the special case obtainable in the vicinity of a house, he says, ‘And here, the vicinity of a house,’ and so forth. ‘One circuit’ means it is to be used by one door. ‘In various residences’ means in the residences of various families. Because a modest, amiable, and wise one, having avoided partiality and having examined, will assign, he says, ‘An amiable, modest, and wise one is to be desired.’ ‘Of one seated or of one sleeping’ is a genitive construction used to show disregard. Regarding ‘with the three robes as an accessory,’ here it is said in the glosses: ‘Just as one who receives a water bowl, if another does not receive the designated meal but receives various kinds of things such as cloth, it belongs to him.’ He is called a ‘dispatched messenger’ because he has been sent to fetch whatever is requested according to one’s own preference. ‘Whatever one wishes’ means whatever he desires when saying, ‘Give the designated bowl,’ and so forth. ‘By way of a share in the question’ means similar to a question.

“Ekā kūṭaṭṭhitikā nāma hotī”ti vatvā tameva ṭhitikaṃ vibhāvento “rañño vā hī”tiādimāha. Aññehi uddesabhattehi amissetvā visuṃyeva ṭhitikāya gahetabbattā “ekacārikabhattānī”ti vuttaṃ. Theyyāya harantīti pattahārakā haranti. Gīvā hotīti āṇāpakassa gīvā hoti. “Manussānaṃ vacanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti gacchantīti “manussānaṃ vacanaṃ kātuṃ vaṭṭatī”ti tena bhikkhunā vuttā gacchanti. Akatabhāgo nāmāti āgantukabhāgo nāma. “Sabbo saṅgho paribhuñjatū”ti [M 3.0407] vutteti ettha “paṭhamameva ‘sabbaṃ saṅghikaṃ pattaṃ dethā’ti vatvā pacchā ‘sabbo saṅgho paribhuñjatū’ti avuttepi bhājetvāva paribhuñjitabba”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ.

Having said, ‘There is one called a standing provision,’ he explains that very standing provision, beginning with ‘For the king or….’ Because it is to be taken separately as a standing provision without being mixed with other designated meals, it is called ‘single meals.’ Regarding ‘they carry with thievish intent,’ this means the bowl-carriers carry it. ‘It is the neck’ means it is the neck of the one who gives the order. Regarding ‘they go, thinking, “It is proper to do the bidding of men,”’ this means they go having been told by that monk, ‘It is proper to do the bidding of men.’ ‘The unmade portion’ is the name for the newcomer’s portion. Regarding ‘when it is said, “Let the whole Sangha enjoy,”’ here it is said in the glosses: ‘Even if one first says, “Give all the Sangha’s bowls,” and afterwards does not say, “Let the whole Sangha enjoy,” it should be divided and then enjoyed.’

Nimantanabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Discourse on Invitation Meals

“Ettake bhikkhū saṅghato uddisitvā dethā”tiādīni avatvā “ettakānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti vatvā dinnaṃ saṅghikaṃ nimantanaṃ nāma. Piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭatīti bhikkhāpariyāyena vuttattā vaṭṭati. Paṭipāṭiyāti laddhapaṭipāṭiyā. Vicchinditvāti “bhattaṃ gaṇhathā”ti padaṃ avatvā. Tenevāha “bhattanti avadantenā”ti. Ālopasaṅkhepenāti ekekapiṇḍavasena. Ayañca nayo nimantaneyeva, na uddesabhatte. Tattha hi ekassa pahonakappamāṇaṃyeva bhājetabbaṃ, tasmā uddesabhatte ālopaṭṭhitikā nāma natthi. Acchatīti tiṭṭhati. “Ekavāranti yāva tasmiṃ āvāse vasanti bhikkhū, sabbe labhantī”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Ayaṃ panettha adhippāyo – ekavāranti na ekadivasaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ, yattakā pana bhikkhū tasmiṃ āvāse vasanti, te sabbe. Ekasmiṃ divase gahitabhikkhū aññadā aggahetvā yāva ekavāraṃ sabbe bhikkhū bhojitā honti, tāva ye jānanti, te gahetvā gantabbanti.

When, without saying things such as, ‘Having designated this many bhikkhus from the Sangha, give,’ what is given after saying, ‘Accept food for this many bhikkhus,’ is called a Sangha invitation. It is permissible even for those who live on alms-food, because it is stated in the section on alms-food. ‘In order’ means in the order of having received. ‘By interrupting’ means without saying the words ‘Accept food.’ Therefore, he said, ‘by one not saying “food.”’ ‘By the measure of a morsel’ means by way of each morsel. And this method applies only to an invitation, not to a designated meal. For in that case, only an amount sufficient for one person should be apportioned; therefore, in a designated meal, there is no such thing as a ‘morsel-based provision.’ ‘It remains’ means it stays. In the glosses it is said: ‘“One turn” means that as long as bhikkhus reside in that monastery, all receive.’ This, however, is the intention here: ‘one turn’ is not said with reference to a single day, but rather all the bhikkhus who reside in that monastery. The bhikkhus who have received on one day should not receive on another day; until all bhikkhus have been fed one time, those who know should accept and go.

Salākabhattakathāvaṇṇanā

The Exposition of the Discourse on Ticket-Meals

Upanibandhitvāti likhitvā. Niggahena datvāti anicchantampi niggahena sampaṭicchāpetvā[V 3.0372]. Ekagehavasenāti ekāya gharapāḷiyā vasena. Uddisitvāti “tuyhañca tuyhañca pāpuṇātī”ti vatvā. Dūrattā niggahetvāpi vārena gāhetabbagāmo vāragāmo. Vihāravāre niyuttā vihāravārikā, vārena vihārarakkhaṇakā. Aññathattanti pasādaññathattaṃ. Phātikammameva bhavantīti vihārarakkhaṇatthāya saṅghena dātabbaatirekalābhā honti. Saṅghanavakena laddhakāleti divase divase ekekassa pāpitāni dve tīṇi ekacārikabhattāni teneva niyāmena attano pāpuṇanaṭṭhāne saṅghanavakena laddhakāle. Yassa kassaci sammukhībhūtassa pāpetvāti ettha “yebhuyyena ce bhikkhū bahisīmagatā honti, sammukhībhūtassa [M 3.0408] yassa kassaci pāpetabbaṃ sabhāgattā ekena laddhaṃ sabbesaṃ hoti, tasmimpi asati attano pāpetvā dātabba”nti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Rasasalākanti ucchurasasalākaṃ.

‘Having registered it’ means having written it down. ‘Having given with compulsion’ means having made even an unwilling person accept it by force. ‘By way of one residence’ means by way of a single row of houses. ‘Having designated’ means saying, “It reaches you and you.” A village from which alms must be taken by turn, even with compulsion due to its distance, is a ‘turn-village.’ Those appointed for the monastery’s turn are the monastery-turn-takers; they are guardians of the monastery by turn. ‘A change of state’ means a change of faith. ‘They become simply an allowable transaction’ means they are extra gains to be given by the Sangha for the purpose of protecting the monastery. ‘At the time of being received by the Sangha’s junior monk’ means at the time when two or three single meals, which are assigned to each one day by day, are received by the Sangha’s junior monk at one’s own place of receipt, by that very same method. Regarding ‘having made it reach whoever is present,’ here it is said in the glosses: “If most bhikkhus have gone outside the boundary, it should be made to reach whoever is present; because it is common property, what is received by one belongs to all. If even that one is not present, it should be made to reach oneself and then given.” ‘A juice-ticket’ means a sugarcane-juice ticket.

“Saṅghato nirāmisasalākāpi vihāre pakkabhattampi vaṭṭatiyevā”ti sādhāraṇaṃ katvā visuddhimagge (visuddhi. 1.26) vuttattā “evaṃ gāhite sāditabbaṃ, evaṃ na sāditabba”nti visesetvā avuttattā ca bhesajjādisalākāyo cettha kiñcāpi piṇḍapātikānampi vaṭṭanti, salākavasena gāhitattā pana na sāditabbāti ettha adhippāyo vīmaṃsitabbo. Yadi hi bhesajjādisalākā salākavasena gāhitā na sāditabbā siyā, saṅghato nirāmisasalākā vaṭṭatiyevāti na vadeyya, “atirekalābho saṅghabhattaṃ uddesabhatta”ntiādivacanato (mahāva. 128) “atirekalābhaṃ paṭikkhipāmī”ti salākavasena gāhetabbaṃ bhattameva paṭikkhittaṃ, na bhesajjaṃ. Saṅghabhattādīni hi cuddasa bhattāniyeva tena na sāditabbānīti vuttāni, khandhakabhāṇakānaṃ vā matena idha evaṃ vuttanti gahetabbaṃ. Aggato dātabbabhikkhā aggabhikkhā. Laddhā vā aladdhā vāti labhitvā vā alabhitvā vā. Nibaddhāya aggabhikkhāya appamattikāya eva sambhavato labhitvāpi punadivase gaṇhituṃ vuttaṃ. Aggabhikkhāmattanti hi ettha matta-saddo bahubhāvaṃ nivatteti.

Because it is stated in the Visuddhimagga (Vism. 1.26), making it a general rule, that ‘From the Sangha, even a non-material ticket and also cooked food in the monastery are indeed permissible,’ and because it is not stated with any specification, such as ‘when taken in this way it should be consumed, when in that way it should not be consumed,’ the intention here should be investigated: although tickets for medicine and so on are permissible even for alms-food eaters, since they are taken by way of a ticket, they should not be consumed. For if tickets for medicine and so on, taken by way of a ticket, were not to be consumed, he would not say, ‘From the Sangha, a non-material ticket is indeed permissible.’ From the saying (Mahāva. 128), ‘Excess gain, a Sangha meal, a designated meal,’ etc., the statement ‘I decline the excess gain’ means that only the meal to be taken by way of a ticket is rejected, not medicine. Indeed, it is said that the fourteen kinds of meals, beginning with the Sangha meal, are not to be consumed by him; or it should be understood that this is said here according to the opinion of the reciters of the Khandhakas.

Salākabhattaṃ nāma vihāreyeva uddisīyati vihārameva sandhāya diyyamānattāti āha “vihāre apāpitaṃ panā”tiādi. Tatra āsanasālāyāti tasmiṃ gāme āsanasālāya. Vihāraṃ ānetvā gāhetabbanti tathā vatvā tasmiṃ divase dinnabhattaṃ vihārameva ānetvā ṭhitikāya gāhetabbaṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ disābhāge. Taṃ gahetvāti taṃ vāragāmasalākaṃ attanā gahetvā. Tenāti yo attano pattaṃ vāragāmasalākaṃ disaṃgamikassa adāsi, tena. Anatikkanteyeva tasmiṃ tassa salākā gāhetabbāti yasmā upacārasīmaṭṭhasseva salākā pāpuṇāti, tasmā tasmiṃ disaṃgamike [V 3.0373] upacārasīmaṃ anatikkanteyeva tassa disaṃgamikassa pattasalākā attano pāpetvā gahetabbā.

A ticket-meal is designated only in the monastery because it is given with reference to the monastery itself; therefore he said, ‘But what has not been brought to the monastery…’ and so on. There, ‘in the assembly hall’ means in the assembly hall of that village. ‘Having brought it to the monastery, it should be taken’ means that, having said so, the meal given on that day should be brought to the monastery itself and taken as a standing provision. ‘There’ means in that region. ‘Having taken that’ means having personally taken that turn-village ticket. ‘By him’ means by the one who gave his own turn-village ticket to a traveling bhikkhu. Regarding ‘his ticket should be taken while he has not yet crossed,’ this is because a ticket is due only to one who is standing within the vicinity-boundary. Therefore, while that traveling bhikkhu has not yet crossed the vicinity-boundary, that traveling bhikkhu’s received ticket should be made to reach oneself and be taken.

Anāgatadivaseti [M 3.0409] ettha kathaṃ tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ āgatānāgatabhāvo viññāyatīti ce? Yasmā tato tato āgatā bhikkhū tasmiṃ gāme āsanasālāya sannipatanti, tasmā tesaṃ āgatānāgatabhāvo sakkā viññātuṃ. Amhākaṃ gocaragāmeti salākabhattadāyakānaṃ gāme. Bhuñjituṃ āgacchantīti “mahāthero ekakova vihāre ohīno avassaṃ sabbasalākā attano pāpetvā ṭhito”ti maññamānā āgacchanti.

On the “future day,” how is the arrival and non-arrival of those bhikkhus known? Since bhikkhus, having come from various places, assemble in the assembly hall of that village, therefore their arrival and non-arrival can be known. “Our alms-resort village” means the village of the alms-givers who provide the ticket-meal. They come to eat, thinking, “The senior bhikkhu is staying alone in the monastery; surely he will inevitably have taken all the tickets for himself and be waiting there.”

Pakkhikabhattādikathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of Fortnightly Meals and So Forth

Abhilakkhitesu catūsu pakkhadivasesu dātabbabhattaṃ pakkhikaṃ. Abhilakkhitesūti ettha abhīti upasaggamattaṃ, lakkhaṇīyesu icceva attho, uposathasamādānadhammassavanapūjāsakkārādikaraṇatthaṃ lakkhitabbesu sallakkhetabbesu upalakkhetabbesūti vuttaṃ hoti. Sve pakkhoti “ajja pakkhikaṃ na gāhetabba”nti pakkhikassa aniyamattā vuttaṃ. “Sve amhākaṃ ghare lūkhabhattaṃ bhavissatī”ti potthakesu likhanti, “pakkhabhattaṃ bhavissatī”ti pāṭhena bhavitabbaṃ. Uposathe dātabbaṃ bhattaṃ uposathikaṃ. Nibandhāpitanti “asukavihārassā”ti niyamitaṃ. Gāhetvā bhuñjitabbanti tasmiṃ senāsane vasantehi ṭhitikāya gāhetvā bhuñjitabbaṃ. Taṇḍulādīnipesenti…pe… vaṭṭatīti abhihaṭabhikkhattā vaṭṭati. Tathā paṭiggahitattāti bhikkhānāmena paṭiggahitattā. Pattaṃ pūretvā thaketvā dinnanti “guḷakabhattaṃ demā”ti dinnaṃ. Guḷapiṇḍepi…pe… dātabboti ettha guḷapiṇḍaṃ tālapakkappamāṇanti veditabbaṃ. Sesamettha suviññeyyamevāti.

The meal to be given on the four designated fortnightly days is a fortnightly meal. Regarding 'abhilakkhitesu,' here 'abhi' is merely a prefix; the meaning is 'on those days which are to be marked.' It is said that these are the days to be marked, noted, or recognized for the purpose of undertaking the Uposatha, listening to the Dhamma, making offerings, and showing respect. 'Tomorrow is the fortnightly day' is said because of the non-fixed nature of the fortnightly meal, meaning 'the fortnightly meal is not to be taken today.' In the books they write, 'Tomorrow, at our house, there will be plain food,' but it should be read as, 'There will be a fortnightly meal.' The meal to be given on the Uposatha day is the Uposatha meal. 'Assigned' means designated as, 'for such-and-such monastery.' 'Having taken it, it should be eaten' means that those staying in that residence should take it and eat it according to the established rule. They send rice and so forth... it is valid because it is an invited meal. 'Because it was received in that way' means it was received in the name of the bhikkhus. 'Given by filling the bowl and covering it' means it was given as a 'sugar-lump meal.' Similarly, with a lump of sugar... it should be given. Here, a lump of sugar should be understood as the size of a ripe palmyra fruit. The rest here is easily understood.

Senāsanakkhandhakavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Chapter on Dwellings is Completed.

7. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhakaṃ

7. The Chapter on Schism in the Saṅgha

Chasakyapabbajjākathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Account of the Renunciation of the Six Sakyans

330. Saṅghabhedakakkhandhake [M 3.0410][V 3.0374] anupiyāyantiādīsu “anupiyā nāmā”ti vattabbe ākārassa rassattaṃ anunāsikassa ca āgamaṃ katvā “anupiyaṃ nāmā”ti vuttaṃ. Mallānanti mallarājūnaṃ. Na heṭṭhā pāsādā orohatīti uparipāsādato heṭṭhimatalaṃ na orohati, “heṭṭhāpāsāda”ntipi paṭhanti. Anuruddho vā pabbājeyyāti yojetabbaṃ. Gharāvāsatthanti gharāvāsassa anucchavikaṃ kammaṃ. Udakaṃ abhinetabbanti udakaṃ āharitabbaṃ. Ninnetabbanti ābhatamudakaṃ puna nīharitabbaṃ. Niddhāpetabbanti antarantarā uṭṭhitatiṇāni uddharitvā apanetabbaṃ. Lavāpetabbanti paripakkakāle lavāpetabbaṃ. Ubbāhāpetabbanti khalamaṇḍalaṃ harāpetabbaṃ. Ujuṃ kārāpetabbanti puñjaṃ kārāpetabbaṃ. Palālāni uddharāpetabbānīti palālāni apanetabbāni. Bhusikā uddharāpetabbāti gunnaṃ khuraggehi sañchinnā bhusasaṅkhātā nāḷadaṇḍā apanetabbā. Opunāpetabbanti vātamukhe opunāpetvā palālaṃ apanetabbaṃ. Atiharāpetabbanti antokoṭṭhāgāraṃ upanetabbaṃ. Na kammāti na kammāni. Gharāvāsatthenāti upayogatthe karaṇavacanaṃ. Upajānāhīti ca upasaggamatto upa-saddo. Tenāha “gharāvāsatthaṃ jānāhī”ti. Jānāhīti cettha paṭipajjāti attho veditabbo. Akāmakāti anicchamānā.

330. In the Chapter on Schism in the Saṅgha, regarding 'anupiyāyanti' and so forth, though it should be said as 'anupiyā nāmā,' the shortening of the vowel 'ā' and the addition of a nasal sound result in 'anupiyaṃ nāmā' being stated. 'Mallānaṃ' means of the Malla kings. 'Na heṭṭhā pāsādā orohati' means he does not descend from the upper palace to the lower floor; some read 'heṭṭhāpāsāda' as well. 'Anuruddho vā pabbājeyya' should be construed. 'Gharāvāsatthanti' means work appropriate for household life. 'Udakaṃ abhinetabba' means water should be fetched. 'Ninnetabba' means the water that has been brought should be taken away again. 'Niddhāpetabba' means the grass that has sprung up intermittently should be uprooted and removed. 'Lavāpetabba' means it should be harvested at the right time. 'Ubbāhāpetabba' means the grain should be brought to the threshing floor. 'Ujuṃ kārāpetabba' means a heap should be made. 'Palālāni uddharāpetabbāni' means the straw should be removed. 'Bhusikā uddharāpetabbā' means the stalks cut by the hooves of cattle, called chaff, should be removed. 'Opunāpetabba' means the straw should be winnowed in the wind and removed. 'Atiharāpetabba' means it should be brought into the inner storehouse. 'Na kamma' means not the works. 'Gharāvāsatthena' is the instrumental case indicating purpose. In 'Upajānāhi,' the word 'upa-' is merely a prefix. Therefore, it is said, 'gharāvāsatthaṃ jānāhi.' Here, 'jānāhi' should be understood as 'undertake.' 'Akāmakā' means unwilling.

331-332. Yaṃ na nivattoti yasmā na nivatto. Suññāgāragatoti (udā. aṭṭha. 20) “ṭhapetvā gāmañca gāmūpacārañca avasesaṃ arañña”nti (pārā.92) vuttaṃ araññaṃ rukkhamūlañca ṭhapetvā aññaṃ pabbatakandarādi pabbajitasāruppaṃ nivāsaṭṭhānaṃ janasambādhābhāvato idha “suññāgāra”nti adhippetaṃ. Atha vā jhānakaṇṭakānaṃ saddānaṃ abhāvato vivittaṃ yaṃ kiñci agārampi “suññāgāra”nti veditabbaṃ. Taṃ suññāgāraṃ upagato. Abhikkhaṇanti bahulaṃ. Udānaṃ udānesīti so hi āyasmā araññe divāvihāraṃ upagatopi rattivāsūpagatopi yebhuyyena phalasamāpattisukhena nirodhasamāpattisukhena ca vītināmesi, tasmā [M 3.0411] taṃ sukhaṃ sandhāya pubbe [V 3.0375] attanā anubhūtaṃ sabhayaṃ sapariḷāhaṃ rajjasukhaṃ jigucchitvā “aho sukhaṃ aho sukha”nti somanassasahitañāṇasamuṭṭhānaṃ pītisamuggāraṃ samuggirati. Te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocunti te sambahulā bhikkhū ullumpanasabhāvasaṇṭhitā tassa anuggaṇhanādhippāyena bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ, na ujjhānavasena. Nissaṃsayanti asandehena, ekantenāti attho. Te kira bhikkhū puthujjanā tassa āyasmato vivekasukhaṃ sandhāya udānaṃ ajānantā evamāhaṃsu. Samanussarantoti ukkaṇṭhanavasena anussaranto.

331-332. 'Yaṃ na nivatto' means because he did not turn back. 'Gone to an empty dwelling' refers to what is said: 'Except for villages and their outskirts, the rest is wilderness.' Here, excluding the wilderness and the foot of trees, any other suitable dwelling place for a renunciant, such as mountain caves, is meant by 'empty dwelling' due to the absence of crowds. Alternatively, any dwelling, even a house, should be understood as an 'empty dwelling' because it is secluded from the sounds that are thorns to meditation. He went to that empty dwelling. 'Abhikkhaṇa' means frequently. 'Udānaṃ udānesi' means that venerable one, whether he went to the wilderness for daytime abiding or for nighttime dwelling, mostly spent his time in the bliss of fruition attainment and cessation attainment. Therefore, despising the fearful and feverish pleasure of kingship he had previously experienced, he uttered an eructation of joy that arises from knowledge accompanied by mental gladness: 'Ah, happiness! Ah, happiness!' 'Te bhikkhū bhagavantaṃ etadavocuṃ' means those many monks, being of a nature to uplift, spoke to the Blessed One with the intention of supporting him, not out of complaint. 'Nissaṃsaya' means without uncertainty; the meaning is 'absolutely.' It is said that those monks, being worldlings, spoke thus, not knowing the venerable one's inspired utterance concerning the happiness of seclusion. 'Samanussaranto' means remembering with longing.

Aññataranti nāmagottena apākaṭaṃ ekaṃ bhikkhuṃ. Āmantesīti āṇāpesi te bhikkhū saññāpetukāmo. Evanti vacanasampaṭiggahe, sādhūti attho. Evaṃ bhanteti ettha pana evaṃ-saddo paṭiññāyaṃ. “Abhikkhaṇaṃ ‘aho sukhaṃ aho sukha’nti imaṃ udānaṃ udānesī”ti yathā te bhikkhū vadanti, taṃ evaṃ tathevāti attano udānaṃ paṭijānāti. “Kiṃ pana tvaṃ bhaddiyā”ti kasmā bhagavā pucchati, kiṃ tassa cittaṃ na jānātīti? No na jānāti, teneva pana tamatthaṃ vadāpetvā te bhikkhū saññāpetuṃ pucchati. Vuttañhetaṃ “jānantāpi tathāgatā pucchanti, jānantāpi na pucchantī”tiādi (pārā. 16, 194). Atthavasanti kāraṇaṃ.

'Aññatara' refers to a certain monk, not distinguished by name or clan. 'Āmantesi' means he instructed, desiring to convince those monks. 'Evaṃ' is an expression of acceptance of a statement; the meaning is 'good.' In 'Evaṃ bhante,' however, the word 'evaṃ' is an affirmation. Just as those monks say, 'He frequently uttered this inspired utterance: "Ah, happiness! Ah, happiness!"' he acknowledges his own inspired utterance to be thus, to be that very thing. 'But what, Bhaddiya?'—why does the Blessed One ask? Is it that he does not know his mind? No, it is not that he does not know; but he asks in order to have that matter stated and to convince those monks. For it is said: 'Even though the Tathāgatas know, they ask; even though they know, they do not ask,' etc. 'Atthavasa' means for a reason.

Antopi antepureti itthāgārassa sañcaraṇaṭṭhānabhūte rājagehassa abbhantare, yattha rājā nahānabhojanasayanādiṃ kappeti. Rakkhā susaṃvihitāti ārakkhādikatapurisehi gutti suṭṭhu samantato vihitā. Bahipi antepureti aṭṭakaraṇaṭṭhānādike antepurato bahibhūte rājagehe. Evaṃ rakkhito gopito santoti evaṃ rājageharājadhānīrajjadesesu anto bahi ca anekesu ṭhānesu anekasatehi susaṃvihitarakkhāvaraṇaguttiyā mameva nibbhayatthaṃ phāsuvihāratthaṃ rakkhito gopito samāno. Bhītotiādīni padāni aññamaññavevacanāni. Atha vā bhītoti pararājūhi bhāyamāno. Ubbiggoti sakarajjepi pakatikkhobhato uppajjanakabhayubbegena ubbiggo calito. Ussaṅkīti “raññā nāma sabbakālaṃ avissatthena bhavitabba”nti vacanato sabbattha avissāsanavasena tesaṃ tesaṃ kiccakaraṇīyānaṃ accayato uppajjanakaparisaṅkāya ca uddhamuddhaṃ saṅkamāno. Utrāsīti “santikāvacarehipi ajānantasseva me kadāci [M 3.0412] anattho bhaveyyā”ti uppannena sarīrakampampi uppādanasamatthena tāsena utrāsi. “Utrasto”tipi paṭhanti. Viharāmīti evaṃbhūto hutvā viharāmi.

'Within the inner palace' means within the king's residence, in the thoroughfare of the women's quarters, where the king undertakes bathing, eating, sleeping, and so forth. 'Protection is well-arranged' means security is thoroughly and completely arranged by guards and other men. 'Also outside the inner palace' refers to places such as the courthouse, which are outside the inner palace but within the king's residence. 'Thus being guarded and protected' means being guarded and protected in this way, for my own fearlessness and comfortable living, by hundreds of well-arranged guards, ramparts, and security measures in many places, both inside and outside, within the king's residence, the royal capital, and the country. The words 'afraid' and so on are synonyms for one another. Or else, 'afraid' means fearing other kings. 'Agitated' means shaken, agitated by the fear and anxiety arising from natural disturbances even in one's own kingdom. 'Apprehensive' means, in accordance with the saying, 'A king must always be distrustful,' being increasingly apprehensive due to being distrustful in all matters and due to the suspicion arising from the transgression of the various duties and responsibilities of others. 'Terrified' means, thinking, 'Even by those close to me, harm might unknowingly befall me at some time,' one is terrified by a fear that has arisen which is capable of producing even bodily tremors. Some also read 'utrasto'. 'I dwell' means being in such a state, I dwell.

Etarahīti idāni pabbajitakālato paṭṭhāya. Ekoti asahāyo. Tena vivekaṭṭhakāyataṃ dasseti. Abhītotiādīnaṃ padānaṃ vuttavipariyāyena attho veditabbo. Bhayādinimittassa pariggahassa [V 3.0376] taṃnimittassa ca kilesagahanassa abhāvenevassa abhītāditāti etena cittavivekaṃ dasseti. Appossukkoti sarīraguttiyaṃ nirussukko. Pannalomoti lomahaṃsuppādakassa chambhitattassa abhāvena anuggatalomo. Padadvayenapi serivihāraṃ dasseti. Paradattavuttoti parehi dinnena cīvarādinā vattamāno. Etena sabbaso saṅgābhāvadīpanamukhena anavasesabhayahetuvirahaṃ dasseti. Migabhūtena cetasāti vissatthavihāritāya migassa viya jātena cittena. Migo hi amanussapathe araññe vasamāno vissattho tiṭṭhati nisīdati nipajjati yenakāmañca pakkamati appaṭihatacāro, evaṃ ahampi viharāmīti dasseti. Vuttañhetaṃ paccekasambuddhena –

'Now' means from the time of going forth. 'Alone' means without a companion. By this, he shows his desire for physical seclusion. The meaning of the words 'fearless' and so on should be understood in the opposite way to what was previously stated. Because there is no grasping of the signs of fear and so on, and no taking hold by the thicket of defilements of such signs, he is fearless and so on—by this, he shows mental seclusion. 'Free from anxiety' means without concern for the body's protection. 'With hair lying down' means his hair is not raised due to the absence of the terror that causes hair to bristle. With these two phrases, he shows his dwelling at ease. 'Living on what is given by others' means sustaining himself with robes and so on given by others. By this, through indicating the complete absence of attachment, he shows the absence of all causes of fear. 'With a mind become like a deer's' means with a mind that has become like a deer's due to its confident way of dwelling. For a deer, dwelling in the wilderness on a path not frequented by humans, remains confident—it stands, sits, lies down, and goes wherever it wishes, its movement unimpeded. In the same way, he shows, 'I too dwell thus.' For this was said by a Paccekabuddha:

“Migo araññamhi yathā abaddho;

Yenicchakaṃ gacchati gocarāya;

Viññū naro serita pekkhamāno;

Eko care khaggavisāṇakappo”ti. (su. ni. 39; apa. thera 1.1.95);

“As a deer in the forest, unbound, goes for pasture wherever it wishes, so a wise person, recognizing his freedom, should wander alone like a rhinoceros horn.”

Imaṃ kho ahaṃ, bhante, atthavasanti bhagavā yadidaṃ mama etarahi paramaṃ vivekasukhaṃ phalasamāpattisukhaṃ, idameva kāraṇaṃ sampassamāno “aho sukhaṃ, aho sukha”nti udānemi. Etamatthanti etaṃ bhaddiyattherassa puthujjanavisayātītaṃ vivekasukhasaṅkhātaṃ atthaṃ sabbākārato viditvā. Imaṃ udānanti imaṃ sahetukabhayasokavigamānubhāvadīpakaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

'This is the reason, venerable sir': This is the reason I see, namely, this supreme bliss of seclusion, this bliss of the attainment of fruition, that is now mine; seeing this very reason, I utter the inspired utterance, 'Oh, what bliss! Oh, what bliss!' 'This meaning' means: having known in all its aspects this meaning for the Elder Bhaddiya, designated as the bliss of seclusion, which transcends the sphere of worldlings. 'This inspired utterance' means: he uttered this inspired utterance which illuminates the experience of the removal of fear and sorrow along with its cause.

Yassantarato na santi kopāti yassa ariyapuggalassa antarato abbhantare attano citte cittakālussiyakaraṇato cittappakopā [M 3.0413] rāgādayo āghātavatthuādikāraṇabhedato anekabhedā dosakopā eva vā na santi, maggena pahīnattā na vijjanti. Ayañhi antara-saddo kiñcāpi “mañca tvañca kimantara”ntiādīsu (saṃ. ni. 1.228) kāraṇe dissati, “antaraṭṭhake himapātasamaye”tiādīsu (mahāva. 346) vemajjhe, “antarā ca jetavanaṃ antarā ca sāvatthi”ntiādīsu (udā. 13, 44) vivare, “bhayamantarato jāta”ntiādīsu (itivu. 88; mahāni. 5) citte, idhāpi citte eva daṭṭhabbo. Tenevāha “yassa citte kopā na santī”ti.

'For whom there are no agitations within' means: for that noble person, within, in his own mind, mental agitations such as lust and so on, which cause mental turbidity, or indeed the many kinds of agitations of hatred, which are differentiated by causes such as the grounds for resentment, do not exist; they are not found because they have been abandoned by the path. For this word 'antara', although it is seen to mean 'cause' in passages such as 'What is the difference between me and you?', and 'middle' in passages such as 'during the eight-day interval of snowfall', and 'gap' in passages such as 'between Jeta's Grove and Sāvatthī', and 'mind' in passages such as 'fear is born from within'—here too it should be understood as 'mind'. Therefore it is said, 'in whose mind there are no agitations'.

Abhava-saddassa vibhava-saddena atthuddhāre kāraṇamāha “vibhavoti ca abhavoti ca atthato eka”nti. Iti-saddo pakāravacanoti āha “iti anekappakārā bhavābhavatā”ti. Vītivattoti atikkanto[V 3.0377]. Ettha ca “yassā”ti idaṃ yo vītivattoti vibhattivipariṇāmavasena yojetabbaṃ. Taṃ vigatabhayanti taṃ evarūpaṃ yathāvuttaguṇasamannāgataṃ khīṇāsavaṃ cittakopābhāvato itibhavābhavasamatikkamanato ca bhayahetuvigamena vigatabhayaṃ. Vivekasukhena aggaphalasukhena ca sukhiṃ, vigatabhayattā eva asokaṃ. Devā nānubhavanti dassanāyāti adhigatamagge ṭhapetvā sabbepi upapattidevā vāyamantāpi cittacāradassanavasena dassanāya daṭṭhuṃ nānubhavanti na abhisambhuṇanti na sakkonti, pageva manussā. Sekkhāpi hi puthujjanā viya arahato cittappavattiṃ na jānanti. Tassa dassanaṃ devānampi dullabhanti etthāpi cittacāradassanavasena tassa dassanaṃ devānampi dullabhaṃ alabbhanīyaṃ, devehipi taṃ dassanaṃ na sakkā pāpuṇitunti evamattho gahetabbo. Abhāvattho hettha du-saddo “duppañño”tiādīsu viya.

He states the reason for extracting the meaning of the word 'non-existence' (abhava) with the word 'annihilation' (vibhava): ''Annihilation' and 'non-existence' are one in meaning.' He says that the word 'thus' (iti) indicates various modes: 'thus, the many kinds of existence and non-existence.' 'Has passed beyond' means has transcended. Here, 'whose' (yassā) should be connected by way of a change in grammatical case as 'he who has passed beyond' (yo vītivatto). 'That one free from fear' means: such a one, an Arahant endowed with the aforementioned qualities, is free from fear because the causes of fear have ceased due to the absence of mental agitation and the complete transcendence of this existence and non-existence. He is happy with the bliss of seclusion and the bliss of the highest fruition; and because he is free from fear, he is sorrowless. 'Devas cannot manage to see him' means: setting aside those established on the attained path, all devas by rebirth, even if they strive, cannot manage, are not able, are not competent to see him by way of seeing the course of his mind, let alone humans. For even trainees, like worldlings, do not know the proceeding of an Arahant's mind. 'His seeing is difficult even for devas' means: here too, the seeing of him by way of the course of his mind is difficult to obtain, unobtainable, even for devas; the meaning should be taken as 'even by devas that seeing cannot be attained.' Here the prefix 'du-' has the sense of 'difficulty', as in 'of little wisdom' (duppañño) and so on.

333. Bhattābhihāroti abhiharitabbabhattaṃ. Tassa pana pamāṇaṃ dassetuṃ “pañca ca thālipākasatānī”ti vuttaṃ. Tattha eko thālipāko dasannaṃ purisānaṃ bhattaṃ gaṇhāti. Lābhasakkārasilokenāti ettha lābho nāma catupaccayalābho. Sakkāroti tesaṃyeva sukatānaṃ susaṅkhatānaṃ lābho. Silokoti vaṇṇaghoso. Manomayaṃ kāyanti jhānamanena nibbattaṃ brahmakāyaṃ. Upapannoti upagato. Attabhāvappaṭilābhoti sarīrapaṭilābho. Dve vā tīṇi vā māgadhakāni gāmakhettānīti [M 3.0414] ettha māgadhakaṃ gāmakhettaṃ atthi khuddakaṃ, atthi majjhimaṃ, atthi mahantaṃ. Khuddakaṃ gāmakhettaṃ ito cattālīsa usabhāni, etto cattālīsa usabhānīti gāvutaṃ hoti. Majjhimaṃ ito gāvutaṃ, etto gāvutanti aḍḍhayojanaṃ hoti. Mahantaṃ ito diyaḍḍhagāvutaṃ, etto diyaḍḍhagāvutanti tigāvutaṃ hoti. Tesu khuddakena gāmakhettena tīṇi, khuddakena ca majjhimena ca dve gāmakhettāni tassa attabhāvo. Tigāvutañhissa sarīraṃ. Pariharissāmīti paṭijaggissāmi gopayissāmi. Rakkhassetanti rakkhassu etaṃ.

333. 'A bringing of food' means food that should be brought. To indicate its measure, it is said, 'five hundred cooked pots'. Here, one cooked pot holds food for ten men. 'By gain, honor, and renown': here, 'gain' means the gain of the four requisites. 'Honor' means the gain of those same requisites when they are well-made and well-prepared. 'Renown' means a reputation for virtue. 'A mind-made body' means the brahma-body produced by the jhānic mind. 'Arisen' means attained. 'The acquisition of a selfhood' means the acquisition of a body. 'Two or three Magadhan village-fields': here, a Magadhan village-field may be small, medium, or large. A small village-field is forty usabhas from here and forty usabhas from there, which is a gāvuta. A medium one is a gāvuta from here and a gāvuta from there, which is one and a half yojanas. A large one is one and a half gāvutas from here and one and a half gāvutas from there, which is three gāvutas. Among these, his selfhood is the size of three small village-fields, or two village-fields—one small and one medium. For his body is three gāvutas. 'I will maintain' means I will look after, I will protect. 'Protect it' means you protect this.

Pañcasatthukathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse of the Five Teachers

334. Satthāroti gaṇasatthāro. Nāssassāti na etassa bhaveyya. Tanti taṃ satthāraṃ. Tenāti amanāpena. Samudācareyyāmāti katheyyāma. Sammannatīti amhākaṃ sammānaṃ karoti. Tenāha “sammānetī”ti, sammannatīti vā parehi sammānīyatīti attho.

334. “Teachers” (satthāro) means teachers of a group. “He should not be his” (nāssassā) means it should not be for him. “That” (taṃ) refers to that teacher. “By that” (tena) means by something disagreeable. “We would approach” (samudācareyyāma) means we would speak. “He esteems” (sammannati) means he pays us respect. Therefore it is said, “he esteems,” or “sammannati” means he is esteemed by others—this is the meaning.

335. Nāsāya pittaṃ bhindeyyunti acchapittaṃ vā macchapittaṃ vā nāsāpuṭe pakkhipeyyuṃ. Parābhavāyāti avaḍḍhiyā vināsāya. Assatarīti vaḷavāya kucchismiṃ gadrabhassajātā, taṃ assena [V 3.0378] saddhiṃ sampayojenti, sā gabbhaṃ gaṇhitvā kāle sampatte vijāyituṃ na sakkoti, pādehi bhūmiṃ paharantī tiṭṭhati, athassā cattāro pāde catūsu khāṇukesu bandhitvā kucchiṃ phāletvā potakaṃ nīharanti, sā tattheva marati. Tena vuttaṃ “attavadhāya gabbhaṃ gaṇhātī”ti.

335. “They would split open the nose with bile” means they would insert bear bile or fish bile into the nostril. “For ruin” means for decline and destruction. “Assatarī” (a female mule) means one born in the womb of a mare from a donkey. They mate her with a horse, and having conceived, when the time comes, she is unable to give birth. She stands striking the ground with her hooves. Then they tie her four legs to four posts, cut open her womb, and pull out the foal. She dies right there. Hence it is said, “She conceives for her own destruction.”

339. Potthanikanti churikaṃ, yaṃ kharantipi vuccati.

339. “Potthanikā” means a knife, which is also called a “scraper.”

Nāḷāgiripesanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Story of Sending Nāḷāgiri

342. Mā kuñjara nāgamāsadoti bho, kuñjara, buddhanāgaṃ vadhakacittena mā upagaccha. Dukkhanti dukkhakāraṇattā dukkhaṃ. Kathaṃ taṃ dukkhanti āha “na hi nāgahatassā”tiādi. Nāgahatassa sugatipaṭikkhepena buddhanāgassa ghāto duggatidukkhakāraṇanti dasseti. Itoti ito jātito. Yatoti yasmā. Ito paraṃ yatoti ito paraṃ gacchantassāti vā [M 3.0415] attho. Madoti mānamado. Pamādoti pamattabhāvo. Paṭikuṭitoti saṅkuṭito. Alakkhikoti ahiriko. Yatra hi nāmāti yo nāma.

342. “Do not approach the elephant, O elephant” means “O elephant, do not approach the Buddha-elephant with a mind of violence.” “Suffering” means suffering because it is the cause of suffering. “How is that suffering?” He said, “For of one who strikes the Nāga,” and so forth. He shows that striking the Buddha-elephant, by rejecting a good destination, is the cause of suffering in a bad destination. “From here” means from this birth. “Because” means since. “Beyond this” means going beyond this, or the meaning is from now on. “Intoxication” means the intoxication of pride. “Negligence” means a state of heedlessness. “Twisted” means contracted. “Shameless” means without moral shame. “Wherever it be” means whoever it be.

Pañcavatthuyācanakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on the Five Requests

343. Tikabhojananti tīhi bhuñjitabbabhojanaṃ, tiṇṇaṃ ekato paṭiggahetvā bhuñjituṃ paññapessāmīti attho. Kokālikotiādīni catunnaṃ devadattapakkhiyānaṃ gaṇapāmokkhānaṃ nāmāni. Āyukappanti ekaṃ mahākappaṃ asītibhāgaṃ katvā tato ekabhāgamattaṃ kālaṃ antarakappasaññitaṃ kālaṃ.

343. “Threefold meal” means a meal to be eaten from three sources; the meaning is, “I will prescribe receiving from three sources together and then eating.” “Kokālika,” and so forth, are the names of the four leaders of Devadatta’s faction. “An aeon of life” means an intermediate aeon, a period of time equal to one part of a great aeon divided into eighty parts.

Āyasmantaṃ ānandaṃ etadavocāti (udā. aṭṭha. 48) devadatto sabbaṃ saṅghabhedassa pubbabhāgaṃ nipphādetvā “ekaṃseneva ajja āveṇikaṃ uposathaṃ saṅghakammañca karissāmī”ti cintetvā etaṃ “ajjatagge”tiādivacanaṃ avoca. Tattha aññatreva bhagavatāti vinā eva bhagavantaṃ, taṃ satthāraṃ akatvāti attho. Aññatra bhikkhusaṅghā uposathaṃ karissāmi saṅghakammāni cāti bhagavato ovādakārakaṃ bhikkhusaṅghaṃ vinā maṃ anuvattantehi bhikkhūhi saddhiṃ āveṇikaṃ uposathaṃ saṅghakammāni ca karissāmi. Ajjatagge, bhante, devadatto saṅghaṃ bhindissatīti bhedakārakānaṃ sabbesaṃ devadattena sajjitattā “ekaṃseneva devadatto ajja saṅghaṃ bhindissatī”ti maññamāno evamāha. Bhindissatīti dvidhā karissati.

Regarding “He said this to Venerable Ānanda” (Udāna Aṭṭhakathā 48): Devadatta, having accomplished all the preliminary parts of creating a schism in the Saṅgha, thought, “Today I will surely perform a separate Uposatha and Saṅgha acts,” and spoke these words, “From today,” and so forth. Therein, “apart from the Blessed One” means without the Blessed One, the meaning being without accepting him as the Teacher. “Apart from the Saṅgha of monks, I will perform the Uposatha and Saṅgha acts” means “I will perform a separate Uposatha and Saṅgha acts with the monks who follow me, without the Saṅgha of monks who follow the Blessed One’s instruction.” Regarding the words, “From today, venerable sir, Devadatta will split the Saṅgha,” Ānanda spoke thus, thinking, “Today Devadatta will surely split the Saṅgha,” because all the schism-makers had been prepared by Devadatta. “Will split” means will make into two.

Etamatthaṃ [V 3.0379] viditvāti etaṃ avīcimahānirayuppattisaṃvattaniyaṃ kappaṭṭhiyaṃ atekicchaṃ devadattena nibbattiyamānaṃ saṅghabhedakammaṃ sabbākārato viditvā. Imaṃ udānanti kusalākusalesu yathākkamaṃ sappurisāsappurisānaṃ sukarā paṭipatti, na pana nesaṃ akusalakusalesūti idamatthavibhāvanaṃ udānaṃ udānesi.

“Having understood this matter” means having fully understood in every way this act of creating schism in the Saṅgha, generated by Devadatta, which leads to arising in the great Avīci hell, lasts for the aeon, and is incurable. “He uttered this inspired utterance” means he uttered this inspired utterance elucidating the meaning that for the virtuous and the non-virtuous respectively, practice is easy with regard to wholesome and unwholesome deeds, but not for them with regard to the unwholesome and wholesome respectively.

Tattha sukaraṃ sādhunā sādhūti attano paresañca hitaṃ sādhetīti sādhu, sammāpaṭipanno. Tena sādhunā sāriputtādinā sāvakena paccekasambuddhena sammāsambuddhena aññena vā lokiyasādhunā sādhu sundaraṃ bhaddakaṃ attano paresañca hitasukhāvahaṃ sukaraṃ sukhena kātuṃ sakkā. Sādhu pāpena dukkaranti tadeva pana vuttalakkhaṇaṃ sādhu pāpena devadattādinā [M 3.0416] pāpapuggalena dukkaraṃ kātuṃ na sakkā, na so taṃ kātuṃ sakkotīti attho. Pāpaṃ pāpena sukaranti pāpaṃ asundaraṃ attano paresañca anatthāvahaṃ pāpena yathāvuttapāpapuggalena sukaraṃ sukhena kātuṃ sakkuṇeyyaṃ. Pāpamariyehi dukkaranti ariyehi pana buddhādīhi taṃ pāpaṃ dukkaraṃ durabhisambhavaṃ. Setughātoyeva hi tesaṃ tatthāti dīpeti.

There, “good is easy for the good” means “good” (sādhu) is that which accomplishes benefit for oneself and others—it is right practice. By that good person, whether by a disciple like Sāriputta, a Paccekabuddha, a Perfectly Self-Enlightened One, or another worldly good person, that which is good, beautiful, and excellent, bringing welfare and happiness to oneself and others, is easy to do, possible to do with ease. “Good is hard for the wicked to do” means that very good with the stated characteristics is difficult for the wicked, for wicked individuals like Devadatta, to do; they are incapable of doing it—that is the meaning. “Evil is easy for the wicked to do” means evil, what is unlovely and brings harm to oneself and others, is easily done by a wicked individual as described, possible for them to accomplish with ease. “Evil is hard for the noble to do” means but for noble ones like the Buddha, that evil is difficult, hard to bring about. Indeed, it is like destroying a bridge for them in that regard—this is shown.

Saṅghabhedakathāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Discourse on Schism in the Saṅgha

345. Atha kho āyasmā sāriputto ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsaniyātiādīsu parassa cittaṃ ñatvā kathanaṃ ādesanāpāṭihāriyaṃ, sāvakānañca buddhānañca satataṃ dhammadesanaṃ anusāsanīpāṭihāriyaṃ, iddhividhaṃ iddhipāṭihāriyaṃ. Tattha iddhipāṭihāriyena saddhiṃ anusāsanīpāṭihāriyaṃ mahāmoggallānattherassa āciṇṇaṃ, ādesanāpāṭihāriyena saddhiṃ anusāsanīpāṭihāriyaṃ dhammasenāpatissa. Tena vuttaṃ “āyasmā sāriputto ādesanāpāṭihāriyānusāsaniyā bhikkhū dhammiyā kathāya ovadī”tiādi. Tadā hi dvīsu aggasāvakesu dhammasenāpati tesaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ cittacāraṃ ñatvā dhammaṃ desesi, mahāmoggallānatthero vikubbanaṃ dassetvā dhammaṃ desesi, pāḷiyañcettha dvinnampi therānaṃ desanāya dhammacakkhupaṭilābhova dassito. Dīghabhāṇakā pana evaṃ vadanti “bhagavatā pesitesu dvīsu aggasāvakesu dhammasenāpati tesaṃ cittacāraṃ ñatvā dhammaṃ desesi, therassa dhammadesanaṃ sutvā pañcasatāpi bhikkhū sotāpattiphale patiṭṭhahiṃsu. Atha nesaṃ mahāmoggallānatthero vikubbanaṃ dassetvā dhammaṃ desesi, taṃ sutvā sabbe arahattaphale patiṭṭhahiṃsū”ti. Devadattaṃ uṭṭhāpesīti jaṇṇukena hadayamajjhe paharitvā uṭṭhāpesi.

345. Now then, regarding the miracle of mind-reading and the miracle of instruction, and so on: speaking after knowing the minds of others is the miracle of mind-reading. The constant teaching of the Dhamma by disciples and Buddhas is the miracle of instruction. The various psychic powers are the miracle of psychic power. Among these, the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna was accustomed to the miracle of instruction along with the miracle of psychic power, while the General of the Dhamma was accustomed to the miracle of instruction along with the miracle of mind-reading. Hence it is said, “The Venerable Sāriputta advised the bhikkhus with a Dhamma talk through the miracle of mind-reading and instruction,” and so on. At that time, among the two chief disciples, the General of the Dhamma taught the Dhamma after knowing the mental inclinations of those bhikkhus. The Venerable Mahāmoggallāna taught the Dhamma after displaying transformations. And in the Pāḷi text here, for the teaching of both elders, only the attainment of the Dhamma-eye is shown. The Dīgha reciters, however, say this: “When the Blessed One sent the two chief disciples, the General of the Dhamma, knowing their mental inclinations, taught them the Dhamma. Hearing the elder’s Dhamma teaching, the five hundred bhikkhus became established in the fruit of stream-entry. Then the Venerable Mahāmoggallāna displayed transformations and taught them the Dhamma. Hearing that, all became established in the fruit of arahantship.” “He roused Devadatta” means he struck him in the middle of the chest with his knee and roused him.

346. Sarasīti [V 3.0380] saro. Suvikkhālitanti suṭṭhu vikkhālitaṃ, suvisodhitaṃ katvāti attho. Saṃkhāditvāti suṭṭhu khāditvā. Mahiṃ vikubbatoti mahiṃ dantehi vilikhantassa. Nadīsu bhisaṃ ghasānassāti yojetabbaṃ. Nadīti cettha mahāsaro adhippeto. Jaggatoti hatthiyūthaṃ pālentassa. Bhiṅkovāti hatthipotako viya. Mamānukubbanti maṃ anukaronto.

346. Sarasī means a lake. Suvikkhālitaṃ means well-washed, thoroughly cleansed; the meaning is having been thoroughly purified. Saṃkhāditvā means having chewed well. Mahiṃ vikubbato means of one scraping the earth with his teeth. The phrase Nadīsu bhisaṃ ghasānassa should be construed as ‘of one eating lotus roots in the rivers.’ And here, nadī is intended to mean a great lake. Jaggato means of one protecting the herd of elephants. Bhiṅko means like a young elephant. Mamānukubbanti means imitating me.

347. Dūteyyanti [M 3.0417] dūtakammaṃ. Gantumarahatīti dūteyyasaṅkhātaṃ sāsanaṃ harituṃ dhāretvā harituṃ arahati. Sotāti yaṃ assa sāsanaṃ denti, tassa sotā. Sāvetāti taṃ uggaṇhitvā “idaṃ nāma tumhehi vutta”nti paṭisāvetā. Uggahetāti suuggahitaṃ katvā uggahetā. Dhāretāti sudhāritaṃ katvā dhāretā. Viññātāti attanā tassa atthaṃ jānitā. Viññāpetāti paraṃ vijānāpetā. Sahitāsahitassāti “idaṃ sahitaṃ, idaṃ asahita”nti evaṃ sahitāsahitassa kusalo upagatānupagatesu cheko sāsanaṃ ārocento sahitāsahitaṃ sallakkhetvā āroceti. Na byathatīti na vedhati na chambhati. Uggavādininti pharusavacanena samannāgataṃ. Pucchitoti paṭiññatthāya pucchito.

347. Dūteyya means the duty of a messenger. Gantumarahati means he is worthy to carry the message, known as a mission; having retained it, he is worthy to deliver it. Sotā means the hearer of the message given to him. Sāvetā means having learned it, he reports back, saying, “This is what you said.” Uggahetā means having well grasped it, he learns it. Dhāretā means having well retained it, he remembers it. Viññātā means he understands its meaning himself. Viññāpetā means he makes others understand it. Sahitāsahitassa means skilled in what is fitting and unfitting; being an expert in what is suitable and unsuitable, when delivering the instruction, he announces it after discerning what is fitting and unfitting. Na byathati means he does not tremble or become frightened. Uggavādin means endowed with harsh speech. Pucchito means questioned regarding the meaning of his declaration.

348. Aṭṭhahi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehītiādīsu asaddhammehīti (itivu. aṭṭha. 89) asataṃ dhammehi, asantehi vā asobhanehi vā dhammehi. Abhibhūtoti ajjhotthaṭo. Pariyādinnacittoti khepitacitto lābhādihetukena icchācārena mānamadādinā ca khayaṃ pāpitakusalacitto. Atha vā pariyādinnacittoti parito ādinnacitto, vuttappakārena akusalakoṭṭhāsena yathā kusalacittassa uppattivāro na hoti, evaṃ samantato gahitacittasantānoti attho. Apāye nibbattanārahatāya āpāyiko. Tatthapi avīcisaṅkhāte mahāniraye uppajjatīti nerayiko. Ekaṃ antarakappaṃ paripuṇṇameva katvā tattha tiṭṭhatīti kappaṭṭho. Atekicchoti buddhehipi anivattanīyattā avīcinibbattiyā tikicchābhāvato atekiccho, atikicchanīyoti attho. Lābhenāti lābhena hetubhūtena. Atha vā lābhahetukena mānādinā. Lābhañhi nissāya idhekacce puggalā pāpicchā icchāpakatā icchācāre ṭhatvā “lābhaṃ nibbattessāmā”ti anekavihitaṃ anesanaṃ appatirūpaṃ āpajjitvā ito cutā apāyesu nibbattanti. Apare yathālābhaṃ labhitvā taṃnimittaṃ mānātimānamadamacchariyādivasena pamādaṃ āpajjitvā ito cutā apāyesu nibbattanti, ayañca tādiso. Tena vuttaṃ “lābhena, bhikkhave, abhibhūto pariyādinnacitto devadatto āpāyiko”tiādi. Asakkārenāti hīḷetvā paribhavitvā parehi attani pavattitena [M 3.0418] asakkārena, asakkārahetukena vā mānādinā. Asantaguṇasambhāvanādhippāyena pavattā pāpā icchā etassāti pāpiccho, tassa bhāvo pāpicchatā, [V 3.0381] tāya. “Ahaṃ buddho bhavissāmi, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī”ti hi tassa icchā uppannā. Kokālikādayo pāpā lāmakā mittā etassāti pāpamitto, tassa bhāvo pāpamittatā, tāya.

348. In “Monks, by eight unrighteous qualities,” etc., “unrighteous qualities” (Itivuttaka Commentary, p. 89) means by qualities of the unvirtuous, or by unwholesome or ignoble qualities. Abhibhūta means overwhelmed. Pariyādinnacitta means his mind is destroyed, his wholesome qualities brought to ruin by wrong conduct motivated by craving for gain, and by pride, intoxication, etc. Alternatively, “pariyādinnacitta” means his mind is seized from all sides, meaning his mental continuum is completely gripped by unwholesome tendencies of the kind mentioned, so that there is no opportunity for wholesome states of mind to arise. Āpāyika means destined for rebirth in the lower realms. Nerayika means he is reborn even there, in the great hell called Avīci. Kappaṭṭha means he remains there for a full intermediate aeon. Atekiccha means incurable, because it cannot be reversed even by Buddhas, and there is no remedy for rebirth in Avīci; it means beyond remedy. By gain means due to gain as a cause. Or, it refers to pride and other defilements caused by gain. Indeed, relying on gain, some individuals, being evil-wishing and overcome by craving, engage in wrong conduct, thinking, “We will produce gain,” and having resorted to various improper and unsuitable means of livelihood, they pass away from here and are reborn in the lower realms. Others, having obtained gain as they wished, become negligent on account of it, due to arrogance, excessive pride, intoxication, envy, etc., and having passed away from here, they are reborn in the lower realms. And this one (Devadatta) is such a person. Hence it is said: “Monks, Devadatta, overcome and consumed by gain, is destined for the lower realms,” etc. By disrespect means by the disrespect shown towards him by others, by being scorned and humiliated, or by pride and other defilements caused by disrespect. Pāpiccha means one whose evil wishes arise with the intention of being regarded as possessing non-existent virtues; its state is pāpicchatā, by that. Indeed, the wish arose in him: “I will become a Buddha and lead the monastic community.” Pāpamitta means one who has evil, wretched friends like Kokālika and others; its state is pāpamittatā, by that.

349. Abhibhuyyāti abhibhavitvā madditvā.

349. Abhibhuyya means having overcome and crushed.

350. Tīhi, bhikkhave, asaddhammehītiādi vuttanayameva. Oramattakena visesādhigamena antarā vosānaṃ āpādīti ettha pana ayamattho. Oramattakenāti appamattakena jhānābhiññāmattena. Visesādhigamenāti uttarimanussadhammādhigamena. Antarāti vemajjhe. Vosānaṃ āpādīti akatakiccova samāno “katakiccomhī”ti maññamāno samaṇadhammato vigamaṃ āpajji. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – jhānābhiññāhi uttarikaraṇīye adhigantabbe maggaphale anadhigate satiyeva taṃ anadhigantvā samaṇadhammato vigamaṃ āpajjīti. Iti bhagavā iminā suttena visesato puthujjanabhāve ādīnavaṃ pakāseti “bhāriyo puthujjanabhāvo, yatra hi nāma jhānābhiññāpariyosānā sampattiyo nibbattetvāpi anekānatthāvahaṃ nānāvidhadukkhahetuasantaguṇasambhāvanaṃ asappurisasaṃsaggaṃ ālasiyānuyogañca avijahanto avīcisaṃvattanikaṃ kappaṭṭhiyaṃ atekicchaṃ kibbisaṃ pasavatī”ti.

350. In “Monks, by three unrighteous qualities,” etc., the explanation is as stated before. But here, the meaning of “with a trifling attainment of distinction, he reached cessation midway” is this. Oramattakena means with a mere attainment of jhāna and higher knowledges. Visesādhigamena means with the attainment of superior human states. Antarā means in the middle. Vosānaṃ āpādi means that, while still having an uncompleted task, he thought, “My task is done,” and thus deviated from the ascetic life. This is what is meant: without having attained the path and fruit, which are to be attained as a higher accomplishment through jhāna and higher knowledges, he deviated from the ascetic life without attaining them. Thus the Blessed One, by this discourse, specifically reveals the danger in the state of an ordinary person: 'Burdensome indeed is the state of an ordinary person, for one who, even after developing attainments culminating in jhāna and higher knowledges, does not abandon the assumption of non-existent virtues—which brings manifold harm and is a cause of various kinds of suffering—association with bad people, and indulgence in laziness, thereby produces a grave, incurable misdeed that leads to Avīci and lasts for an aeon.'

Gāthāsu māti paṭisedhe nipāto. Jātūti ekaṃsena. Kocīti sabbasaṅgāhakavacanaṃ. Lokasminti sattaloke. Idaṃ vuttaṃ hoti – imasmiṃ sattaloke koci puggalo ekaṃsena pāpiccho mā hotūti. Tadamināpi jānātha, pāpicchānaṃ yathā gatīti pāpicchānaṃ puggalānaṃ yathāgati yādisī nibbatti yādiso abhisamparāyoti imināpi kāraṇena jānāthāti devadattaṃ nidassento evamāha.

In the verses, mā is a prohibitive particle. Jātu means certainly. Koci is a word that includes all. Lokasmiṃ refers to the world of beings. This is what is meant: In this world of beings, may no individual ever be definitely evil-wishing. By this also, know the fate of the evil-wishing means: by this reason too, know what the destiny of evil-wishing individuals is, what kind of rebirth, what kind of future existence; thus he spoke, pointing out Devadatta as an example.

Paṇḍitoti samaññātoti pariyattibāhusaccena paṇḍitoti ñāto. Bhāvitattoti sammatoti jhānābhiññāhi bhāvitacittoti sambhāvito. Tathā hi so “mahiddhiko godhiputto, mahānubhāvo godhiputto”ti [M 3.0419] dhammasenāpatināpi pasaṃsito ahosi. Jalaṃva yasasā aṭṭhā, devadattoti vissutoti attano kittiyā parivārena ca jalanto viya obhāsanto viya ṭhito devadattoti evaṃ vissuto pākaṭo ahosi. “Me suta”ntipi pāṭho, mayā sutaṃ sutamattaṃ, katipāheneva atathābhūtattā tassa taṃ paṇḍiccādisavanamattamevāti attho.

Paṇḍita means known as wise, meaning known as wise through extensive learning in the scriptures. Bhāvitatta means esteemed, meaning regarded as one whose mind is developed through jhāna and higher knowledges. Indeed, he was praised even by the General of the Dhamma as “Godhiputta of great psychic power, Godhiputta of great majesty.” He stood like a flame with fame, well-known as Devadatta, meaning he was thus well-known and manifest as Devadatta, shining and gleaming with his own renown and retinue. There is also the reading “me sutaṃ” (heard by me), meaning it was merely heard by me, and since it proved untrue in a few days, his being called wise and the like was merely a matter of hearsay—that is the meaning.

So [V 3.0382] pamādaṃ anuciṇṇo, āsajja naṃ tathāgatanti so evaṃbhūto devadatto “buddhopi sākiyaputto, ahampi sākiyaputto, buddhopi samaṇo, ahampi samaṇo, buddhopi iddhimā, ahampi iddhimā, buddhopi dibbacakkhuko, dibbasotacetopariyañāṇalābhī, buddhopi atītānāgatapaccuppanne dhamme jānāti, ahampi te jānāmī”ti attano pamāṇaṃ ajānitvā sammāsambuddhaṃ attanā samasamaṭṭhapanena pamādaṃ āpajjanto “idānāhaṃ buddho bhavissāmi, bhikkhusaṅghaṃ pariharissāmī”ti abhimārapayojanādinā tathāgataṃ āsajja āsādetvā viheṭhetvā. “Pamādamanujiṇṇo”tipi paṭhanti. Tassattho – pamādaṃ vuttanayena pamajjanto pamādaṃ nissāya bhagavatā saddhiṃ yugaggāhacittuppādena saheva jhānābhiññāhi anujiṇṇo parihīnoti. Avīcinirayaṃ patto, catudvāraṃ bhayānakanti jālānaṃ tattha uppannasattānaṃ vā nirantaratāya “avīcī”ti laddhanāmaṃ catūsu passesu catumahādvārayogena catudvāraṃ atibhayānakaṃ mahānirayaṃ paṭisandhiggahaṇavasena patto. Tathā hi vuttaṃ –

He who indulges in heedlessness, having assailed the Tathāgata—that is, Devadatta, being of such a nature, thought: "The Buddha is a Sakyan, I too am a Sakyan; the Buddha is an ascetic, I too am an ascetic; the Buddha is one with psychic powers, I too have psychic powers; the Buddha has the divine eye, the divine ear, and the knowledge of others' minds, I too have these; the Buddha knows the past, future, and present, I too know these." Not knowing his own measure, and by equating himself with the Fully Enlightened One, falling into heedlessness, thinking, "Now I will become a Buddha, I will lead the community of monks," through pride, ambition, and the like, he assailed, attacked, and harassed the Tathāgata. There is also the reading, 'Pamādamanujiṇṇo'. Its meaning is: being heedless in the manner described, and on account of that heedlessness, as soon as the thought of competing with the Blessed One arose, he declined from, that is, he fell away from, the jhānas and higher knowledges. He fell into the Avīci hell, a place of four doors, exceedingly terrifying—due to the unceasing nature of the flames or of the beings born there, it has obtained the name "Avīci." It is a great hell with four doors due to its connection with four great doors on its four sides, exceedingly fearsome, and he fell there, taking rebirth. As it is said:

“Catukkaṇṇo catudvāro, vibhatto bhāgaso mito;

Ayopākārapariyanto, ayasā paṭikujjito.

“Four-cornered, with four gates, divided into portions, well-measured; bounded by an iron rampart, covered over with iron.

“Tassa ayomayā bhūmi, jalitā tejasā yutā;

Samantā yojanasataṃ, pharitvā tiṭṭhati sabbadā”ti. (ma. ni. 3.250, 267; a. ni. 3.36);

“Its ground is made of iron, blazing, endowed with heat; extending a hundred leagues all around, it always stands.” (MN 129; MN 130; AN 3.35)

Aduṭṭhassāti aduṭṭhacittassa. Dubbheti dusseyya. Tameva pāpaṃ phusatīti tameva aduṭṭhadubbhiṃ pāpapuggalaṃ pāpaṃ nihīnaṃ pāpaphalaṃ phusati pāpuṇāti abhibhavati. Bhesmāti vipulabhāvena gambhīrabhāvena ca bhiṃsāpano, bhiṃsāpento viya vipulagambhīroti attho. Vādenāti dosena. Upahiṃsatīti bādhati āsādeti. Vādo tamhi na rūhatīti tasmiṃ tathāgate [M 3.0420] parena āropiyamāno doso na ruhati na tiṭṭhati, visakumbho viya samuddassa na tassa vikāraṃ janetīti attho.

“‘Of one who is not hateful’ means of one whose mind is not hateful. ‘Harms’ means may harm. ‘That very evil touches him’ means that the inferior evil result touches, reaches, and overcomes that very evil person who harms the one who is not hateful. ‘Terrifying’ means causing fear due to its vastness and depth; the meaning is that it is vast and profound, as if instilling fear. ‘With blame’ means with hate. ‘Harms’ means oppresses or assails. ‘Blame does not grow in him’ means the blame attributed to the Tathāgata by another does not grow, does not stand; just as a vessel of poison does not cause any change in the ocean is the meaning.

Evaṃ chahi gāthāhi pāpicchatādisamannāgatassa nirayūpagabhāvadassanena dukkhato aparimuttiṃ dassetvā idāni tappaṭipakkhadhammasamannāgatassa dukkhakkhayaṃ dassento “tādisaṃ mitta”nti osānagāthamāha. Tassattho – yassa sammā paṭipannassa maggānugo paṭipattimaggaṃ anugato sammā paṭipanno appicchatādiguṇasamannāgamena sakalassa vaṭṭadukkhassa khayaṃ pariyosānaṃ [V 3.0383] pāpuṇeyya, tādisaṃ buddhaṃ buddhasāvakaṃ vā paṇḍito sappañño attano mittaṃ kubbetha tena mettiṃ kareyya, tañca sevetha tameva payirupāseyyāti.

Thus, with six verses, having shown the non-deliverance from suffering by demonstrating the state of being bound for hell for one endowed with evil desires and the like, now, to show the destruction of suffering for one endowed with the opposite qualities, he spoke the concluding verse beginning, ‘such a friend.’ Its meaning is this: a wise person, one with wisdom, should make a friend of such a one—a Buddha or a disciple of the Buddha—who is rightly practicing, following the path of practice, and endowed with qualities such as having few desires, by which one would attain the destruction and end of all the suffering of the round of rebirths. One should cultivate friendship with them, associate with them, and attend upon them.

Kiṃ panetaṃ suttaṃ devadattassa nirayūpapattito pubbe bhāsitaṃ, udāhu pacchāti? Itivuttakaṭṭhakathāyaṃ (itivu. aṭṭha. 89) tāva –

But was this sutta spoken before Devadatta's rebirth in hell or after? In the Itivuttaka commentary (Itiv. Aṭṭha. 89), it is stated:

“Devadatte hi avīcimahānirayaṃ paviṭṭhe devadattapakkhikā aññatitthiyā ‘samaṇena gotamena abhisapito devadatto pathaviṃ paviṭṭho’ti abbhācikkhiṃsu. Taṃ sutvā sāsane anabhippasannā manussā ‘siyā nu kho etadevaṃ, yathā ime bhaṇantī’ti āsaṅkaṃ uppādesuṃ. Taṃ pavattiṃ bhikkhū bhagavato ārocesuṃ. Atha kho bhagavā ‘na, bhikkhave, tathāgatā kassaci abhisapaṃ denti, tasmā na devadatto mayā abhisapito, attano kammeneva nirayaṃ paviṭṭho’ti vatvā tesaṃ micchāgāhaṃ paṭisedhento imāya aṭṭhuppattiyā idaṃ suttaṃ abhāsī”ti –

“When Devadatta had entered the Avīci great hell, sectarians who sided with Devadatta falsely claimed, ‘Devadatta has been cursed by the ascetic Gotama and has sunk into the earth.’ Hearing this, people who were not pleased with the teaching became doubtful, thinking, ‘Could it be just as these people say?’ The monks reported this occurrence to the Blessed One. Then the Blessed One said, ‘Monks, the Tathāgatas do not pronounce curses on anyone. Therefore, Devadatta was not cursed by me—he entered hell by his own kamma.’ Having spoken thus to dispel their wrong grasp, he delivered this discourse based on this origin story.”

Vuttaṃ, tasmā tesaṃ matena tassa nirayūpapattito pacchāpi bhagavā idaṃ suttamabhāsīti veditabbaṃ. Idha pana tassa nirayūpapattito paṭhamameva uppanne vatthumhi bhāsitaṃ pāḷiāruḷhanti daṭṭhabbaṃ. Teneva “avīcinirayaṃ patto”ti idaṃ pana āsaṃsāyaṃ atītavacananti vuttaṃ, āsaṃsāti cettha avassambhāvinī atthasiddhi adhippetā. Avassambhāviniñhi atthasiddhimapekkhitvā anāgatampi bhūtaṃ viya voharanti, tañca saddalakkhaṇānusārena veditabbaṃ.

It is said. Therefore, it should be understood that according to their opinion, the Blessed One spoke this discourse after his [Devadatta's] rebirth in hell. But here, it should be seen that it is established in the Pāli text as having been spoken immediately when the incident arose, before his rebirth in hell. Therefore, it is said that the phrase ‘he has fallen into the Avīci hell’ is a past tense used in anticipation. And here by ‘anticipation’ is meant the inevitable fulfillment of the meaning. For, in anticipation of an inevitable fulfillment, people often speak of a future event as if it has already occurred, and this should be understood according to the characteristics of language.

Saṅghabhedakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the discourse on schism in the Sangha is concluded.

Upālipañhakathāvaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Discourse on Upāli's Questions

351. Upālipañhe [M 3.0421] yaṃ vattabbaṃ, taṃ aṭṭhakathāyaṃ dassitameva. Tattha anunayantoti anujānāpento, bhedassa anurūpaṃ vā bodhento, yathā bhedo hoti, evaṃ bhinditabbe bhikkhū viññāpentoti attho. Tenāha “na tumhāka”ntiādi.

351. Regarding the questions of Upāli, what is to be said has already been shown in the commentary. Therein, ‘persuading’ means causing them to consent, or instructing them in a manner suitable for schism; that is, informing the monks who are to be divided how a schism occurs. Therefore, he said, ‘not for you,’ and so on.

352. Aṭṭhārasabhedakaravatthumhi dasa akusalakammapathā saṃkiliṭṭhadhammatāya vodānadhammapaapakkhattā “adhammo”ti dassitā, tathā upādānādayo, bodhipakkhiyadhammānaṃ ekantānavajjabhāvato [V 3.0384] natthi adhammabhāvo, bhagavatā pana desitākārena hāpetvā vaḍḍhetvā vā kathanaṃ yathādhammaṃ akathananti katvā adhammabhāvoti dassento āha “tayo satipaṭṭhānā”tiādi. Niyyānikanti sapāṭihīraṃ appaṭihataṃ hutvā pavattatīti attho. Tathevāti iminā “evaṃ amhāka”ntiādinā vuttamatthaṃ ākaḍḍhati. Kātabbaṃ kammaṃ dhammo nāmāti yathādhammaṃ karaṇato dhammo nāma, itaraṃ vuttavipariyāyato adhammo nāma.
