Tattha micchāñāṇanti pāpakiriyāsu upāyacintāvasena pāpakaṃ katvā “sukataṃ mayā”ti paccavekkhaṇākārena ca uppanno moho. Micchāvimuttīti avimuttasseva sato vimuttisaññitā. Samathakkhandhake niddiṭṭhāti “oramattakaṃ adhikaraṇaṃ hoti, na ca gatigataṃ, na ca saritasārita”ntiādinā (cūḷava. 204) niddiṭṭhā. Samathakkhandhake vuttehi samannāgato hotīti [M 3.0482] sambandho. Māturakkhitādayo dasa itthiyo. Dhanakkītādayo dasa bhariyāyo.

“Wrong view and so on culminate in wrong liberation”: this is said with reference to what is found thus: “Wrong view, wrong intention, wrong speech, wrong action, wrong livelihood, wrong effort, wrong mindfulness, wrong concentration, wrong knowledge, wrong liberation” (Vibha. 970). Therein, “wrong knowledge” is the delusion that arises by way of contemplating means for evil actions and in the manner of reflecting, after having done evil, “I have done well.” “Wrong liberation” is the perception of being liberated on the part of one who is not liberated. “It is specified in the Chapter on Settling Legal Questions”: it is specified by the method beginning, “The legal question is minor, not gone over again and again, not brought up again and again” (Cūḷava. 204). The connection is that one is endowed with what is stated in the Chapter on Settling Legal Questions. The ten kinds of women are those protected by their mother and so on. The ten kinds of wives are those bought with wealth and so on.

Dasakavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Section of Tens is concluded.

Ekādasakavāravaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Section of Elevens

331. Ekādasakesu [V 3.0441] na vodāyantīti na pakāsanti. Suyuttayānasadisāya katāyāti icchiticchitakāle sukhena pavattetabbattā yuttayānaṃ viya katāya. Yathā patiṭṭhā hotīti sampattīnaṃ yathā patiṭṭhā hoti. Anu anu pavattitāyāti bhāvanābahulīkārehi anu anu pavattitāya.

331. In the Elevens, “they do not become pure” means they do not shine forth. “Made like a well-yoked chariot” means that because it should be made to proceed with ease at any desired time, it is made like a yoked chariot. “As there is a foundation” means as there is a foundation for attainments. “Continuously developed” means continuously brought about by making the cultivation frequent.

Sukhaṃ supatītiādīsu (a. ni. aṭṭha. 3.11.15; visuddhi 1.258) yathā sesajanā samparivattamānā kākacchamānā dukkhaṃ supanti, evaṃ asupitvā sukhaṃ supati, niddaṃ okkantopi samāpattiṃ samāpanno viya hoti. Sukhaṃ paṭibujjhatīti yathā aññe nitthunantā vijambhantā samparivattantā dukkhaṃ paṭibujjhanti, evaṃ appaṭibujjhitvā vikasamānamiva padumaṃ sukhaṃ nibbikāraṃ paṭibujjhati. Anubhūtapubbavasena devatūpasaṃhāravasena cassa bhaddakameva supinaṃ hoti, na pāpakanti āha “pāpakameva na passatī”tiādi. Dhātukkhobhahetukampi cassa bahulaṃ bhaddakameva siyā yebhuyyena cittajarūpānuguṇatāya utuāhārajarūpānaṃ. Tattha pāpakameva na passatīti yathā aññe attānaṃ corehi samparivāritaṃ viya, vāḷehi upaddutaṃ viya, papāte patantaṃ viya ca passanti, evaṃ pāpakameva supinaṃ na passati. Bhadrakaṃ pana vuḍḍhikāraṇabhūtaṃ passatīti cetiyaṃ vandanto viya, pūjaṃ karonto viya, dhammaṃ suṇanto viya ca hoti.

In the passage “He sleeps happily,” etc. (AN 8.3.11.15; Vism 1.258), just as other people toss and turn, groaning, and sleep in discomfort, so he sleeps happily without sleeping like that. Even when sleep overcomes him, he is as if one who has entered meditative absorption. “He awakens happily” means that while others wake up groaning, yawning, and tossing in discomfort, he awakens happily, undisturbed, like a blooming lotus. Due to past experience and the influence of divine beings, he has only auspicious dreams, not bad ones—hence it is said, “He sees nothing bad,” etc. Even disturbances in the bodily elements often result in auspicious experiences for him, mostly because the forms born of mind are in harmony with those born of season and food. Here, “he sees nothing bad” means that while others might dream of being surrounded by thieves, attacked by wild beasts, or falling into an abyss, he does not see such bad dreams. Instead, he sees auspicious things that promote growth—such as paying homage to a shrine, making offerings, or listening to the Dhamma.

Manussānaṃ piyo hotīti ure āmukkamuttāhāro viya, sīse piḷandhamālā viya ca manussānaṃ piyo hoti manāpo. Amanussānaṃ piyo hotīti yatheva ca manussānaṃ piyo, evaṃ amanussānampi piyo hoti visākhatthero viya. Nāssa aggi vā visaṃ vā satthaṃ vā kamatīti mettāvihārissa kāye uttarāya upāsikāya viya aggi vā, saṃyuttabhāṇakacūḷasīvattherasseva [M 3.0483] visaṃ vā, saṃkiccasāmaṇerasseva satthaṃ vā na kamati na pavisati, nāssa kāyaṃ vikopetīti vuttaṃ hoti. Dhenuvatthumpi cettha kathayanti, ekā kira dhenu vacchakassa khīradhāraṃ muñcamānā aṭṭhāsi. Eko luddako “taṃ vijjhissāmī”ti hatthena samparivattetvā dīghadaṇḍakaṃ sattiṃ muñci. Sā tassā sarīraṃ āhacca tālapaṇṇaṃ viya vivaṭṭamānā gatā, neva upacārabalena na appanābalena, kevalaṃ pana vacchake balavahitacittatāya. Evaṃ mahānubhāvā mettā. Khippaṃ samādhiyatīti kenaci paripanthena parihīnajjhānassa byāpādassa dūrasamanussaritabhāvato khippameva samādhiyati. Mukhavaṇṇo vippasīdatīti bandhanā pamuttatālapakkaṃ viya cassa vippasannavaṇṇaṃ mukhaṃ hoti. Asammūḷho kālaṃ [V 3.0442] karotīti mettāvihārino sammohamaraṇaṃ nāma natthi, asammūḷhova niddaṃ okkamanto viya kālaṃ karoti.

He is dear to people, like an adornment of pearls on the chest or a garland worn on the head—so he becomes beloved and pleasing to people. He is dear to non-humans—just as he is dear to humans, so too is he dear to non-humans, like the Elder Visākha. Fire, poison, or a weapon does not harm him—for one who dwells in loving-kindness, fire does not harm his body, as with the laywoman Uttarā; nor poison, as with the Elder Cūḷasīva, the reciter of the Saṃyutta; nor a weapon, as with the novice Saṃkicca. It is said that it does not proceed against, enter, or destroy his body. They also tell the story of the cow here: Once, a cow stood still, releasing a stream of milk for her calf. A hunter, thinking, “I will shoot her,” brandished a long-shafted spear and threw it. But it struck her body and turned aside like a palm leaf—not by the power of access concentration or absorption, but simply because of the strength of her mind directed with love towards her calf. So mighty is loving-kindness. His mind is quickly concentrated—because ill will, an obstacle to absorption, is far removed, his mind is swiftly concentrated. His facial complexion becomes serene—like a ripe palm fruit freed from its stalk, his face becomes serene. He dies unconfused—one who dwells in loving-kindness does not experience a confused death; like one falling asleep, he passes away unconfused.

Ekādasakavāravaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Section of Elevens is concluded.

Ekuttarikanayavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Numerical Progression Method is concluded.

Uposathādipucchāvissajjanāvaṇṇanā

The Commentary on Questions and Answers concerning the Uposatha and Other Matters

332. “Saṅghaṃ, bhante, pavāremītiādi pavāraṇākathā nāmā”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ.

332. “Venerable Sir, I invite the Saṅgha,” and so on, is called the Pavāraṇā talk, as stated in the Gaṇṭhipadas.

Atthavasapakaraṇavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Atthavasapakaraṇa

334. Paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanāyameva vuttanti “saṅghasuṭṭhutāyā”tiādīnaṃ atthavaṇṇanaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dasakkhattuṃ yojanāya padasataṃ vuttanti ekamūlakanaye dasakkhattuṃ yojanāya katāya saṅkhalikanaye vuttapadehi saddhiṃ padasataṃ vuttanti evamattho gahetabbo. Aññathā ekamūlake eva naye na sakkā padasataṃ laddhuṃ. Ekamūlakanayehi purimapacchimapadāni ekato katvā ekekasmiṃ vāre nava nava padāni vuttānīti dasakkhattuṃ yojanāya navuti padāniyeva labbhanti. Tasmā tāni navuti padāni saṅkhalikanaye baddhacakkavasena yojite dasa padāni labbhantīti tehi saddhiṃ padasatanti sakkā vattuṃ. Ito aññathā pana ubhosupi [M 3.0484] nayesu visuṃ visuṃ atthasataṃ dhammasatañca yathā labbhati, tathā paṭhamapārājikasaṃvaṇṇanāyameva amhehi dassitaṃ, taṃ tattha vuttanayeneva gahetabbaṃ. Purimapacchimapadāni ekattena gahetvā “padasata”nti vuttattā “tattha pacchimassa pacchimassa padassa vasena atthasataṃ, purimassa purimassa vasena dhammasata”nti vuttaṃ. Tasmiṃ padasate “saṅghasuṭṭhū”tiādinā vuttapurimapadānaṃ vasena dhammasataṃ, “saṅghaphāsū”tiādinā vuttapacchimapadānaṃ vasena atthasatanti adhippāyo.

334. “It is stated in the commentary on the first Pārājika itself” is said with reference to the explanation of the meaning of phrases such as “for the well-being of the Saṅgha.” “A hundred terms are stated through tenfold application” should be understood to mean that in the single-root method, when ten applications are made, a hundred terms are stated together with the terms stated in the chain method. Otherwise, it is not possible to obtain a hundred terms in the single-root method alone. In the single-root method, by combining the initial and final terms, nine terms are stated in each round, so only ninety terms are obtained through tenfold application. Therefore, it can be said that those ninety terms, when applied in the chain method like a bound wheel, yield ten terms, making a hundred terms together with them. However, apart from this, how a hundred meanings and a hundred teachings are obtained separately in both methods has been shown by us in the commentary on the first Pārājika itself, and that should be understood in the manner stated there. Since the initial and final terms are taken as one and it is said to be “a hundred terms,” it is stated that “a hundred meanings are derived based on the last of the last terms, and a hundred teachings based on the first of the first terms.” The intended meaning is that in those hundred terms, the hundred teachings are derived based on the initial terms stated as “for the well-being of the Saṅgha” and so on, and the hundred meanings are derived based on the final terms stated as “for the comfort of the Saṅgha” and so on.

Mahāvaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Commentary on the Mahāvagga is concluded.

Paṭhamagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

The First Collection of Verses

Sattanagaresu paññattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā

The Commentary on the Training Rules Established in the Seven Cities

335. Aḍḍhuḍḍhasatānīti [M 3.0485][V 3.0443] tīṇi satāni paññāsañca sikkhāpadāni. Viggahanti manussaviggahaṃ. Atirekanti dasāhaparamaṃ atirekacīvaraṃ. Kāḷakanti “suddhakāḷakāna”nti vuttakāḷakaṃ. Bhūtanti bhūtārocanaṃ. Paramparabhattanti paramparabhojanaṃ. Bhikkhunīsu ca akkosoti “yā pana bhikkhunī bhikkhuṃ akkoseyya vā paribhāseyya vā”ti (pāci. 1029) vuttasikkhāpadaṃ. Antaravāsakanti aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvarapaṭiggaṇhanaṃ. Rūpiyanti rūpiyasaṃvohāraṃ. Suttanti “sāmaṃ suttaṃ viññāpetvā tantavāyehī”ti (pārā. 637) vuttasikkhāpadaṃ. Ujjhāpanaketi ujjhāpanake khiyyanake pācittiyaṃ. Pācitapiṇḍanti bhikkhunīparipācitaṃ. Cīvaraṃ datvāti “samaggena saṅghena cīvaraṃ datvā”ti (pāci. 485) vuttasikkhāpadaṃ. Vosāsantīti “bhikkhū paneva kulesu nimantitā bhuñjanti, tatra cesā bhikkhunī”ti (pāci. 558) vuttapāṭidesanīyaṃ. Giragganti “yā pana bhikkhunī naccaṃ vā gītaṃ vā”ti (pāci. 834) vuttasikkhāpadaṃ. Cariyāti “antovassaṃ cārikaṃ careyyā”ti (pāci. 970) ca, “vassaṃvutthā cārikaṃ na pakkameyyā”ti (pāci. 974) ca vuttasikkhāpadadvayaṃ. Chandadānenāti pārivāsikena chandadānena.

335. “Three hundred and fifty” means three hundred and fifty training rules. “Form” means the human form. “Excess” means an extra robe permissible for a maximum of ten days. “Black” refers to the black color mentioned as “pure black.” “Actual” means the declaration of what is actual. “Successive meals” means eating food in a series of invitations. “And reviling” in the context of bhikkhunīs refers to the training rule, “Whatever bhikkhunī should revile or abuse a bhikkhu…” (Pācittiya 1029). “Inner robe” refers to accepting a robe from a bhikkhunī who is not a relative. “Silver” refers to dealings with silver. “Thread” refers to the training rule that states, “Having personally requested thread and having it woven by weavers…” (Pārājika 637). “Complaining” refers to a pācittiya offense for complaining and being displeased. “Cooked almsfood” refers to food cooked by a bhikkhunī. “Having given a robe” refers to the training rule that states, “Having given a robe with the agreement of the whole Saṅgha…” (Pācittiya 485). “Giving orders” refers to the pāṭidesanīya offense stated as, “If bhikkhus are invited to families and are eating, and a bhikkhunī is there giving orders…” (Pāṭidesanīya 558). “Hilltop fair” refers to the training rule that states, “Whatever bhikkhunī should go to see dancing or singing…” (Pācittiya 834). “Wandering” refers to the two training rules that state, “She may wander on tour during the rains-residence…” (Pācittiya 970), and “Having completed the rains-residence, she should not depart on tour…” (Pācittiya 974). “By giving consent” refers to the giving of consent by one on probation.

Pārājikāni cattārīti bhikkhunīnaṃ cattāri pārājikāni. Kuṭīti kuṭikārasikkhāpadaṃ. Kosiyanti kosiyamissakasikkhāpadaṃ. Seyyāti anupasampannena sahaseyyasikkhāpadaṃ. Khaṇaneti pathavīkhaṇanaṃ. Gaccha devateti bhūtagāmasikkhāpadaṃ. Siñcanti sappāṇakaudakasiñcanaṃ. Mahāvihāroti mahallakavihāro. Aññanti aññavādakaṃ. Dvāranti yāva dvārakosā. Sahadhammoti sahadhammikaṃ vuccamāno. Payopānanti surusurukārakaṃ. Eḷakalomānīti eḷakalomadhovāpanaṃ. Pattoti ūnapañcabandhanapatto. Ovādoti bhikkhunupassayaṃ upasaṅkamitvā ovādo. Bhesajjanti taduttaribhesajjaviññāpanaṃ. Sūcīti aṭṭhimayādisūcigharaṃ. Āraññikoti [V 3.0444] “yāni kho pana tāni āraññakāni senāsanānī”tiādinā (pāci. 570) vuttapāṭidesanīyaṃ[M 3.0486]. Ovādoti “yā pana bhikkhunī ovādāya vā saṃvāsāya vā na gaccheyyā”ti (pāci. 1055) vuttasikkhāpadaṃ.

"The four Pārājikas" are the four pārājikas for bhikkhunīs. "Hut" refers to the training rule on building a hut. "Silk" refers to the training rule on silk mixed with other materials. "Bed" refers to the training rule on sleeping together with one who is not fully ordained. "Digging" refers to digging in the ground. "Go, deity" refers to the training rule on plant life. "Pouring" refers to pouring water containing living things. "Great monastery" refers to a large monastery. "Another" refers to speaking evasively. "Door" means as far as the door-frame. "In accordance with the Dhamma" refers to being addressed in accordance with the Dhamma. "Drinking milk" refers to making a slurping sound. "Wool" refers to having wool washed. "Bowl" refers to a bowl with fewer than five repairs. "Admonishment" refers to approaching a bhikkhunī's residence for admonishment. "Medicine" refers to requesting further medicine. "Needle" refers to a needle case made of bone, etc. "Forest dweller" refers to the pāṭidesanīya concerning "those forest dwellings..." (Pācittiya 570). "Admonishment" refers to the training rule: "Whatever bhikkhunī should not go for admonition or for association..." (Pācittiya 1055).

Pārājikāni cattārītiādinā chasu nagaresu paññattaṃ ekato sampiṇḍitvā sāvatthiyā paññattaṃ visuṃ gaṇetvā sabbāneva sikkhāpadāni dvīhi rāsīhi saṅgaṇhāti.

Beginning with 'the four Pārājikas,' the rules established in six cities are compiled together, and those established in Sāvatthī are counted separately. All the training rules are thus grouped into two categories.

Sattanagaresu paññattasikkhāpadavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The Explanation of the Training Rules Established in the Seven Cities is concluded.

Catuvipattivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Four Failures

336. Ekatiṃsa garukā nāma ubhato aṭṭha pārājikā, bhikkhūnaṃ terasa, bhikkhunīnaṃ dasa saṅghādisesā. Aṭṭhettha anavasesāti etesu yathāvuttagarukesu sādhāraṇāsādhāraṇavasena aṭṭha pārājikā anavasesā nāma.

336. Thirty-one grave offenses are named: eight pārājika offenses for both communities, thirteen saṅghādisesa offenses for monks, and ten saṅghādisesa offenses for nuns. Herein, 'the eight without remainder' refers to the eight pārājika offenses, common and uncommon, as previously stated among these grave offenses, being 'without remainder'.

Asādhāraṇādivaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Uncommon and So Forth

338. “Dhovanañca paṭiggaho”ti gāthā aṭṭhakathācariyānaṃ. Tattha dhovanañca paṭiggahoti aññātikāya bhikkhuniyā cīvaradhovāpanaṃ cīvarapaṭiggahaṇañca. Koseyya…pe… dve lomāti eḷakalomavagge ādito satta sikkhāpadāni vuttāni. Vassikāti vassikasāṭikasikkhāpadaṃ. Āraññakena cāti sāsaṅkasikkhāpadaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṇītanti paṇītabhojanaviññatti. Ūnanti ūnavīsativassasikkhāpadaṃ. Nisīdane ca yā sikkhā, vassikā yā ca sāṭikāti nisīdanavassikasāṭikānaṃ pamāṇātikkamo.

338. The verse 'Washing and accepting' is from the commentators. Here, 'washing and accepting' means having a robe washed by an unrelated bhikkhunī and accepting a robe. 'Silk… two wools' refers to the seven training rules stated at the beginning of the section on wool. 'Rainy-season' refers to the training rule concerning the rainy-season cloth. 'And by the forest-dweller' refers to the training rule concerning a dangerous place. 'Choice' refers to the requesting of choice food. 'Less' refers to the training rule concerning one less than twenty years old. 'And the rule on the sitting-cloth, and that on the rainy-season cloth' refers to exceeding the measurements for sitting cloths and rainy-season cloths.

Āpattikkhandhā ceva uposathādīni ca “pārājikasaṅghādisesā”tiādinā vibhattattā “vibhattiyo”ti vuttāni. Tevīsati saṅghādisesāti bhikkhunīnaṃ āgatāni dasa, bhikkhūnaṃ terasāti tevīsati. Dvecattālīsa nissaggiyātiādīsupi eseva nayo. Dvīhi…pe… kiccaṃ ekena sammatīti dvīhi vivādādhikaraṇaṃ, catūhi anuvādādhikaraṇaṃ, tīhi āpattādhikaraṇaṃ, ekena kiccādhikaraṇaṃ sammatīti attho.

The offense categories and the Uposatha, etc., are called 'classifications' because they are divided as 'pārājika, saṅghādisesa,' and so forth. Twenty-three saṅghādisesa offenses: ten that apply to bhikkhunīs and thirteen to bhikkhus, totaling twenty-three. The same method applies in the cases of forty-two nissaggiya offenses, and so forth. 'By two… a duty by one is settled' means that a dispute legal issue is settled by two, an accusation legal issue by four, an offense legal issue by three, and a duty legal issue by one.

339. Niraṅkatoti [V 3.0445] saṅghamhā apasārito.

339. 'Made unmarked' means expelled from the Saṅgha.

Adhikaraṇabhedavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Divisions of Legal Issues

340. Yasmā [M 3.0487] adhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento samathappattameva ukkoṭeti, tasmā “vivādādhikaraṇaṃ ukkoṭento kati samathe ukkoṭetī”tiādi vuttaṃ.

340. Because one who re-opens a legal issue re-opens only what has reached a settlement, it is therefore said, 'When re-opening a dispute legal issue, how many settlements does one re-open?' and so forth.

341. Pāḷimuttakavinicchayenevāti vinayalakkhaṇaṃ vinā kevalaṃ dhammadesanāmattavasenevāti attho. Yenāpi vinicchayenāti pāḷimuttakavinicchayameva sandhāya vuttaṃ. Khandhakato ca parivārato ca suttenāti khandhakaparivārato ānītasuttena. Nijjhāpentīti paññāpenti.

341. 'Solely by a decision outside the Pāli' means solely by way of a Dhamma teaching, without the characteristics of the Vinaya. 'By whatever decision' is stated with reference to a decision based on what is outside the Pāli. 'By a sutta from the Khandhaka and from the Parivāra' means by a sutta brought from the Khandhaka and Parivāra. 'They cause to consider' means they make known.

342. Kiccaṃ nissāya uppajjanakakiccānanti pubbe kataukkhepanīyādikiccaṃ nissāya uppajjanakakiccānaṃ. Kīdisānaṃ? Yāvatatiyasamanubhāsanādīnaṃ.

342. 'Duties that arise depending on a duty' refers to duties that arise depending on a previously performed duty, such as suspension and so forth. Of what kind? Such as those involving admonition up to the third time, and so forth.

343. Taṃ hīti taṃ vivādādhikaraṇaṃ.

343. 'That indeed' means that dispute legal issue.

344. Adhikaraṇesu yena adhikaraṇena sammanti, taṃ dassetuṃ vuttanti yadā adhikaraṇehi sammanti, tadā kiccādhikaraṇeneva sammanti, na aññehi adhikaraṇehīti dassanatthaṃ vuttanti adhippāyo.

344. It is stated to show by which legal issue among legal issues they are settled. The intention is that it is stated to show that when they are settled by legal issues, they are settled by the duty legal issue alone, not by other legal issues.

353. “Sattannaṃ samathānaṃ katame chattiṃsa samuṭṭhānā”ti pucchitvāpi “kammassa kiriyā karaṇa”ntiādinā sammukhāvinayassa samuṭṭhānāni avibhajitvāva sativinayādīnaṃ channaññeva cha samuṭṭhānāni vibhattāni, taṃ kasmāti āha “kiñcāpi sattannaṃ samathāna”ntiādi. Sativinayādīnaṃ viya saṅghasammukhatādīnaṃ kiccayatā nāma natthīti āha “kammasaṅgahābhāvenā”ti.

353. Even after asking, 'Of the seven methods of settlement, what are the thirty-six origins?', the origins of settlement in the presence are not analyzed with phrases like 'the performance of an act, the carrying out,' and so forth; rather, only six origins are analyzed for the six others, such as settlement by mindfulness, and so forth. Why is this? It is said, 'Although there are seven methods of settlement,' and so forth. It is said that, unlike settlement by mindfulness and so forth, there is no such thing as the functional nature of the Sangha's presence and so forth—hence it is stated, 'due to the absence of inclusion in a formal act'.

Dutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Collection of the Second Verse

359. Mantaggahaṇanti [V 3.0446] aññamaññaṃ saṃsandanaṃ. Anu anu sandhānaṃ anusandhitanti bhāvasādhano anusandhitasaddoti āha “anusandhitanti kathānusandhī”ti.

359. 'Taking counsel' means mutual consultation. 'Repeated connection' is 'anusandhita.' The word 'anusandhita' is formed in the sense of a state, thus it is said: 'Anusandhita means the continuation of the discourse.'

Saṅgāmadvayavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Two Kinds of Conflict

365. Ṭhānanisajjavattādinissitāti [M 3.0488] “evaṃ ṭhātabbaṃ, evaṃ nisīditabba”nti evamādikā. Saññājananatthanti cuditakacodakānaṃ saññuppādanatthaṃ. Anuyogavattaṃ kathāpetvāti “kiṃ anuyogavattaṃ jānāsī”ti pucchitvā teneva kathāpetvā.

365. 'Based on the observances of standing and sitting, etc.' means instructions such as 'one should stand thus, one should sit thus,' and so on. 'For the purpose of generating recognition' means for the purpose of generating understanding in the accused and the accuser. 'Having had the procedure of questioning explained' means having asked, 'Do you know the procedure of questioning?' and then having had that person explain it.

375. Nīlādivaṇṇāvaṇṇavasenāti nīlādivaṇṇavasena ārogyatthādiavaṇṇavasena ca.

375. 'By way of color and non-color' means by way of colors such as blue, etc., and by way of non-colors such as for the sake of health, etc.

Kathinabhedavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Breaking of the Kathina

404. Purejātapaccaye panesa uddiṭṭhadhammesu ekadhammampi na labhatīti esa udakāharaṇādipayogo attano purejātapaccayabhāve pubbakaraṇavasena uddiṭṭhesu dhovanādidhammesu ekadhammampi na labhati attano purejātassa pubbakaraṇasaṅgahitassa dhammassa natthitāya.

404. 'In the case of the pre-existence condition, however, not even a single one of the specified factors is obtained.' This means that this activity of fetching water, etc., due to its nature as a pre-existence condition, does not obtain even a single one of the factors like washing, etc., specified by way of prior actions, because there is no factor belonging to its pre-existing state that is included as a prior action.

412. Rūpādīsu dhammesūti vaṇṇagandhādīsu suddhaṭṭhakadhammesu.

412. 'Among phenomena such as form, etc.' means among the pure octad phenomena such as color, smell, etc.

416. Purimā dveti imasmiṃ adhikāre paṭhamaṃ vuttā antarubbhārasahubbhārā, na pakkamanantikādayo dve uddhārā.

416. 'The first two' refers to the internal withdrawal and co-withdrawal mentioned first in this section, not the two removals such as that at departure, etc.

Upālipañcakavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of Upāli's Pentad

420-421. Omaddakārakoti omadditvā abhibhavitvā kārako. Upatthambho na dātabboti sāmaggivināsāya anubalaṃ na dātabbaṃ. Diṭṭhāvikammampi katvāti “na metaṃ khamatī”ti diṭṭhiṃ āvi katvāpi.

420-421. 'One who crushes' means one who acts by crushing and overpowering. 'Support should not be given' means reinforcement for the destruction of harmony should not be given. 'Even after making a view manifest' means even after making a view public by stating, 'This is not agreeable to me.'

Vohāravaggavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Chapter on Discourse

424. Kāyappayogena [V 3.0447] āpajjitabbā kāyappayogā. Vacīpayogena āpajjitabbā vacīpayogā. Navasu ṭhānesūti osāraṇādīsu navasu ṭhānesu. Dvīsu ṭhānesūti ñattidutiyañatticatutthakammesu. Tasmāti yasmā mahāaṭṭhakathāyaṃ vuttanayena ubhatovibhaṅgā asaṅgahitā, tasmā. Yaṃ kurundiyaṃ vuttaṃ, taṃ gahetabbanti sambandho.

424. Offenses of bodily application are those to be incurred through bodily application. Offenses of verbal application are those to be incurred through verbal application. 'In nine instances' means in the nine instances beginning with rehabilitation. 'In two instances' means in the formal acts with a motion as the second or fourth part. 'Therefore' means: because, according to the method stated in the Great Commentary, the two Vibhaṅgas are not included, therefore what is said in the Kurundī should be adopted; this is the connection.

Diṭṭhāvikammavaggavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Chapter on Making a View Manifest

425. “Catūhi [M 3.0489] pañcahī”ti vacanato dvīhi vā tīhi vā ekato desetuṃ vaṭṭati, tato paraṃ na vaṭṭati. Māḷakasīmāyāti khaṇḍasīmāya. Avippavāsasīmāyāti mahāsīmāya.

425. According to the phrase 'by four or five,' it is permissible to confess to two or three together, but not more than that. 'Within the Māḷaka boundary' means within a limited boundary. 'Within the non-separation boundary' means within the great boundary.

Musāvādavaggavaṇṇanā

The Explanation of the Section on False Speech

444. Pariyāyena jānantassa vuttamusāvādoti yassa kassaci jānantassa pariyāyena vuttamusāvādoti attho.

444. 'A lie told indirectly by one who knows' means a lie spoken indirectly by anyone who knows; this is the meaning.

446. Anuyogo na dātabboti tena vuttaṃ anādiyitvā tuṇhī bhavitabbanti attho.

446. 'No questioning should be undertaken' means one should remain silent, disregarding what was said by that person.

Bhikkhunovādavaggavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Bhikkhunovāda Chapter

454. Ekūnavīsatibhedāyāti maggapaccavekkhaṇādivasena ekūnavīsatibhedāya.

454. Of nineteen kinds refers to the nineteen divisions beginning with the reviewing of the path, etc.

Adhikaraṇavūpasamavaggavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Chapter on the Settlement of Disputes.

458. Pañcahi kāraṇehīti idaṃ atthanipphādanakāni tesaṃ pubbabhāgāni ca kāraṇabhāvasāmaññena ekajjhaṃ gahetvā vuttaṃ, na pana sabbesaṃ pañcannaṃ samānayogakkhemattā. Anussāvanenāti bhedassa anurūpasāvanena. Yathā bhedo hoti, evaṃ bhinditabbānaṃ bhikkhūnaṃ attano vacanassa sāvanena viññāpanenāti attho. Tenāha “nanu tumhe”tiādi. Kaṇṇamūle vacībhedaṃ katvāti etena pākaṭaṃ katvā bhedakaravatthudīpanaṃ voharaṇaṃ. Tattha attanā vinicchitamattaṃ [V 3.0448] rahassavasena viññāpanaṃ anussāvananti dasseti. Kammameva uddeso vā pamāṇanti tehi saṅghabhedasiddhito pamāṇaṃ, itare pana tesaṃ sambhārabhūtā. Tenāha “vohārā”tiādi. Tatthāti voharaṇe.

458. “By five reasons” (pañcahi kāraṇehi): This is stated by taking together the purpose-achieving factors and their preliminary factors due to their common characteristic of being reasons, but not because all five have equal security from bondage. “By proclamation” (anussāvanena): This means a proclamation suitable for the schism. That is, it means making one’s own statement known to the bhikkhus who are to be divided, in such a way that a schism occurs. Therefore, it is said, “Are you not,” etc. “Having made a verbal split at the ear” (kaṇṇamūle vacībhedaṃ katvā): By this, it is meant the declaration of the schism-causing matter by making it public through speech. There, the private communication of what one has personally decided is shown to be the “proclamation.” “The act itself is the recitation or the measure” (kammameva uddeso vā pamāṇaṃ): This means that for them, the success of the schism is the measure, while the others are merely contributing factors to it. Therefore, it is said, “by speech,” etc. “Therein” (tattha): refers to the declaration.

Kathinatthāravaggavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Chapter on the Spreading of the Kathina Robe.

467. Antarā vuttakāraṇenāti “tañhi vandantassa mañcapādādīsupi nalāṭaṃ paṭihaññeyyā”tiādinā vuttakāraṇena.

467. “By the reason stated in between” (antarā vuttakāraṇena): This means by the reason stated, such as “for when one bows, the forehead might strike a bedpost, etc.”

Samuṭṭhānavaṇṇanā

Explanation of Arising.

470. Pubbe [M 3.0490] vuttamevāti sahaseyyādipaṇṇattivajjaṃ. Itaranti sacittakaṃ. Bhiṃsāpanādīni katvāti bhiṃsāpanādinā āpattiṃ āpajjitvāti adhippāyo.

470. “As previously stated” (pubbe vuttameva): This refers to the offense concerning sharing a bed, etc., as laid down. “The other” (itaraṃ): refers to what is accompanied by intention. “Having done frightening, etc.” (bhiṃsāpanādīni katvā): The meaning is having incurred an offense by frightening, etc.

Aparadutiyagāthāsaṅgaṇikaṃ

Summary of the Other Second Verse.

Kāyikādiāpattivaṇṇanā

Explanation of Offenses Beginning with Bodily Action.

474. Vinaye garukā vinayagarukā. Kiñcāpi idaṃ dvīsu gāthāsu āgataṃ, aññehi pana missetvā vuttabhāvato nānākaraṇaṃ paccetabbaṃ.

474. “Grave in the Vinaya” (vinaye garukā): This means those who are grave regarding the Vinaya. Although this occurs in two verses, because it is stated mixed with others, the distinction should be understood accordingly.

Desanāgāminiyādivaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Desanāgāminī and So Forth.

475. Dve saṃvāsakabhūmiyoti ettha bhūmīti avatthā. Aṅgahīnatā kāraṇavekallavasenapi veditabbāti āha “apicetthā”tiādi. Esa nayoti “apicetthā”tiādinā vuttanayo. Vanappatiṃ chindantassa pārājikanti adinnādāne vanappatikathāya āgataṃ parasantakaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ. Vissaṭṭhichaḍḍaneti sukkavissaṭṭhiyā mocane. Dukkaṭā katāti dukkaṭaṃ vuttaṃ. Paṭhamasikkhāpadamhiyevāti bhikkhunovādakavaggassa paṭhamasikkhāpadeyeva. Āmakadhaññaṃ viññāpetvā bhuñjantiyā pubbapayoge dukkaṭaṃ, ajjhohāre pācittiyaṃ.

475. “Two grounds for co-residence” (dve saṃvāsakabhūmiyo): Here, “ground” (bhūmi) means a state. That the deficiency of limbs should also be understood by way of a lack of causes is stated thus: “Furthermore, here,” etc. “This is the method” (esa nayo): This is the method stated by “Furthermore, here,” etc. “Cutting down a tree results in a pārājika offense” (vanappatiṃ chindantassa pārājikaṃ): This refers to taking what is not given, and is stated concerning the property of another in the discourse about trees. “In the emission of discharge” (vissaṭṭhichaḍḍane): This means in the release of semen. “A dukkaṭa offense has been committed” (dukkaṭā katā): This means a dukkaṭa offense is stated. “In the first training rule itself” (paṭhamasikkhāpadamhiyeva): This is in the very first training rule of the Bhikkhunovādaka chapter. For one who eats after requesting raw grain, a dukkaṭa offense is incurred in the initial act, and a pācittiya offense upon swallowing.

Pācittiyavaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Pācittiya Offenses.

476. Abbhuṇhasīloti [V 3.0449] abhinavasīlo.

476. “Newly virtuous” (abbhuṇhasīlo): This means one who is newly virtuous.

478. Asuttakanti suttavirahitaṃ, suttato apanītaṃ natthīti attho.

478. “Unsewn” (asuttakaṃ): This means devoid of thread, removed from the thread, meaning it does not exist.

Sedamocanagāthā

Verses on the Expulsion of Sweat.

Avippavāsādipañhavaṇṇanā

Explanation of Questions Beginning with Non-Separation.

479. Sedamocanagāthāsu [M 3.0491] tahinti tasmiṃ puggale. “Akappiyasambhogo nāma methunadhammādī”ti gaṇṭhipadesu vuttaṃ. Esā pañhā kusalehi cintitāti liṅgavipallāsavasenetaṃ vuttaṃ, eso pañho kusalehi cintitoti attho.

479. In the Verses on the Expulsion of Sweat, “therein” (tahiṃ) refers to that person. “Unsuitable association means sexual practice, etc.” (akappiyasambhogo nāma methunadhammādī): This is stated in the Knot Commentary. “This question was considered by the skillful” (esā pañhā kusalehi cintitā): This is stated due to an inversion of gender, meaning “this question was considered by the skillful.”

Dasāti avandiye dasa. Ekādasāti paṇḍakādayo ekādasa. Ubbhakkhake na vadāmīti iminā mukhe methunadhammābhāvaṃ dīpeti. Adhonābhiṃ vivajjiyāti iminā vaccamaggapassāvamaggesu.

“Ten” (dasa): This refers to the ten who should not be venerated. “Eleven” (ekādasa): This refers to the eleven, such as eunuchs and so on. “I do not speak of the upper lip” (ubbhakkhake na vadāmi): By this, it indicates the absence of sexual activity in the mouth. “Avoiding below the navel” (adhonābhiṃ vivajjiya): By this, it refers to the anal and urinary passages.

Gāmantarapariyāpannaṃ nadīpāraṃ okkantabhikkhuniṃ sandhāyāti ettha nadī bhikkhuniyā gāmapariyāpannā, paratīraṃ gāmantarapariyāpannaṃ. Tattha paratīre paṭhamaleḍḍupātappamāṇo gāmūpacāro nadīpariyantena paricchinno, tasmā paratīre ratanamattampi araññaṃ natthi, paratīrañca tiṇādīhi paṭicchannattā dassanūpacāravirahitaṃ karoti. Tattha attano gāme āpatti natthi, paratīre pana paṭhamaleḍḍupātasaṅkhāte gāmūpacāreyeva pādaṃ ṭhapeti. Antare abhidhamme vuttanayena araññabhūtaṃ sakagāmaṃ atikkamati nāma, tasmā gaṇamhā ohīyanā nāma hotīti veditabbaṃ.

“Concerning a nun who has crossed to the far bank of a river, enclosed within another village” (gāmantarapariyāpannaṃ nadīpāraṃ okkantabhikkhuniṃ sandhāya): Here, the river is enclosed within the village boundaries for the bhikkhunī, while the far bank is enclosed within the boundaries of another village. There, the proximity to the village on the far bank is measured by the distance of the first clod’s throw, bounded by the river’s edge. Thus, on the far bank, there is not even a speck of wilderness, and the far bank, being covered by grass, etc., makes it devoid of a visible boundary. In that case, there is no offense in one’s own village, but on the far bank, she places her foot within the village proximity, reckoned as the first clod’s throw. In between, according to the method stated in the Abhidhamma, she is said to cross over her own village, which has become wilderness, and therefore, it should be understood that this is called “departure from the group.”

Bhikkhūnaṃ santike ekatoupasampannā nāma mahāpajāpatipamukhā pañcasatasākiniyo bhikkhuniyo. Mahāpajāpatipi hi ānandattherena dinnaovādassa paṭiggahitattā bhikkhūnaṃ santike upasampannā nāma.

“Ordained together in the presence of bhikkhus” (bhikkhūnaṃ santike ekatoupasampannā): This refers to the bhikkhunīs, namely Mahāpajāpatī and the five hundred Sakyan women. Indeed, because Mahāpajāpatī accepted the advice given by the Venerable Ānanda, she is called “ordained in the presence of bhikkhus.”

Pārājikādipañhavaṇṇanā

Explanation of Questions Beginning with the Pārājikas.

480. Saha [V 3.0450] dussena methunavītikkamassa sakkuṇeyyatāya “dussakuṭiādīni sandhāyā”ti vuttaṃ. Liṅgaparivattaṃ sandhāya vuttāti “liṅgaparivatte sati paṭiggahaṇassa vijahanato sāmaṃ gahetvā bhuñjituṃ na vaṭṭatī”ti liṅgaparivattanaṃ sandhāya vuttā.

480. Regarding the possibility of a sexual transgression with a cloth, it is said with reference to 'cloth huts, etc.' It is said with reference to a change of gender: 'When there is a change of gender, because of abandoning the act of receiving, it is not proper to take and eat oneself.' This is said with reference to a change of gender.

481. Suppatiṭṭhitanigrodhasadisanti yojanadviyojanādiparamaṃ mahānigrodhaṃ sandhāya vuttaṃ.

481. ‘Like a well-established banyan tree’ refers to a great banyan tree, spoken with reference to one that may extend for one or two yojanas, or even more.

Sedamocanagāthāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Sedamocana verses is concluded.

Pañcavaggo

The Fifth Chapter.

Kammavaggavaṇṇanā

The commentary on the Chapter on Kamma.

483. Kammavagge [M 3.0492][V 3.0451] ummattakassa bhikkhuno ummattakasammuti ummattake yācitvā gate asammukhāpi dātuṃ vaṭṭati, tattha nisinnepi na kuppati niyamābhāvato. Asammukhā kate pana dosābhāvaṃ dassetuṃ “asammukhākataṃ sukataṃ hotī”ti vuttaṃ. Dūtena upasampadā pana sammukhā kātuṃ na sakkā kammavācānānattasambhavato. Pattanikkujjanādayo hatthapāsato apanītamattepi kātuṃ vaṭṭanti. Saṅghasammukhatātiādīsu yāvatikā bhikkhū kammappattā, te āgatā honti, chandārahānaṃ chando āhaṭo hoti, sammukhībhūtā na paṭikkosanti, ayaṃ saṅghasammukhatā. Yena dhammena yena vinayena yena satthusāsanena saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, ayaṃ dhammasammukhatā. Tattha dhammoti bhūtaṃ vatthu. Vinayoti codanā ceva sāraṇā ca. Satthusāsanaṃ nāma ñattisampadā ceva anussāvanasampadā ca. Yassa saṅgho kammaṃ karoti, tassa sammukhabhāvo puggalasammukhatā. Kattikamāsassa pavāraṇamāsattā “ṭhapetvā kattikamāsa”nti vuttaṃ. Paccukkaḍḍhitvā ṭhapitadivaso cāti kāḷapakkhe cātuddasiṃ vā pannarasiṃ vā sandhāya vuttaṃ. Dve ca puṇṇamāsiyoti paṭhamapacchimavassūpagatānaṃ vasena vuttaṃ.

483. In the chapter on formal acts, regarding an insane monk, the declaration of insanity (ummattakasammuti) may be granted even if he has been requested to leave and is absent. Even if he is seated there, it is not invalidated due to the absence of a fixed rule. However, to show that there is no fault in performing the procedure in absentia, it is said, 'What is done in absentia is well done.' Regarding ordination by messenger, it cannot be performed face-to-face due to the possibility of variations in the Kammavācā. Procedures like overturning the bowl, etc., can be carried out even if the person has merely been moved beyond arm's reach. As for the presence of the Saṅgha, etc.: as many monks as are qualified to participate in the procedure have arrived, the consent of those who are eligible to give consent has been brought, and those who are present do not object—this constitutes the presence of the Saṅgha. The presence of the Dhamma means the procedure is conducted in accordance with the Dhamma, the Vinaya, and the Teacher’s instruction. Here, 'Dhamma' refers to the actual fact. 'Vinaya' means both the charge and the reminding. 'The Teacher’s instruction' refers to the completion of the motion and the completion of the announcement. The presence of the individual means the person for whom the Saṅgha is performing the procedure is present. Regarding the month of Kattika, because it is the month for the Pavāraṇā, it is said, 'except for the month of Kattika.' The day set aside after having been withdrawn refers to the fourteenth or fifteenth day of the dark fortnight. The two full-moon days refer to those who have undertaken the rains residence early or late.

485. Ṭhānakaraṇāni sithilāni katvā uccāretabbaṃ akkharaṃ sithilaṃ, tāniyeva dhanitāni asithilāni katvā uccāretabbaṃ akkharaṃ dhanitaṃ. Dvimattakālaṃ dīghaṃ, ekamattakālaṃ rassaṃ. Dasadhā byañjanabuddhiyā pabhedoti evaṃ sithilādivasena byañjanabuddhiyā akkharuppādakacittassa dasappakārena pabhedo. Sabbāni hi akkharāni cittasamuṭṭhānāni yathādhippetatthabyañjanato byañjanāni ca. Saṃyogo paro etasmāti saṃyogaparo, na saṃyogaparo asaṃyogaparo. Āyasmato buddharakkhitatherassa yassa na khamatīti ettha ta-kāra na-kārasahitākāro asaṃyogaparo. Karaṇānīti kaṇṭhādīni.

485. The organs of speech should be relaxed to produce a soft letter; and those same organs should be tensed to produce a hard letter. A long sound lasts for two moras, a short sound for one mora. The distinction of consonants is tenfold according to the understanding of their articulation. Thus, due to laxity and hardness, there is a tenfold distinction in the mind that produces the letter. All letters are mind-produced, and they are called consonants because they manifest the intended meaning. ‘Followed by a consonant cluster’ means followed by a consonant cluster; not followed by a consonant cluster means not followed by a consonant cluster. In the phrase ‘which is not pleasing to the Venerable Buddharakkhita Thera,’ the vowel ‘a’ in syllables such as ‘ta’ and ‘na’ is not followed by a consonant cluster. ‘Articulators’ refers to the throat and so on.

488. Anukkhittā [M 3.0493][V 3.0452] pārājikaṃ anāpannā ca pakatattāti āha “pakatattā anukkhittā”tiādi. Tattha anissāritāti purimapadasseva vevacanaṃ. Parisuddhasīlāti pārājikaṃ anāpannā. Na tesaṃ chando vā pārisuddhi vā etīti tīsu dvīsu vā nisinnesu ekassa vā dvinnaṃ vā chandapārisuddhi āhaṭāpi anāhaṭāva hotīti adhippāyo.

488. He said, 'of natural character and not expelled,' etc., referring to one who is not expelled, has not fallen into a pārājika offense, and is of natural character. Here, 'not banished' is a synonym for the preceding term. 'Of purified morality' means not having fallen into a pārājika offense. 'Neither their consent nor purity comes' means that even if the consent and purity of one or two are brought when three or two are seated, it is as if they were not brought—this is the intended meaning.

Apalokanakammakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Discourse on the Procedure by Announcement.

495-496. Kāyasambhogasāmaggīti sahaseyyapaṭiggahaṇādi. So ratoti subhe rato. Suṭṭhu oratoti vā sorato. Nivātavuttīti nīcavutti. Paṭisaṅkhāti paṭisaṅkhāya ñāṇena upaparikkhitvā. Yaṃ taṃ avandiyakammaṃ anuññātanti sambandho. Imassa apalokanakammassa ṭhānaṃ hotīti evampi apalokanakammaṃ pavattatīti attho. Kammameva lakkhaṇanti kammalakkhaṇaṃ. Osāraṇanissāraṇabhaṇḍukammādayo viya kammañca hutvā aññañca nāmaṃ na labhati, kammameva hutvā upalakkhīyatīti “kammalakkhaṇa”nti vuccati. Etampi kammalakkhaṇamevāti vuttakammalakkhaṇaṃ dassetuṃ “acchinnacīvarajiṇṇacīvaranaṭṭhacīvarāna”ntiādi vuttaṃ. Iṇapalibodhampīti iṇameva palibodho iṇapalibodho, tampi dātuṃ vaṭṭati. Sace tādisaṃ bhikkhuṃ iṇāyikā palibundhanti, tatruppādatopi tassa iṇaṃ sodhetuṃ vaṭṭatīti adhippāyo.

495-496. 'Bodily harmony' means agreement in shared lodging, acceptance of requisites, and so on. 'He delights' means he delights in what is auspicious. Or, 'well restrained' means thoroughly restrained. 'Of humble conduct' means of lowly behavior. 'He reflects' means having examined with reflective wisdom. 'That which is an allowable action, not to be censured' is the connection. 'This is a basis for the procedure by announcement'—thus, the procedure by announcement occurs in this way, is the meaning. 'The action itself is the characteristic' means the action-characteristic. Like actions such as reinstatement, expulsion, and the act of admonition, it does not obtain another name besides being an action; it is recognized simply as an action, hence it is called 'action-characteristic.' This too is merely an action-characteristic—to show the action-characteristic, it is said: 'for undivided robes, worn-out robes, or lost robes,' and so on. 'Even a debt-obstruction'—a debt itself is an obstruction, a debt-obstruction, and it is proper to pay it. If creditors obstruct such a monk, it is proper to clear that debt even if it arises from that situation—this is the intended meaning.

Chattaṃ vā vedikaṃ vāti ettha vedikāti cetiyassa upari caturassacayo vuccati. Chattanti tato uddhaṃ valayāni dassetvā kato aggacayo vuccati. Cetiyassa upanikkhepatoti cetiye navakammattāya upanikkhittato, cetiyasantakatoti vuttaṃ hoti. Aññā katikā kātabbāti purimakatikāya asaṅgahitattā vuttaṃ. Tehīti yesaṃ puggalikaṭṭhāne tiṭṭhanti, tehi. Dasabhāganti dasamabhāgaṃ. Tatthāti tasmiṃ vihāre. Mūleti pubbe. “Ito paṭṭhāya bhājetvā khādantū”ti vacaneneva yathāsukhaṃ paribhogo paṭikkhitto hotīti āha “purimakatikā paṭippassambhatī”ti.

A canopy or a railing—here, 'railing' refers to the square structure on top of the shrine. 'Canopy' refers to the pinnacle made above that, showing rings. 'Deposited near the shrine' means deposited near the shrine for the purpose of new construction, hence it is said 'belonging to the shrine'. 'Another agreement should be made'—this is said because it was not included in the previous agreement. 'By them' means by those for whom they are considered individual property. 'A tenth part' means a tenth portion. 'There' means in that monastery. 'At the root' means previously. By the statement, "From here on, having divided, let them consume," unrestricted use is prohibited—hence it is said, "the previous agreement is rescinded."

Anuvicaritvāti pacchato pacchato gantvā. Apaccāsīsantenāti tesaṃ santikā

Having followed after. Not expecting anything in return from them.

Paccayaṃ apaccāsīsantena. Mūlabhāganti vuttamevatthaṃ vibhāveti “dasabhāgamatta”nti. Akatāvāsaṃ vā katvāti tato uppannaāyena [M 3.0494] katvā. Jaggitakāle ca na vāretabbāti jaggitānaṃ pupphaphalabharitakāle na vāretabbā. Jagganakāleti jaggituṃ āraddhakāle. Ñattikammaṭṭhānabhedeti ñattikammassa ṭhānabhede.

Not expecting a requisite in return. 'Root portion': this clarifies the meaning already stated as 'about a tenth part.' 'Or, having made an unestablished dwelling' means having made it with the income that arose from it. 'And at the time of tending, they should not be prevented' means that when the tended plants are laden with flowers and fruit, they should not be prevented from partaking. 'At the time of tending' means at the time when tending has begun. 'In the distinction of cases for a formal act by motion' means in the distinction of the basis for a formal act by motion.

Kammavaggavaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The commentary on the Chapter on Acts is completed.

Apaññatte paññattavaggavaṇṇanā

In the Section on the Unpromulgated, the Explanation of the Chapter on the Promulgated.

500. Satta [V 3.0453] āpattikkhandhā paññattaṃ nāmāti sambandho. Kakusandhakoṇāgamanakassapā eva satta āpattikkhandhe paññapesuṃ, vipassīādayo pana ovādapātimokkhaṃ uddisiṃsu, na sikkhāpadaṃ paññapesunti āha “kakusandhañca…pe… antarā kenaci apaññatte sikkhāpade”ti. Sesamettha suviññeyyameva.

500. The connection is that the seven groups of offenses are called 'the promulgated.' Kakusandha, Koṇāgamana, and Kassapa indeed laid down the seven groups of offenses, but Vipassī and the others only recited the admonitory Pātimokkha—they did not lay down training rules. Hence, it is said: "Kakusandha and... etc.... in the meantime, no training rule had been laid down by anyone." The rest here is easily understood.

Iti samantapāsādikāya vinayaṭṭhakathāya sāratthadīpaniyaṃ

Thus, in the Sāratthadīpanī, a sub-commentary on the Vinaya Commentary, the Samantapāsādikā.

Parivāraṭṭhakathāvaṇṇanā samattā.

The explanation of the Parivāra Commentary is complete.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā

Explanation of the Concluding Discourse

Avasānagāthāsu [M 3.0495] pana ayamattho. Vibhattadesananti ubhatovibhaṅgakhandhakaparivārehi vibhattadesanaṃ vinayapiṭakanti yojetabbaṃ. Tassāti tassa vinayassa.

However, in the concluding verses, this is the meaning. The term 'Distinguished Exposition' should be connected with the Vinaya Piṭaka, meaning 'the exposition distinguished by the Ubhatovibhaṅga, Khandhaka, and Parivāra'. The phrase 'Of that' refers to that Vinaya.

Tatridantiādi paṭhamapārājikavaṇṇanāyaṃ vuttanayameva.

Here, the method is the same as that stated in the commentary on the first Pārājika, beginning with 'Tatridaṃ'.

Satthumahābodhivibhūsitoti satthunā paribhuttamahābodhivibhūsito maṇḍito, tassa mahāvihārassa dakkhiṇabhāge uttamaṃ yaṃ padhānagharanti sambandho. Tattha padhānagharanti taṃnāmakaṃ pariveṇaṃ. Sucicārittasīlena, bhikkhusaṅghena sevitanti idampi padhānagharavisesanaṃ.

'Adorned with the Teacher's Great Bodhi Tree' means adorned and decorated with the Great Bodhi Tree used by the Teacher; the connection is 'that which is the foremost meditation hall in the southern part of that great monastery.' Here, 'meditation hall' refers to the monastic dwelling (pariveṇa) of that name. 'Frequented by a community of monks with pure conduct and virtue' is also a qualifier of the meditation hall.

Tatthāti tasmiṃ padhānaghare. Cārupākārasañcitanti manāpena pākārena parikkhittaṃ. Sītacchāyatarūpetanti ghananicitapattasañchannasākhāpasākhatāya sītacchāyehi rukkhehi upetaṃ. Vikasitakamalakuvalayapuṇḍarīkasogandhikādipupphasañchannamadhurasītaludakapuṇṇatāya sampannā salilāsayā assāti sampannasalilāsayo. Uddisitvāti buddhasiriṃ nāma theraṃ nissāya, tassa ajjhesanaṃ nissāyāti vuttaṃ hoti. Iddhāti atthavinicchayādīhi iddhā phītā paripuṇṇā.

'Therein' means in that meditation hall. 'Enclosed by a charming wall' means surrounded by a pleasing wall. 'Endowed with cool-shaded trees' means endowed with trees providing cool shade due to their dense foliage and interwoven branches. 'Endowed with water reservoirs' means it has water reservoirs that are well-endowed by being full of sweet, cool water covered with blooming flowers such as lotuses, blue water lilies, white lotuses, and fragrant water lilies. 'Having pointed out' means relying on the elder named Buddhasiri; it is said that it was at his request. 'Prosperous' means flourishing, abundant, and complete in the discernment of meaning, etc.

Sirinivāsassāti siriyā nivāsaṭṭhānabhūtassa. Jayasaṃvacchareti jayappattasaṃvacchare. Ayanti theraṃ buddhasiriṃ uddissa yā vinayavaṇṇanā āraddhā, ayaṃ. Dhammūpasaṃhitāti kusalasannissitā. Idāni sadevakassa lokassa accantasukhādhigamāya attano puññaṃ pariṇāmento “ciraṭṭhitattha dhammassā”tiādimāha[V 3.0454]. Tattha samācitanti upacitaṃ. Sabbassa ānubhāvenāti sabbassa tassa puññassa tejena. Sabbepi pāṇinoti kāmāvacarādibhedā sabbe sattā. Saddhammarasasevinoti yathārahaṃ bodhittayādhigamavasena saddhammarasasevino bhavantu. Sesamettha suviññeyyameva.

'Of Sirinivāsa' means of one who has become the dwelling place of glory. 'In the year of victory' means in the year a victory was attained. 'This' refers to this Vinaya commentary that was begun, dedicated to the elder Buddhasiri. 'Connected with the Dhamma' means based on what is wholesome. Now, dedicating his own merit for the attainment of ultimate happiness for the world with its devas, he says, beginning with 'for the long-lastingness of the Dhamma.' Here, 'accumulated' means collected. 'By the power of all' means by the power of all that merit. 'All beings' refers to all beings differentiated as those of the sensual sphere, etc. 'Partakers of the taste of the true Dhamma' means may they become partakers of the taste of the true Dhamma by attaining the threefold enlightenment according to their ability. The rest here is easily understood.

Nigamanakathāvaṇṇanā niṭṭhitā.

The explanation of the Concluding Discourse is finished.

Nigamanakathā

Concluding Discourse

Ettāvatā [M 3.0496] ca –

And thus far –

Vinaye pāṭavatthāya, sāsanassa ca vuḍḍhiyā;

Vaṇṇanā yā samāraddhā, vinayaṭṭhakathāya sā.

For proficiency in the Vinaya, and for the growth of the Dispensation, this commentary on the Vinaya Commentary was begun.

Sāratthadīpanī nāma, sabbaso pariniṭṭhitā;

Tiṃsasahassamattehi, ganthehi parimāṇato.

Named 'Sāratthadīpanī', it is entirely finished, its extent being about thirty thousand textual units.

Ajjhesito narindena, sohaṃ parakkamabāhunā;

Saddhammaṭṭhitikāmena, sāsanujjotakārinā.

I, having been requested by the king, Parakkamabāhu, who desired the stability of the true Dhamma and brought light to the Dispensation,

Teneva kārite ramme, pāsādasatamaṇḍite;

Nānādumagaṇākiṇṇe, bhāvanābhiratālaye.

in that delightful place caused to be built by him, adorned with a hundred palaces, filled with various groups of trees, an abode for those delighting in meditation,

Sītalūdakasampanne, vasaṃ jetavane imaṃ;

Atthabyañjanasampannaṃ, akāsiṃ suvinicchayaṃ.

dwelling in this Jetavana, which abounds in cool waters, I composed this well-analyzed exposition, complete in meaning and expression.

Yaṃ siddhaṃ iminā puññaṃ, yaṃ caññaṃ pasutaṃ mayā;

Etena puññakammena, dutiye attasambhave.

By whatever merit has been achieved by this, and whatever other has been produced by me, by this meritorious deed, in my next existence,

Tāvatiṃse pamodento, sīlācāraguṇe rato;

Alaggo pañcakāmesu, patvāna paṭhamaṃ phalaṃ.

may I rejoice in Tāvatiṃsa, delighting in the virtue of good conduct, unattached to the five sensual pleasures, having attained the first fruition.

Antime [V 3.0455] attabhāvamhi, metteyyaṃ munipuṅgavaṃ;

Lokaggapuggalaṃ nāthaṃ, sabbasattahite rataṃ.

In my final existence, may I meet Metteyya, the bull among sages, the world's supreme individual, the protector, devoted to the welfare of all beings.

Disvāna tassa dhīrassa, sutvā saddhammadesanaṃ;

Adhigantvā phalaṃ aggaṃ, sobheyyaṃ jinasāsanaṃ.

Having seen that wise one and heard the teaching of the true Dhamma, having attained the highest fruit, may I glorify the Dispensation of the Conqueror.

Sadā rakkhantu rājāno, dhammeneva imaṃ pajaṃ;

Niratā puññakammesu, jotentu jinasāsanaṃ.

May kings always protect this populace righteously; devoted to meritorious deeds, may they illuminate the Dispensation of the Conqueror.

Ime ca pāṇino sabbe, sabbadā nirupaddavā;

Niccaṃ kalyāṇasaṅkappā, pappontu amataṃ padanti.

And may all these beings, always without affliction, constantly with wholesome intentions, attain the deathless state.

Sāratthadīpanī nāma vinayaṭīkā niṭṭhitā.

The Vinaya Sub-commentary named Sāratthadīpanī is completed.
